The goal is to multiply engineering delivery by an order of magnitude: not by cutting corners or generating throwaway code, but by designing robust systems and processes that let agents handle well-defined work while engineers focus on architecture, design, and the problems that actually require human judgment. This is a deliberate, engineering-led approach. We care about code quality, testability, and maintainability - the agent-generated code meets the same standards as everything else. We expect that a successful candidate will be able to bring their expertise to help guide and refine our agentic development process as it matures - a meaningful opportunity to influence how we work as well as what we ship.

Working with the Football Intelligence Data team, you will develop models and insights that inform recruitment, training and match strategy, while helping football practitioners understand what it takes to perform at the highest level. 


 


Who We Are 


Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way. 


 
Within our 1st Team Analysis department, we work across performance analysis and football intelligence to support better decision-making on and off the pitch. By combining technical expertise, football understanding and collaborative ways of working, the team develops practical insight for Manchester City and the wider City Football Group network. 


 


The Role 


As a First Team Data Scientist, you will research and build data science solutions that help football practitioners and decision-makers answer important questions about performance and recruitment. Your work will turn complex information into clear, useful insight that can support the way teams prepare, perform and develop. 


 
You will develop statistical and machine-learning models that deepen our understanding of what it takes to perform, contributing to quantitative approaches across technical, tactical and physical areas of football. You will explore patterns and trends, identify meaningful features, test ideas and make predictions that can inform training programmes and match strategies. 


 
Working alongside data scientists, analysts and colleagues across multidisciplinary teams, you will communicate your findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. You will manage your work against agreed plans, contribute to shared project outcomes and bring curiosity, imagination and practical problem-solving to new football performance challenges.

A Masters or equivalent industry experience in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, statistics, physics, computer science or a related subject. 




Experience designing and training complex statistical models. 




Proficiency in Python for data analysis and model development. 




Experience working with structured and unstructured data sources, including spatio-temporal data. 




Clear and effective communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings to non-technical audiences. 




Proven ability to collaborate with other data scientists and across multidisciplinary teams. 


 

 


Why Choose Us 


Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

We are the UK's aviation and aerospace regulator and recognised as a world leader in its field. Our activities are diverse, enabling the aviation industry to meet the highest safety standards, and we pride ourselves on our ability to adapt to the constantly evolving aviation environment.

The restructuring of UK airspace is facilitated through airspace change proposals submitted to the CAA by a range of aviation and non-aviation stakeholders. These proposals vary greatly in terms of size, operational complexity, and scale of consequential impacts, and are required to follow the CAA’s CAP1616 Airspace Change approval process. The Airspace experts within AR perform oversight of such proposals with respect to their impact on existing airspace structures, airports, and all users of airspace, ensuring modern standards for regulatory decision-making are fair, transparent, consistent, and proportionate.

The Role

Are you looking for an exciting new opportunity to influence the integration of new technologies such as UAS into UK airspace? The CAA is looking for a highly skilled expert, to join the rapidly expanding Airspace Regulation (AR) team during this exciting time as the UK looks to implement a new Airspace Modernisation Strategy. The strategy aims to create an aviation infrastructure for the future to make quicker, quieter and cleaner journeys whilst enabling new technology and user groups to safely integrate into UK Airspace. 

You should have an in-depth understanding of UK airspace and air traffic operations, with an interest or experience in Uncrewed Air System (UAS) operations or integration. If you have the technical expertise and are excited by the idea of being involved in an opportunity like this, then the CAA wants to hear from you. This role provides the opportunity to be at the forefront of evolving airspace change proposals in the UK within a diverse technical team making key decisions. See your expertise help industry to meet the highest of safety standards in this highly rewarding role. 

Core Accountabilities 

• Support integrating the demands of diverse airspace users such as UAS, e-VTOL/hybrid aircraft, General Aviation, Military Aviation, Commercial Aviation, Spaceports and Space Launch Operators, all within the framework of the Airspace Modernisation Strategy whilst ensuring that the assessment of airspace impacts have been appropriately considered. 

• Perform regulatory oversight of the current airspace system to supporting development of polices to integrate new users such as UAS and Advanced Air Mobility. 

• Review and scrutinise airspace proposals from a wide range of sponsors such as operators, innovation companies, airports, the military, spaceports, producing objective and independent assessments of the direct and consequential airspace impacts for each proposed airspace change design. 

• Lay out the conclusions of these assessments and form a key part of the CAA’s transparent decision-making process for approvals. 

• Provide advice, guidance and direction to airspace change sponsors or any other interested parties regarding airspace issues related to operations conducted both inside and outside controlled airspace. 

• Assist in developing and implementing strategies and policies for the consideration of airspace design, use or change in accordance with the Department for Transport’s directions to the CAA, UK legislation and Government regulation and guidance. 

• As an Airspace Regulator you will act as the subject matter expert on airspace matters within the CAA. 

• Your role will sit at the very heart of the UKs developing airspace, where you will work within cross capability teams both within Airspace Regulation, across the authority, across Government and with external sponsors including, amongst many, UAS technology companies. 

About You

Essential: 

• You will possess an excellent understanding of UK airspace and air traffic operations. 

• Understanding or experience in UAS and how to safely integrate them with other airspace users. Knowledge of UK SORA Air Risk methodology is desirable, but not essential.

• A sound understanding of UK airspace, air traffic operations and emerging technology developments in the aviation industry. 

• Awareness of the environmental impact of aviation, and of existing and developing strategies and actions to mitigate these.

job_title: Navigating Modern Employment: Pivot, Prepare, Go Remote
job_description:
Today’s job market rewards adaptability and focus. Learn how to map your skills, target growth industries, use remote work job boards effectively, apply career pivot strategies, and master interview preparation techniques to land offers with confidence.

The employment landscape is evolving faster than most job seekers can track, but the fundamentals of thoughtful planning still win. Successful candidates blend targeted search tactics with deliberate skill building and consistent practice. That means learning how to read labor-market signals, treating your application materials as living documents, and training like an athlete for conversations with employers. Practical pillars—using remote work job boards with intention, applying career pivot strategies that fit your strengths, and drilling the right interview preparation techniques—can transform a scattershot search into a focused campaign that compels hiring teams to say yes.

Start with a rigorous skills assessment to replace guesswork with data. Inventory technical competencies, domain knowledge, and soft skills, then validate them against real job descriptions you collect from multiple sources. Circle the capabilities that recur across roles and industries—especially the transferable skills such as communication, project management, problem solving, and stakeholder influence. Rate your current proficiency, gather evidence from measurable achievements, and identify critical gaps. This exercise narrows your target, clarifies a learning roadmap, and gives you precise language for resume optimization and conversations with mentors during networking.

Next, scan the market like an analyst. Create a simple spreadsheet to map roles, industries, and company stages (startup, growth, enterprise) and note hiring velocity from recent postings. Track skills adjacencies to make your transition faster: an operations coordinator can bridge into project management; a salesperson can cross into customer success; a teacher can pivot to learning and development. In this phase, the most effective career pivot strategies emphasize minimal leap distance—moving one function or one industry at a time—while you build missing capabilities through short courses and stretch projects. Pair this research with informational interviews to confirm where demand is hottest and where your story resonates.

Translate insights into a 60–90 day learning plan. Choose two cornerstone competencies and one differentiator that align with your target roles. For each, define a practical output—an analysis, a prototype, or a case study—that you can showcase in a portfolio. Timebox sprints, and schedule weekly reviews to assess progress. Favor projects that mirror real job tasks, such as building dashboards, writing test cases, designing onboarding flows, or drafting market briefs. Document not only what you built but why it mattered, the metrics you influenced, and the tradeoffs you made. This deliberate practice both strengthens transferable skills and gives you credible stories for interviews.

When you are ready to compete, elevate your documents. Resume optimization starts with ruthless relevance: mirror the language of your target postings without exaggeration, front-load quantified impact, and compress legacy experience. Use clear section headings, consistent formatting, and standard fonts to improve ATS parsing. Replace dense paragraphs with concise bullets that begin with strong verbs and end with measurable outcomes. Your cover letter should act as a tailored business case, not a biography—lead with the employer’s priorities, connect two or three proof points, and close with a confident ask. Keep a running library of cover letter tips that work for your audience, noting the hooks and outcomes that earn replies.

Build a digital presence that signals credibility before anyone reads your resume. Update your headline and About section to reflect your target role, not just your past. Share brief artifacts from your projects, publish observations on industry trends, and engage consistently with practitioners to strengthen networking outcomes. Host work samples in a clean, navigable portfolio that clarifies problem, approach, and results in under a minute. If you are pursuing location-flexible roles, tune your profiles and content to demonstrate asynchronous collaboration, documentation habits, and timezone awareness—the very behaviors remote-first teams prize.

Diversify your search channels instead of refreshing the same sites. Combine company career pages, alumni groups, industry newsletters, and curated remote work job boards to surface high-signal leads. In parallel, cultivate advocates: past managers, clients, mentors, and peers who can vouch for specific achievements. Prepare short outreach messages that reference a mutual interest, state your value proposition in one sentence, and propose a low-friction next step. Remember that networking is about exchanging insight, not requesting favors; consistently offer help—sharing a resource, making an introduction, or summarizing a webinar—increases your surface area for serendipity.

Now turn practice into performance with disciplined interview preparation techniques. Start by reverse-engineering the role’s top problems from the job description and recent company news. Build a library of stories using the STAR or PAR framework, emphasizing context, your decision-making, and measurable results. Record mock sessions to refine pacing and eliminate filler words. For a virtual interview, master the basics: stable internet, neutral backdrop, eye-level camera, and concise screen-share artifacts. Create a one-page brief you can reference—key metrics, case prompts, and question themes—so you stay anchored when nerves rise.

Technical and case interviews deserve their own sprints. Deconstruct the skills being tested—analysis, architecture, prioritization, estimation, or debugging—and practice against realistic prompts. Narrate your thinking so interviewers can follow your tradeoffs. Where relevant, bring artifacts from your portfolio to ground your approach in real outcomes. After each attempt, perform a mini retro: what went well, what to change, and one experiment for next time. This loop tightens quickly, especially when paired with peer feedback groups focused on interview preparation techniques.

As offers approach, be ready to negotiate with clarity and respect. Salary negotiation is easier when you have anchored expectations early, researched compensation bands, and framed your ask around market data and your impact. Consider the full package—bonus, equity, learning budget, flexibility, and role scope—and prioritize in advance. For remote roles, specify collaboration hours, equipment stipends, and travel cadence. Practice phrasing that invites problem solving, such as, “Based on the scope and market benchmarks, I’m targeting X–Y. How close can we get?” Then listen. Silence is a tool.

Backend Engineering at Depop

At Depop, backend engineers own the services behind how people buy, sell and stay safe on the platform. We’re hiring mid and senior backend engineers across several teams in Product Engineering. 

Where you could work

• Search & Retrieval: Powers how buyers find what they’re looking for on Depop. The team is responsible for maintaining, scaling and improving the search system. As well as improving the underlying infrastructure that serves search and recommendations at Depop.

• Adtech: Builds the systems behind advertising on Depop, helping sellers get their items in front of the right buyers.

About the role

Our Customer Experience team is here to solve the problems that matter most to our community. Our goal isn't simply to answer questions or close cases - it's to retain our users, rebuild trust when something goes wrong, and help keep our community confidently buying and selling on Depop.

As a Customer Experience Agent, you'll take ownership of some of the most complex issues our users face. Many of the cases that reach you can't be resolved through our standard support channels and may involve complex disputes, multiple users, transactional issues, sensitive circumstances or nuanced applications of our policies.

You'll investigate what has happened, work across different sources of information, apply our policies and processes thoughtfully, and use your judgement to reach a clear and complete resolution. You'll often be the final point of contact for the user, so the decisions you make - and how you communicate them - really matter.

We're looking for people who are naturally curious and confident problem-solvers. You'll need to be comfortable making well-reasoned decisions and taking ownership of an issue through to resolution, always considering the user's wider experience and what we can do to maintain their trust in Depop. You'll be part of a collaborative and supportive team, with guidance from Team Leads and colleagues when needed, while being empowered to use your own judgement and take initiative to deliver the best possible outcomes.

And your impact won't stop with the individual cases you handle. You'll develop a deep understanding of the issues affecting our community, spot patterns and emerging trends, and share insights that can help us improve our overall user experience.

What you'll do

• Own complex cases from investigation through to resolution, using sound judgement and confident decision-making to navigate nuanced issues and deliver outcomes that build trust and keep users buying and selling on Depop.
• Build expert knowledge of Depop’s products, policies, processes and internal tools, and apply it thoughtfully to reach the right outcome, even when the answer isn’t immediately obvious.
• Work confidently with transactional information, reviewing payments, refunds, balances, sales and transaction histories to understand what’s happened and resolve disputes accurately.
• Handle sensitive and challenging interactions with empathy and professionalism, communicating decisions clearly and fairly, even in difficult circumstances.
• Collaborate across Depop when a case requires additional expertise or highlights an issue that needs wider attention.
• Spot patterns and emerging trends, proactively flagging issues that could affect our wider community and sharing insights that help improve our products, policies and processes.
• Adapt as our support environment evolves, quickly learning new tools, processes and ways of working.

What we're looking for

The Role 
Depop is looking for a UK-based Engineering Manager to lead our Trust Detection team.
Trust Detection’s team goal is to catch the bad content and behaviour before the Depop community gets hurt by it. That means fake listings, phishing messages, counterfeits, and the people behind them.
We’re a team of ML Scientists and Backend Engineers. We build, train and maintain our own models, and bring in third-party tools where they’re the better fit. We also build the platform that runs it all in production and acts on what it detects. We prioritise automation as much as we can, so moderators can focus on the hard calls. Every decision a model or a human makes becomes training data for the next one.
Our signals are used across Depop, in listings, search, chat and account security. We want to catch bad actors at the account level rather than one listing at a time, step in in real time, and offer our risk scores as a service other teams can build on.
You'll manage the backend engineers on the team and form its leadership trio alongside the ML Manager and Product Manager. Together, you'll set direction, shape the roadmap and turn the team's mission into shipped, measurable impact.

What you’ll do

Lead and grow the team

• Manage, coach and develop a team of Backend Engineers through 1:1s, feedback, career growth and performance.
• Build an inclusive, high-trust culture where ML and Backend Engineers work as one team, not two disciplines handing work over a wall.
• Shape the team's hiring, onboarding and ways of working as it grows.

Be one third of the leadership trio

• Partner with the ML Manager and Product Manager to set the team's direction, priorities and roadmap.
• Own team delivery and health while the ML Manager leads on modelling approach and the PM on problem and outcome. Hold each other to a shared set of goals.
• Own the technical direction of the trust detection platform, working with staff engineers and partner teams to deliver it.
• Turn strategy into a clear plan: break down ambiguous problems, sequence the work, and keep momentum high.

Drive delivery and engineering quality

• Help the team take models from experiment to reliable production systems, including real-time inference, monitoring and safe rollouts.
• Stay close to architecture and technical trade-offs, especially as we build shared risk-scoring services used by other teams.
• Lift engineering standards across both disciplines: testing, observability, cost, and operational excellence for systems that act on users.
• Make risks, dependencies and decisions visible early, so the right support and alignment are in place.

Work across the business

• Collaborate and influence Trust & Safety Operations, Policy, Legal, Data and partner product teams who consume the team's signals.
• Help the team balance user safety, fairness to genuine sellers, compliance obligations and speed, and explain those trade-offs clearly.
• Champion how we measure success: harm prevented, model precision and recall, and how often decisions are overturned.

What we’re looking for
We’re looking for an engineering leader who combines technical depth, product judgement, and inclusive people leadership.

You’ll be a strong fit if you bring:
• Experience managing and developing engineers, ideally including senior engineers.
• A strong software engineering background, with the confidence to engage in architecture and technical trade-offs.
• Experience leading teams that run production systems, with a focus on reliability and quality.
• Experience working with, or a real appetite to learn how to lead, ML or data-heavy teams. You don't need to build models, but you should be curious about how they get from notebook to production.
• Clear ownership of team health and delivery, and the ability to create momentum in ambiguous, fast-changing problem spaces.
• A collaborative style in a shared-leadership model: you're comfortable with healthy disagreement and making decisions together.
• The confidence to challenge engineers, ML, product partners and stakeholders constructively.
• Motivation to protect people and help build trusted online communities.

We know great Engineering Managers don't always match every line of a job description. If this role excites you, we'd love to hear what you'd bring.

Helpful experience, not dealbreakers
We don't expect one person to bring all of this. Adjacent experience and curiosity are just as valuable.

• ML in production: MLOps, model serving, real-time inference, feature pipelines, retraining or monitoring for drift.
• Detection and risk: trust and safety, fraud, abuse, spam, content moderation or marketplace integrity.
• Platform thinking: building shared services or APIs that other teams depend on.
• Measurement: experimentation, shadow testing, golden-set evaluation or other ways of proving a model's real-world impact.
• Cross-functional delivery: working with Operations, Policy, Legal, Compliance or Security partners.

What’s in it for you
You'll lead a young, high-impact team at an exciting point. Trust Detection is a growing team with a lot still to build, so there’s plenty of room to make a big impact and grow with it. You’ll shape how we scale: catching bad actors at the account level, acting in real time, and building a risk platform the rest of Depop relies on. You’ll work where ML, engineering and real user impact meet, with strong support from your trio partners, the wider Trust & Support group and engineering leadership.

Job description
We are looking for a Senior Knowledge and Content Specialist to own the knowledge that powers support at Depop. This covers our Help Centre, which buyers and sellers read to help themselves, and the content and guidance our AI Agent uses to answer their questions. You will make sure that knowledge is accurate, up to date, easy to understand, and sounds like Depop.
Knowledge is one of the biggest drivers of how well our AI Agent performs, and of how easily our community can find answers on their own. Thousands of buyers and sellers rely on it every week, so the content you write and maintain will directly shape their support experience. If the knowledge isn’t right, the AI Agent’s answers won’t be either, which means your work will have a big impact on metrics such as resolution rate, customer satisfaction, and self-serve success. We are looking for a strong writer who is also AI-literate: someone who uses AI tools confidently to create, review, and improve content faster, without compromising on quality.

What You’ll Do
• Own the Help Centre and the knowledge the AI Agent draws on, keeping it well structured and easy to navigate, and making sure content works well both for customers reading it and for AI using it
• Write and edit clear, concise copy for Help Centre articles, AI Agent guidance, macros, and other support content in Depop’s tone of voice, and create and maintain the style guide and content standards that keep it consistent
• Set up and run systems that keep knowledge up to date, including a regular review cycle so every article is checked at least once a month
• Prioritise the knowledge backlog, deciding what to fix first based on customer impact, and recommend improvements to how we manage knowledge
• Make sure content is accurate for both our UK and US communities, reflecting differences in policies, processes, and language
• Use AI tools to speed up content creation, reviews, and gap analysis, while keeping accuracy and quality high
• Find knowledge gaps and track how content performs, using conversations, Help Centre searches, article ratings, customer feedback, and contact trends, and use what you learn to improve it
• Work with product, policy, and operations teams so content is updated ahead of launches and changes, and make sure sensitive content is reviewed by the relevant teams before it goes live
• Support the upkeep of internal guidance for our advisors, working with the Continuous Improvement team so internal and customer-facing knowledge stay aligned
• Partner with the AI Support Leads and Conversation Designers so that knowledge and guidance work together, and with the CX Content Designer where needed to keep content consistent across the product and support

About You

Essential Experience and Skills
• Proven experience writing and editing content, such as copywriting, help content, UX writing, or knowledge base management
• Excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with the ability to turn complex policies and processes into simple, friendly copy
• AI-literate, confident using AI tools day to day to work more efficiently, and able to judge when AI output needs fixing
• A good understanding of customer support and what customers need from self-service content
• Experience owning a knowledge base or content area end to end, including the processes that keep it accurate and up to date
• Comfortable using data and feedback to measure how content is performing and decide what to improve
• Strong organisational skills, able to manage lots of updates and deadlines at once
• Experience working with cross-functional teams, including product, operations, and technical stakeholders

Preferred Experience and Skills
• Experience with customer facing AI Agents, Zendesk, or similar help centre and knowledge base platforms
• Experience writing content for AI agents or chatbots, or optimising content for AI and search
• Experience working in a customer support team
• Experience creating visual content such as screenshots, GIFs, or short videos
• Basic understanding of HTML and CSS
• Background in e-commerce, marketplace, or high-growth businesses

Role
Backend Enablement is the connective tissue between Depop’s internal engineering teams and the capabilities they need to build great things fast. It owns our API platform, making sure our APIs aren’t just functional, but genuinely good to build on. This is an internally focused space: rather than shipping customer-facing features, it ships the infrastructure and decisions that let dozens of other teams ship theirs.

The Senior Product Manager will be focused on developer experience for our internal engineers, identifying gaps in our services before they become blockers, and building a roadmap flexible enough to support features and experiments other teams haven’t even scoped yet. If you are someone who is curious about how backend systems are built and scaled, comfortable with ambiguity and a confident voice in technical discussions, then this is the role for you.

Responsibilities:
• Own the product strategy, vision and roadmap for Depop’s API platform and backend enablement space, and communicate it clearly and consistently across engineering and stakeholder groups.
• Treat our internal engineers as your users: deeply understand their workflows, pain points, priorities and mental models.
• Hold a high bar for technical solution design, making sure our APIs are intuitive, well-documented and performant, while balancing this against pragmatic delivery timelines.
• Identify gaps in our current services and capabilities before they become blockers, partnering closely with engineering, platform and product teams to understand what they’re trying to build next.
• Think several steps ahead, designing extensible solutions rather than one-off fixes and making deliberate trade-offs between short-term unblocks and long-term platform health.
• Work with engineering leads to sequence work and define success metrics such as adoption, latency, error rates and developer satisfaction.
• Communicate trade-offs and articulate the value of technical initiatives in a user-centric way to stakeholders who may not be technical.
• Shape technical solutions with engineers, without dictating implementation details unless they are material to the developer experience.

Key stakeholders
• Engineering leads and internal engineering teams
• Platform
• Product teams across Depop
• Non-technical stakeholders affected by platform decisions

Requirements
• Experience as a Technical Product Manager, ideally in an API or DB focused environment.
• Hands-on experience with APIs, including REST, versioning and auth patterns.
• Experience setting product strategy and vision with an engineering team, and communicating it clearly and consistently across engineering and stakeholder groups.
• A track record of building trusted relationships with engineering leaders and stakeholders, and using that influence to align priorities across teams you don’t directly manage.
• Experience defining performance and scalability based metrics.
• Able to communicate technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, reframing complexity so it is easy to understand.
• Able to articulate the value of technical initiatives in a user-centric way.
• Familiar with the challenges of building tooling and services for internal customers.

• Hands-on experience as a backend engineer, or a Computer Science background.
• Familiarity with queuing technologies.
• Experience with microservice architecture.

• An instinct for correctness over speed, and the testing habits to back it up: you write automated tests and think about edge cases before someone asks you to
• Ability to own a feature end to end: breaking it down, driving it forward, flagging risks early, and knowing when to ask for help
• Ability to work across disciplines, as you'll partner closely with backend engineers, product, and design, and need to hold your own in conversations

Job Description:
Wintel Active Directory (AD) Engineer – Job Description

Role Summary
The ITO Wintel Active Directory (AD) Engineer provides Level 3 operational support for Windows Server and Microsoft Active Directory across DXC-managed customer environments. The engineer maintains the health, security and compliance of directory services, including domain controllers, Group Policy, DNS/DHCP, certificate services and replication topology. Working within ITIL 4 frameworks, they implement approved changes, enforce secure baselines and support identity lifecycle workflows, keeping services stable, auditable and aligned with contractual SLAs. They escalate complex trust, identity or replication issues to senior engineers or architects.

Due to the nature of the work and the customers we support, the successful candidate must be eligible to meet UK Government and contractual personnel security requirements, including the applicable residency requirements for the role, and have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Some roles may also be subject to nationality requirements where these are necessary to meet UK Government or contractual security obligations.

Please note attendance on-site 5 days a week is required.

Key Responsibilities
Plan AD capacity, domain controller placement, FSMO distribution and site topology.
Maintain accurate Wintel and AD CMDB records, relationships and dependencies.
Support OS lifecycle, patching and security roadmaps and infrastructure forecasting across managed environments.
Investigate recurring directory incidents through Problem Management and propose permanent fixes.
Update AD and Windows runbooks, procedures and knowledge articles with current configurations and lessons learned.
Contribute to post-incident reviews and service improvements that enhance stability and efficiency.
Keep customers informed of planned changes, maintenance windows and service impacts.
Coordinate GPO, DNS and trust dependencies with Security, Identity and Network teams.
Update incident managers and stakeholders on major-incident progress and resolution timelines.
Implement security and operational GPOs with testing and peer review before production deployment.
Support approved AD design and transition changes to OUs, trusts, sites and subnets.
Verify tested, documented system state backups and authoritative restores before directory services go live.
Maintain current, accessible AD topology diagrams and documentation using tools such as Visio.
Build and configure physical and virtual Windows AD servers to CIS or equivalent security baselines.
Patch domain controllers through approved changes, coordinating with Change Management to minimise disruption.
Automate provisioning, health checks, replication monitoring and bulk reporting with PowerShell.
Configure DNS zones, DHCP scopes and certificate dependencies to integrate with AD infrastructure.
Resolve L3 Windows Server and AD incidents involving authentication, replication, GPOs and DNS.
Process JML account provisioning, changes and de-provisioning through approved requests and identity lifecycle policies.
Remove stale objects, review privileged groups and manage dormant accounts for directory security and compliance.
Monitor domain controller health, replication latency and SYSVOL consistency to prevent service degradation.
Secure baselines are enforced, and audit and compliance evidence is gathered and maintained to support internal and external reviews.
Complex trust, identity federation, or multi-domain replication issues are escalated to senior staff with clear diagnostic information and recommended next steps.

Required Skills & Experience
Essential
Windows Server Operations: 4–7 years’ hands-on enterprise managed-services experience administering Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025, with deep installation, configuration, patching and hardening knowledge across physical and virtual platforms.
Active Directory: Strong on-premises expertise in domain controllers, FSMO roles, intra/inter-site replication, sites and services, OU design and trusts, plus comprehensive AD architecture and infrastructure dependency knowledge.
Group Policy: Advanced GPO design, implementation, linking, troubleshooting and security enforcement across complex OUs and multiple sites.
DNS & DHCP: Solid AD-integrated DNS, forward/reverse lookup zone, conditional forwarder and DHCP scope knowledge to resolve authentication and availability issues caused by name resolution.
Security Hardening: Experience enforcing CIS or equivalent Windows Server baselines, with practical privileged access, stale object cleanup, group hygiene and security assessment knowledge.
Identity Lifecycle: Practical JML provisioning, role-change and de-provisioning experience through approved changes, with AD least-privilege and role-based access knowledge.
Virtualisation: Working VMware vSphere and/or Hyper-V deployment, management and troubleshooting knowledge, supporting confident operations and understanding of host impacts on guest OS performance.
Scripting & Automation: Develop, maintain and troubleshoot PowerShell scripts for AD automation, health checks, reporting and bulk operations to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort.
ITIL Practices: Confidently apply ITIL 4 Incident, Problem, Change and Configuration Management and contribute to the managed-services value chain.
Monitoring & Troubleshooting: Methodically diagnose authentication, Kerberos/NTLM, replication and GPO issues using evidence, native Windows tools and third-party monitoring.
Documentation: Maintain high-quality, accurate, current and team-accessible architecture diagrams, runbooks, SOPs and audit artefacts.
CMDB Management: Maintain accurate configuration records and relationships supporting Change, Incident and Problem Management.
Desired:
Certifications: Hold Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate, Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, or equivalent Windows Server and AD vendor certifications.
ITIL 4 Foundation: Foundation certification or higher is desirable, demonstrating ITIL 4 practice and service value chain knowledge.
Certificate Services: Experience with Microsoft AD CS templates, enrolment, renewal dependencies and domain services integration.
Azure AD / Entra ID: Demonstrate exposure to hybrid identity, Azure AD Connect, single sign-on and conditional access, with an understanding of links between on-premises AD and cloud identity services.
Backup & Recovery: Demonstrate experience using Veeam, Commvault or similar enterprise tools for AD and system state recovery, including authoritative and non-authoritative restores.
Capacity Planning: Demonstrate experience forecasting domain controller resources, storage and replication bandwidth to meet growth and service demand.
Monitoring Tools: Demonstrate familiarity with SCOM, SolarWinds, Dynatrace or similar enterprise platforms and the ability to configure alerts and dashboards for proactive infrastructure management.
Compliance Awareness: Demonstrate awareness of ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials and NIST and their impact on AD security configuration and audit requirements.
Security Clearance: Holding or being able to obtain UK DV clearance is advantageous for defence-sector work.

The ITO Linux Engineer (Level 3) is the Linux technical authority across DXC-managed customer environments, accountable for platform integrity, complex troubleshooting, performance optimisation and architectural improvements for mission-critical workloads. They design, validate and maintain secure OS baselines and oversee patching and vulnerability management to ensure stability, security, performance and audit readiness in regulated environments.

They own major Linux incidents and root-cause analysis, advising on clustering, high availability, disaster recovery configurations, kernel tuning, storage integrations and network dependencies. They automate operations using advanced shell scripting and infrastructure-as-code, approve high-risk changes following review, and mentor junior engineers to build capability and consistency.

Bridging operations and engineering, they support lifecycle planning, platform modernisation and integration with automation, monitoring and configuration management tools. They partner with security and compliance teams to enforce enterprise hardening standards and maintain audit-ready documentation and evidence. The role demands deep technical expertise, architectural judgement and calm, authoritative decision-making under pressure in regulated, mission-critical environments.

Due to the nature of the work and the customers we support, the successful candidate must be eligible to meet UK Government and contractual personnel security requirements, including the applicable residency requirements for the role, and have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Lead Linux capacity planning from CPU, memory, disk, I/O, swap and network trends, recommending scaling, consolidation or platform refresh.
Define and regularly review secure RHEL, CentOS, Oracle Linux and SUSE baselines aligned with CIS, STIGs or equivalent standards.
Plan patching and vulnerability cycles, including sequencing, risk assessment and rollback, to maintain service continuity within constrained change windows.
Identify end-of-life distributions, kernels and dependencies and recommend upgrades or migrations to maintain supportability and compliance.
Maintain accurate Linux CMDB records and configuration management discipline across operations and changes.
Analyse incidents, performance data and vulnerability scans to identify systemic weaknesses and improvement opportunities.
Own root-cause analysis for major and recurring incidents, implementing corrective actions and embedding prevention in procedures and baselines.
Automate repetitive tasks with advanced shell scripting, Ansible, Puppet or equivalent tools to improve consistency, accuracy and efficiency.
Update runbooks, procedures and knowledge articles with current practice, known errors and lessons learned.
Evaluate containerisation, immutable infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code, recommending adoption where reliability, security or efficiency improves.
Lead or support platform modernisation aligned with organisational strategy and industry best practice.
Advise customers, service delivery, security and compliance stakeholders in service reviews, governance forums and risk discussions.
Partner with security teams to enforce hardening standards, deliver prioritised vulnerability remediation and maintain audit evidence.
Coordinate with application, database, network, storage and virtualisation teams on Linux dependencies affecting performance, connectivity and high availability.
Lead major-incident technical bridges, updating incident managers and stakeholders on root cause, impact and recovery.
Mentor junior engineers through technical guidance, work reviews, knowledge sharing and structured development.
Design, validate and maintain secure OS baselines and repeatable, auditable builds that meet regulatory and contractual requirements.
Review high-risk kernel, clustering, storage and baseline changes, assessing risk and giving technical approval before CAB submission.
Design, test and document clustering and HA using Pacemaker, Corosync, DRBD, Oracle RAC dependencies and application-level clustering, including failover.
Design and oversee enterprise storage integration across Fibre Channel, iSCSI, DM-Multipath, NFS and GFS2/OCFS2 shared storage.
Support OS upgrades, distribution migrations and the transition to automation, monitoring and configuration management tools.
Maintain build templates, Kickstart/AutoYaST configurations and post-installation automation for consistent, hardened, audit-ready provisioning from first boot.
Develop Bash/Python scripts, Ansible playbooks, Puppet manifests or equivalent infrastructure-as-code for configuration, compliance, patch orchestration and reporting.
Configure and validate Fibre Channel SAN, iSCSI, DM-Multipath, NFS and GFS2/OCFS2 storage with appropriate redundancy and failover.
Tune sysctl, I/O schedulers, hugepages, swappiness, OOM behaviour, ulimits, cgroups and network parameters for mission-critical workloads.
Integrate monitoring (Nagios, Zabbix, Prometheus, SCOM, SolarWinds or equivalent), logging (rsyslog, ELK, Splunk) and configuration management for estate-wide visibility, alerting and compliance reporting.
Own major Linux incidents, directing investigation and resolution of kernel panics, cluster failovers, storage path failures, severe performance issues and security incidents.
Lead post-incident root-cause analysis, producing RCA reports, defining corrective and preventive actions and updating baselines, runbooks and procedures.
Resolve escalations beyond L2, including performance degradation, kernel faults, clustering/HA failures, multipath issues, authentication, certificates and cross-domain Linux, network, storage and application faults.
Act as the Linux team’s final escalation point, providing authoritative technical guidance and decisions under pressure.
Oversee regulated Linux patching and vulnerability cycles, assessing, testing and deploying security errata, kernel updates and configuration fixes within agreed timescales and change processes.
Review and approve high-risk changes before execution, assessing technical risk, impact and rollback readiness and providing required sign-off.
Maintain audit-ready compliance reports, patch records, configuration snapshots, RCA reports and change evidence for internal and external reviews.
Monitor clustering, HA and DR health and performance, validating failover readiness, replication health and quorum status.
Proactively analyse mission-critical workloads to address bottlenecks and tuning opportunities before service impact.

Required Skills & Experience

Essential
Linux Operations Experience. 5 - 10 years administering and engineering Linux in enterprise, mission-critical or regulated environments, with deep operational and architectural expertise in RHEL, CentOS, Oracle Linux or SUSE and proven ownership of complex outcomes across large production estates.
Advanced Troubleshooting. Expert troubleshooting across kernel, system, networking, storage, file systems, authentication and application dependencies, resolving panics, performance crises, storage failures, split-brain and cross-domain faults through structured RCA and crash, strace, perf, ftrace, SystemTap, tcpdump, blktrace, journalctl, dmesg and sar.
Clustering & High Availability. Deep expertise designing, validating and troubleshooting mission-critical HA using Pacemaker, Corosync, DRBD, fencing/STONITH, quorum management and resource agents, including failover testing and split-brain prevention.
Storage Integration. Expert Linux storage integration and troubleshooting across Fibre Channel SAN, iSCSI, DM-Multipath, NFS and GFS2/OCFS2, covering HBA-to-file-system connectivity, path failures and performance issues.
Kernel Tuning & Performance Optimisation. Advanced workload profiling and bottleneck resolution through sysctl, I/O schedulers, hugepages, swappiness, OOM, NUMA, cgroups, resource limits and network tuning for mission-critical applications.
Security Hardening & Compliance. Experience designing, validating and maintaining CIS/STIG-aligned or equivalent OS baselines, with proficiency in SELinux/AppArmor, FIPS, auditd and vulnerability remediation under contractual compliance and external assurance requirements.
Patching & Vulnerability Management. Experience overseeing regulated Linux patching, including strategy, risk assessment, kernel updates and security errata through Red Hat Satellite, SUSE Manager or equivalent, within agreed timescales and change processes.
Automation & Infrastructure-as-Code. Advanced Bash/Python scripting and Ansible, Puppet, Chef or SaltStack experience to design and implement provisioning, configuration enforcement, compliance checks, patch orchestration and reporting at scale.
Networking. Strong Linux networking knowledge covering bonding/teaming, VLANs, routing, firewalld/nftables, TCP tuning and tcpdump/ss/ip/nmcli troubleshooting, including impacts on applications, storage connectivity and cluster communication.
ITIL Practices. Strong Incident, Problem, Change and Configuration Management knowledge, including major-incident ownership, RCA leadership, high-risk change approval, CMDB accuracy and audit-ready documentation.
Major Incident Ownership. Proven ownership of major Linux incidents, directing cross-team diagnostics and resolution under pressure, producing detailed RCA reports and ensuring corrective action.
Mentoring & Technical Leadership. Experience mentoring junior engineers through technical guidance, work reviews and incident/change coaching, with commitment to developing L2 capability and reducing escalations.
Documentation & Audit Readiness. Ability to maintain accurate, controlled and accessible technical documentation, RCA reports, baseline evidence and compliance artefacts for internal and external audits.
Change Review & Approval. Experience approving high-risk changes through technical risk, impact, dependency and rollback assessments and formal technical sign-off.

Desired:
Certifications. RHCE, RHCA, Red Hat Certified Specialist in High Availability Clustering or Linux Performance Tuning, SUSE Certified Engineer (SCE), or equivalent advanced Linux certification.
ITIL 4 Foundation. ITIL 4 Foundation certification or higher, demonstrating knowledge of ITIL 4 practices and the service value chain.
Containerisation & Orchestration. Docker, Podman, Kubernetes and OpenShift experience covering production Linux engineering, resource management, security and troubleshooting.
Cloud Platforms. Linux administration on AWS EC2, Azure VMs and GCP Compute Engine, including cloud networking, storage, identity integration and operational differences from on-premises workloads.
DR & Resilience. Experience designing and validating Linux disaster recovery, including replication, backups and recovery procedures aligned with RTO/RPO targets.
Monitoring & Observability. Deep Nagios, Zabbix, Prometheus/Grafana, ELK and Splunk experience, including custom checks, alert design and Linux performance dashboards.

CI/CD & DevOps Practices. Familiarity with Linux CI/CD, GitOps and DevOps, including automated testing, pipeline-driven configuration deployment and version-controlled infrastructure.
Platform Modernisation. Experience supporting or leading OS upgrades, distribution migrations, immutable infrastructure adoption and transitions from legacy to modern operational tools.

Desktop & Infrastructure Support Engineer

We’re looking for a Desktop & Infrastructure Support Engineer to join our team in Edinburgh, supporting a secure and important client environment.

This is a hands-on role where you’ll provide day-to-day desktop support while also getting involved in wider infrastructure activities. You’ll work across laptops, desktops, VDI and server environments, helping to troubleshoot issues, maintain systems and contribute to infrastructure projects and improvements.

We’re looking for someone who enjoys solving technical problems and working directly with users, but who also has an interest in what’s happening behind the scenes across the wider infrastructure. You’ll have the opportunity to work with a range of Microsoft technologies and enterprise tools, build your technical knowledge and develop your career within a large technology organisation.

We’re passionate about building diverse, inclusive teams and actively encourage applications from women, underrepresented groups, and neurodivergent candidates, with support and adjustments available throughout the hiring process.
Because this is an on-site role, you’ll be someone who enjoys being visible and approachable, working alongside colleagues and building good relationships with the people you support.

Due to the nature of the client environment, eligibility for security clearance is required for this role. To meet the current security requirements, candidates must be sole UK nationals and have lived and worked continuously in the UK for the past five years. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider dual nationals for this position.

What you’ll be doing
Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
Providing technical support across desktop and infrastructure services, responding to issues and helping users resolve technical problems.
Working as part of a support team handling calls and incidents across laptops, desktops, VDI and server environments.
Diagnosing and troubleshooting desktop and infrastructure issues, taking ownership where possible and escalating to the appropriate teams when required.
Supporting the installation, configuration, maintenance and deployment of desktop and infrastructure technologies.
Working with Microsoft SCCM and supporting operating system and application deployment.
Supporting technologies including Microsoft Entra, Azure and Intune.
Working with Trellix ePO and client-side agents as part of the wider security and endpoint environment.
Monitoring desktop and infrastructure systems, identifying issues and helping to maintain optimal performance and availability.
Contributing to infrastructure projects, deployments, upgrades and other technical activities, gaining hands-on experience across the wider environment.
Working closely with infrastructure and technical teams to improve efficiency and resolve more complex technical challenges.
Supporting the development and maintenance of technical documentation, including incident reports, configuration details and support information.
Keeping accurate records of incidents, equipment, changes and technical activities.
Following established processes, security requirements and best practices when delivering both desktop and infrastructure support.
Identifying recurring issues and opportunities to improve the service and user experience.
Continuing to develop your technical knowledge and keeping up to date with relevant technologies and industry practices.
What we’re looking for
We’re looking for someone with a solid technical background who enjoys hands-on support and wants to work across both desktop and infrastructure technologies.

You’ll ideally have:
Proven experience working in desktop support, infrastructure support or a similar technical environment.
Experience providing technical support across desktop and infrastructure technologies.
Experience supporting laptops, desktops, VDI and/or servers.
Good troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work through technical issues logically and take ownership of problems.
Experience with Microsoft SCCM and operating system/application deployment.
Knowledge or experience of Microsoft Entra, Azure and Intune.
Experience with Trellix ePO and client-side agents would be beneficial.
A good understanding of common IT hardware, software, networking and infrastructure concepts.
Experience supporting users and working collaboratively with wider technical teams.
Good communication skills and a customer-focused approach.
The ability to work independently while also being a collaborative member of the wider team.

A willingness to learn new technologies and broaden your infrastructure knowledge.

A degree in a relevant subject or equivalent experience would be beneficial.
Relevant IT qualifications or certifications, such as CompTIA A+, Microsoft 365, AWS Cloud Practitioner or similar, are also welcome but are not essential.

What will make you successful in this role?
You don’t need to be an expert in every technology listed above. What’s important is that you have a strong technical foundation, enjoy getting to the bottom of problems and are keen to develop your knowledge across both desktop and infrastructure.

You’ll be comfortable working directly with users while also understanding that good support often means looking beyond the immediate issue and considering the wider infrastructure.

Enjoys solving problems and finding practical solutions.
Takes ownership and follows issues through to resolution.
Is curious about how technology works and keen to learn.
Can explain technical issues clearly to both technical and non-technical people.
Works well as part of a team and is happy to get involved where needed.
Understands the importance of good documentation, process and security.

About Dyad
Dyad's mission is to improve the delivery and efficiency of healthcare.
We are building a platform to model and manage the flow of information within healthcare organisations, improving outcomes for patients, payers, and healthcare providers. We believe data handling in current healthcare systems is needlessly complex and disconnected, leading to isolated and inefficient decision making. To showcase how this technology can advance the delivery of healthcare and improve lives, we build and deploy products for healthcare providers and payers into the UK and US markets.
Dyad is a fast-growing, Series A-funded health tech company with a team of more than 70 people. We are expanding quickly as we grow from primary care into NHS secondary care and new international markets. We are passionate about technology and its applications in worthwhile ventures. New joiners will have a significant impact on the direction of the company, as well as our culture.
Our products
Dyad's Platform: Dyad's products are founded upon our Semantic AI platform, which enables payers and providers to access cutting-edge AI capabilities for their own use cases and applications. Our partners either use the platform APIs directly or work with us to develop applications for their use cases. For more information, please see our Platform page.
Primary care operations: Dyad develops a suite of products for healthcare operations, including:
• BetterLetter, our AI tool helping practices decrease their admin burden in processing clinical letters. We use this to reduce staff time spent identifying codes to be applied to the record as well as suggesting follow-up tasks and workflow optimisations. BetterLetter helps providers save time, save cost, improve performance under audit and build staffing resilience.

The role
As Head of Customer Success at Dyad, you will shape how GP practices and PCN groups experience BetterLetter, making sure every customer gets lasting value from the product and grows with us. As we expand, the role will increasingly focus on growing revenue within our customer base and building the team to support new markets..
You will lead a small Customer Success team: a CS Team Lead and two Customer Success Executives, with further support from our Principal Clinical Practice Specialist. The team takes every practice from contract signature through onboarding, then into a structured account review lifecycle. You will set the standards for that lifecycle, coach the team to deliver it, and personally lead the conversations that matter most: our largest accounts, and practices at risk of not realising the full benefits of AI-assisted coding.
You will lead on keeping and growing revenue across our customer base. That means understanding what each practice and PCN needs, spotting opportunities to extend the value they get from BetterLetter, and acting early when a customer needs extra support. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Commercial and Customer Operations so that customers stay, succeed and expand with us.
This is a senior role in a fast-growing company. BetterLetter is scaling quickly, with a strong pipeline of PCN and federation opportunities and SystmOne practices coming on stream. Our first contracts in new markets are also expected next year. You will build a Customer Success function ready for new markets and a larger, more diverse customer base.
Reporting to: VP Business Operations/VP Customer Operations
Direct reports: CS Team Lead and two Customer Success Executives.
This is a full-time position, which can be offered on a hybrid or remote basis.
Core responsibilities
• Customer success and growth: Partner with BetterLetter’s customers (GP practices and PCNs) to ensure they realise ongoing value, drive high adoption across internal teams, and foster long-term customer advocacy.
• Strategic accounts: Lead quarterly business reviews and annual account plans for our largest practices and PCN groups. Build senior relationships with practice partners, PCN clinical directors and federation leads, and identify expansion opportunities for the Commercial team.
• Customer lifecycle and operations: Oversee onboarding (with practices live within one month of contract) and the account review lifecycle that follows.
• At-risk accounts: Own every practice rated red, at any point in its lifecycle. Put a retention plan in place within 2 working days, lead difficult conversations with practices, and bring in clinical, product and AI expertise to resolve the underlying issue.
• Retention and net churn: Own the company target of net churn. Produce a monthly churn forecast, report gross and net churn to the leadership team, and maintain a single, reliable record of churned and paused practices.
• Re-engagement: Oversee the pipeline of paused practices run by the CS Team Lead, and agree with Sales how practices move between paused re-engagement and churned win-back.
• Complaint handling: Own the customer complaints procedure, built with our Regulatory team to align with our quality management system and ISO 27001. Make sure every complaint is logged, resolved within target and analysed for root causes.
• Team leadership: Line manage, coach and develop the Customer Success team. Set and review individual objectives quarterly, maintain cover across every role, and contribute to hiring as the team grows.
• Customer insight: Turn what the team hears from practices into clear, prioritised insight for Product and AI teams, and make sure practices hear back about the changes made in response.
• Cross-team collaboration: Work closely with Commercial, Product, Engineering, Customer Operations, Regulatory and Clinical colleagues to give practices a smooth journey from contract through to long-term success.Ensure cover in place for every role.

Our hiring process
• Introductory screening interview (30 minutes).
• Interviews with members of the Customer Success and Support team & at least one member of the Senior Management Team.
• Final interview and offer.
Requirements

Credibility with GP practices is essential for this role. Practice managers, partners and PCN leaders need to trust that you understand how general practice works from the inside, so first-hand primary care experience (or equivalent) is our most important requirement.
Must-have:
• Substantial first-hand experience in or of UK primary care. People who have worked as practice managers, operations or business managers, PCN managers, or primary care transformation leads strongly preferred. You understand how GP practices and PCNs work, who makes decisions, and the pressures practice teams face day to day.
• Strong people management skills with a track record of building inclusive, high-performing teams.
• Significant experience in customer success, account management or a comparable customer-facing role, including at least two years leading a team.
• A track record of owning retention or churn targets and improving them.
• Confidence leading difficult conversations with senior stakeholders, such as practice partners and PCN clinical directors.
• Experience designing customer processes, such as onboarding, account reviews, health scoring or complaints handling.
• Comfortable working with data to track customer health, forecast churn and report to a leadership team.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex topics clearly to clinical and non-clinical audiences.
• A proactive, organised and customer-focused approach, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment.
Nice-to-have:
• Experience in health tech, particularly products used by GP practices.
• Familiarity with UK primary care clinical systems such as EMIS, SystmOne or Docman.
• Background in clinical coding or primary care administration (for example SNOMED, QOF/IIF).
• Experience with customer success platforms and CRM tools, such as Custify, HubSpot or Airtable.
• Experience of complaints handling within a regulated or quality-managed environment, such as ISO 13485 or ISO 27001.
• Experience building or scaling a Customer Success function in a growing company.

• Company Pension
• 25 days of paid annual leave (pro-rata)
• A fun and flexible hybrid working environment
• Access to our Employee Assistance Programme - Health Assured
• A modern, dog-friendly office located near Chancery Lane with free drinks

**Purpose of Job**

The Associate Banker contributes to all phases of the project cycle, including project origination, structuring, execution, and implementation and monitoring. The Associate Banker will take responsibility for those tasks assigned to him/her by the operation leader, which may include undertaking comprehensive due diligence, including financial, market, integrity and EBRD policy compliance, as well as effective post-signing implementation and monitoring. The Associate Banker carries out these tasks as part of a project team under the guidance of an operation leader or under the supervision/guidance of more senior bankers or the team Director.

The Associate Banker role may also include elements of business/pipeline development, client management and policy dialogue.

**Background**

The project life-cycle involves several stages from origination to signing, followed by implementation and monitoring until full completion and repayment or exit. All the stages involve different tasks such as business marketing, project due diligence analysis, structuring and approval, negotiation and signing of project agreements, disbursement and monitoring.

The role of the Associate Banker is to contribute, as a project team member, to the structuring, implementation and monitoring of debt and equity transactions, and their effective implementation and monitoring in line with the Bank’s operational objectives.

Under the guidance of the operation leader and/or more senior bankers, the Associate Banker performs those tasks assigned to him/her. The Associate Banker may also co-ordinate the work of more junior team members and interacts with internal and external counterparts as required.

The position will be based in London and will be dedicated to Infrastructure projects across countries in Eurasia. Intensive travel to the region is expected.

**Accountabilities & Responsibilities**

Under the guidance of the operation leader or a more senior banker:

1.           Structuring and Execution

- Work as a project team member on transactions, contributing to all aspects of project structuring and execution, including working with client counterparts, consultants and other parties to progress the project;
- Be the primary driver of the scope and quality of project due diligence, including financial, market, integrity and EBRD policy compliance;
- Prepare internal project documentation, including approval project memoranda,  financial models, draft term sheets,  presentations, etc. as and when required
- Ensure that a project structure addresses CTF requirements.
- Take responsibility, as TC operation leader, to design and process technical co-operation assistance, ensuring that TC processing and approval fits with the approval schedule of any related investment project or the related policy dialogue initiative;
- Ensure that all tasks within his/her are completed within the specified time frames to a high standard and in line with the policies, procedures and objectives of the Bank.

2.           Portfolio Monitoring, Value Creation and Reporting

- Take responsibility for the implementation and monitoring of all projects to which the Associate Banker is assigned, including compliance with project agreements and Bank procedures related to disbursement; monitoring of progress of the project implementation and financial performance of the client; assessing evolving risk factors and monitoring and assessing covenant compliance, in the case of more senior Associate’s they may become the OL for the project once it is in implementation and/or monitoring phase;
- Prepare timely and comprehensive monitoring reports and include recommendations for corrective actions where required and ensure these proposed corrective actions and recommendations are brought to the attention of more senior team members;
- As TC operation leader, ensure effective implementation and monitoring of TC assignments to ensure their compliance with donor reporting requirements, operational objectives and that all reports are of a high quality;
- As a project team member perform all such tasks as may be assigned by the operation leader and provide constructive advice, guidance and supervision to more junior members of the project team.

3.           Business Development

- Assist, as required, with marketing and business development efforts.

The responsibilities of the Associate Banker are designed to allow for the development of transaction expertise and expansion of responsibilities, leading to assuming the role of an operation leader on standard, non-complex transactions. About Evervault

Evervault offers modular payments infrastructure for companies building their own payments stack. We keep raw card data off your systems, cut PCI compliance work, improve acceptance, mitigate fraud and chargebacks and decrease your cost of payments, so you keep full control. Trusted by Ramp, Rippling, Modern Treasury and Overwolf; Series B, led by Ribbit Capital.

Role Overview

You’ll be the first engineer dedicated to our data platform, and you’ll design and build it largely from scratch. You’ll own the platform that collects our event data, models it, and serves it to customers with roughly 15-second freshness, including building our time-series foundations. This is a senior, hands-on role: you’ll set the architecture, write most of the code and set the bar for the data team that grows around you. You’ll work closely with our VP of Engineering, Product and our leadership team. Product decides which data products to build; you own how they’re built and what the data can support.

What You’ll Be Doing

 - Designing and building real-time ingestion for three sources: events our platform already emits, new instrumentation in our product, and data our customers send us

 - Rebuilding our event streaming layer, with the authority to choose how

 - Modelling structured and time-series data in ClickHouse and Databricks so aggregations, trends and benchmarks are fast and cheap at scale (our current defaults, though you can make the case for change)

 - Designing the external data contracts and APIs customers build on, including versioning, reliability and isolation of each customer’s data

 - Defining the event contracts our product engineers instrument against

 - Owning the platform in production: monitoring, data quality, cost and on-call for the systems you build

Your First Year

In your first few months you’ll assess what we have, decide the platform architecture, and scope our first data product with Product and Engineering. After that, you’ll rebuild the streaming layer and ship the first external product on the new platform, most likely aggregated analytics or direct data access for customers. Later in the year you’ll help us hire a domain expert who decides which signals and benchmarks are worth building. Machine learning is out of scope for now; it comes once we have enough clean historical data.

Requirements

 - Production experience building real-time or near-real-time ingestion with event streaming, such as Kafka, Kinesis or Redpanda

 - Deep experience with ClickHouse or a similar analytical database, including modelling time-series data for fast aggregation at volume

 - A track record of shipping an external, multi-tenant data product or data API that customers depended on (internal reporting pipelines alone won’t cover this)

 - Experience migrating a messy live system to a new one without downtime or data loss

 - Senior-level engineering habits: system design, testing, and running the services you build in production

 - Sound judgement working independently: you’ll be our most senior data voice, and we’ll rely on your technical calls

 - A product mindset: you won’t work directly with customers, but you’ll often be the person who knows what the data can and can’t support

Nice to Have

 - Experience in payments or with sensitive, regulated data

 - Databricks or Spark experience alongside ClickHouse

 - Experience as an early or founding member of a data team, including hiring

This Might Not Be for You If…

 - You’re mainly an analyst, BI or data science specialist: this role builds the platform and the external products on it

 - Your experience is mostly dashboards, internal reporting pipelines or modelling for analysis

 - You want a hands-off architect role: you’ll write most of the code

 - You want to work fully remotely: we’re in our Shoreditch office Tuesday to Thursday

Compensation, Benefits & Why Join

 - Competitive salary

 - Stock options with an extended exercise window

 - Private health insurance

 - Unlimited PTO & flexible working hours

 - Daily lunch budget

 - Build a company’s data platform from the first line of code, with the authority to make the big architectural calls and work directly with C-Level

Interview Process

 1. Recruiter Screen

 2. Hiring Manager Interview

 3. Technical Interview

 4. System Design Interview

 5. Final with our Founder

 6. References and Offer

Location

This role is based in London, in our Shoreditch office Tuesday to Thursday. We do not currently sponsor UK work visas.

EXL delivers data and analytics solutions for its clients. As a Data Architect, you will join an engagement with a specialty insurer in the London Market to design, implement and document the data architecture and enterprise data models for a new Azure Databricks data platform. These solutions support enterprise information management, business intelligence, regulatory and actuarial reporting, machine learning and data science.
The Data Architect will translate client business needs into technical solutions, working within the client’s established data guidelines and approaches or helping to define and mature them as required. The Data Architect will develop conceptual, logical and physical data models and work with data engineers to implement these on a lakehouse following medallion architecture principles on Azure Databricks.

• Mentor and coach engineers, analysts and client staff, and provide oversight as required

• Communicate clearly with technical and business stakeholders

• Solve problems independently and raise risks early

 As part of your duties, you will be responsible for:
Architecture and modelling
• Design the lakehouse architecture on Azure Databricks using Delta Lake and the Medallion pattern (bronze, silver and gold layers), organising data by quality and purpose to keep the platform scalable and maintainable.

• Design and apply dimensional models (e.g. star and snowflake schemas) and apply other major approaches such as ODS and Data Vault modelling where they suit the client’s needs.

• Create and maintain conceptual, logical and physical data models, with corresponding metadata, that translate business needs into long-term solutions. Cover core insurance domains such as policy, premium, claims, exposure, reinsurance and finance.

• Design gold-layer (consumption) models and, where Power BI is the consumption layer, semantic models served from Databricks SQL and shaped for efficient reporting and self-service analytics.

• Select and design for the right storage and exchange formats for each workload, including row-based and columnar storage, Delta and Iceberg table formats, and file and message formats (e.g. Parquet, CSV, Excel, XML, JSON, Protobuf).

• Map business processes to conceptual models, using techniques such as bus matrices to identify dimensions, facts and conformed dimensions.

Data strategy and integration

Standards and governance
• Develop and document naming conventions, coding practices, modelling standards and metadata management procedures, and evaluate data models and physical databases for variances against them.

• Define the data governance and security approach using Unity Catalog, including catalogue and schema design, role-based access control integrated with Microsoft Entra ID, row and column-level security, data masking, lineage, tagging and data quality frameworks, appropriate to sensitive and regulated insurance data.

• Define CI/CD and environment promotion patterns for the platform using Git, Databricks Asset Bundles and infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform, Azure DevOps).

• Lead design workshops and coordinate with project managers and client business and technical staff, building trusted relationships and presenting recommendations to senior stakeholders.
