Financial Restructuring - Senior Executive (Manager), London
 
The Opportunity
EY’s Financial Restructuring (FR) team in London is one of the leading teams of its kind in the market, working with stressed and challenged businesses.  FR is part of EY’s Strategy & Transactions business, working with companies and stakeholders at times of change, and often at an exciting pace. FR covers a number of different sub business units and geographies in the UK and you may have the opportunity to work across different teams in your career with FR.
 
Our clients can be companies, government bodies or financial stakeholders like lenders or shareholders.  They might be on the brink of a crisis, or simply looking to build greater resilience into their business.  In FR we work closely with our clients to deliver the financial and organisational solutions that enable them to adapt and succeed or minimise the downside risks that they are facing. 
The work involves understanding the drivers of value in a business and problem solving to manage the priorities of competing stakeholders. People who flourish in FR want to think broadly about what drives value in a company’s performance and the factors that can drive underperformance or failure. Many of our strong performers have moved from other disciplines (Audit, Tax, Forensics) or wider SaT and have varied experience and knowledge which can be applied to a range of project situations.
 
FR is a growing team expecting significant uptick in its market in the coming months, so there is real opportunity to develop and grow your career.  Whilst we do work at pace at times, the team is a welcoming and inclusive place with a good balance of hybrid working and an enjoyable team environment. The team has an inclusive culture where you can bring your whole self to work with a good balance of hybrid working and enjoyable team environment.
 
Your Key Responsibilities
As a Senior Executive (Manager) in FR, you could be involved in all types of work looking at the things that drive a company’s performance or strategies to turn it around or restructure it.  You may be analysing financial forecasts and preparing reports on your findings, interviewing client teams, or executing restructuring procedures. 
Depending on the size and type of project, you may be part of a large project team or leading part of a team yourself, with all the support you need from peers and senior team members to help you learn and flourish in these roles.
We’ll want you to be active in establishing and nurturing relationships – both inside EY with different specialist teams across the firm, and externally – for example with client staff or junior lawyers – as relationship-building is an important and valued skill in FR.
You will also fit in to our positive learning culture from day one.  You will bring your existing skills/knowledge and coach people in these where that is relevant and applicable to our work, and you will be valued for your efforts to coach and counsel junior team members to help them develop.
 
Skills and Attributes for Success 

Financial analysis and scenario modelling to support decision making and execution.
Commercial acumen –using knowledge and insight gained from other client work and apply your understanding of the wider business environment.
Ability to identify the key issues and flag them to seniors, with suggestions for next steps.
Competent at translating analysis into content that can be incorporated directly into written reports for clients.
Ability to share technical and other knowledge with the team drawing on previous experience and current learning
Demonstrate professionalism and sensitivity to both the interpersonal dynamics and the wider firm risk of working with distressed businesses and their stakeholders
Adapt well to change and have a flexible and positive approach
Desire to support the people development of FR – contributing to or leading training courses, recruitment, and team / wellbeing activities.
Desire to learn and proactive in seeking formal and informal learning and training opportunities.

 
To qualify for the role you must have

Track record within a recognised Restructuring or Transactions team for a minimum of 5 years. 
Professional accountancy qualification (ACA/ACCA or equivalent )
Experience of working on independent business reviews and formal corporate insolvencies
Willingness to adapt in a fast paced and changing environment to meet the needs of the business
Appreciation of the sensitivity and heightened risk of working with people in distressed situations

 
Ideally, you’ll also have

Ability to build your own network of contacts and deal professionally and competently with clients, management teams and others outside the firm.
Skills or desire to be a good manager of people – providing feedback and performance reviews to junior staff.
Ability to build strong internal relationships in FR and across other services and can actively participate in business development.

 
What we look for
We are looking for candidates who are highly motivated, ambitious, and have a passion to be part of a fast-paced, successful transaction team where we encourage everyone to bring their whole self to work.  Being a collaborative team player is also important as well as someone who is happy to work flexibly throughout a period of growth within FR.
 
What we offer
We offer a competitive remuneration package where you’ll be rewarded for your individual and team performance. Our comprehensive Total Rewards package includes support for flexible working and career development, and with FlexEY you can select benefits that suit your needs, covering holidays, health and well-being, insurance, savings and a wide range of discounts, offers and promotions. Plus, we offer: 
 

Continuous learning: You’ll develop the mindset and skills to navigate whatever comes next.
Success as defined by you: We’ll provide the tools and flexibility, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.
Transformative leadership: We’ll give you the insights, coaching and confidence to be the leader the world needs.
Diverse and inclusive culture: You’ll be embraced for who you are and empowered to use your voice to help others find theirs.

Manager – Research & Insights
EY Studio+
About EY Studio+
Growth comes from solving problems that matter for people, customers, patients, employees, and society at large. At EY Studio+ UK, we are building a better working world, by putting the human first.  Our work is rooted in the way people make decisions, it’s helps us to help businesses make better choices and solve the most pressing problems. We work with organisations to create the platforms, products and services for tomorrow; making the world an easier, more enjoyable and sustainable place to live and work.  
We don’t yet have all the answers, because that’d be boring, however we do have some of the best minds in the business and we are comfortable navigating complexity every day.
We’re privileged to have access to senior critical thinkers in our clients and we have conversations that excite us and challenge us all the time. We’re becoming an increasingly bigger part of an established global business, which throws up challenges and opportunities every day. Our way of thinking and doing business is infectious, and influencing more and more of the world around us, but that challenges us to go further and scale faster than before. Becoming part of EY Studio+ UK means getting on to enjoy this ride.
 
The opportunity
Growth comes from solving problems that matter for people — for customers, employees and society at large. Research & Insights sits at the intersection of human understanding and commercial impact. We are a group of world-class researchers, data scientists, strategists and designers who help organisations understand the people they serve and turn that understanding into growth.
We believe appreciating human complexity is the key to building empathy and connection - and that the most powerful insight comes from fusing qualitative depth with quantitative rigour, advanced analytics and AI. As a Manager, you will help lead that fusion, contributing to how EY Studio+ delivers evidence-led transformation for some of the largest and most prominent organisations across multiple sectors.
 
The role
This is a management role for a genuine mixed-method researcher with a customer insights specialism who can translate deep customer understanding into strategic direction and action. You will be expected to manage cross-functional insight and customer experience design workstreams, bringing together researchers, analysts, strategists and designers to solve complex client challenges. You will bring a strong understanding of how research informs service design, product design and marketing strategy, and how insight connects to the breadth of EY’s wider offering. You will manage significant elements of complex client engagements, build trusted relationships with client stakeholders, and lead high-performing multidisciplinary teams with support from senior leaders.
There are a couple of things that we ask of everybody. 

You will be endlessly inquisitive, and ruthlessly user focused and able to use a combination of logic, empathy, rigour and storytelling to articulate a customer or business problem before working creatively and technically to articulate a service that solves it. 
You will be a natural collaborator. Ideas breed ideas, and so we work multi disciplinary teams and embed clients in our process. We work in the open, we share our thinking early and we build on each other’s contribution. 
You will be ambitious yet realistic in your solutions. Our work sits in the sweet spot between desirable, viable, feasible and allowable. Getting it there is a big part of what we do. 
You will be a doer AND a thinker and know when to switch from one to the other and how to create time and space for both. 
You will navigate complexity. People, organisations, technology, policies, regulations. Designing services puts you at the centre of complexity. We need to make sense of it all quickly, and flex and adapt to move through it effectively. 
You will be a self-starter and have an explorative mindset, creating new perspectives and identifying the spaces you can be impactful for both EY Studio+ UK and its clients. 

Key responsibilities

You will manage the delivery of complex research and insight programmes, ensuring alignment to client strategy, measurable outcomes and EY quality standards.
You will design and deliver genuinely mixed-method programmes — integrating qualitative design research (ethnography, contextual inquiry, co-creation, diary studies) with quantitative research (U&A studies, concept testing, Voice of Customer and segmentation) — from scoping and survey design through to analysis and reporting — alongside statistical modelling and data analysis.
You will manage cross-functional insight and customer experience design workstreams, aligning research, analytics, strategy and design around a shared customer-led vision, integrated plan and measurable outcomes.
You will apply strong expertise in statistical modelling and advanced analytics, translating complex data into robust, commercially focused recommendations and customer segmentations.
You will embed AI across the research lifecycle — using it to accelerate synthesis, augment analysis and enhance the speed and quality of insight and develop AI-enabled research outputs that positioning EY Studio+ at the leading edge of applied, responsible AI in insight generation.
You will build and maintain strong client relationships, contributing to agendas and supporting strategic customer, brand and growth decisions.
You will contribute to thought leadership on emerging research, insight and AI trends, supporting EY’s position as a long-term strategic partner.
You will lead and develop high-performing cross-functional teams spanning customer insight, data and analytics, strategy and customer experience design; help set direction, clarify accountabilities, enable effective collaboration, and line-manage and coach individuals through the work.
You will act as a role model and coach for junior colleagues, maintaining EY Studio+'s values, high quality of care and strong culture, while managing hard factors such as issues and risks.
You will contribute to business development, including opportunity shaping, developing proposals and client pitches, and supporting pipeline development through your client relationships and market knowledge.
You will contribute to market-facing thought leadership and the evolution of the EY Studio+ proposition and play an active role in the go-to-market for our Solutions, including Customer Experience (CX), shaping how R&I insight is packaged and taken to clients.
You will maintain rigorous standards across project governance, commercial management, risk and quality assurance in line with EY policies.

Skills, attributes and experience

You will demonstrate customer insights specialism and recognised depth in understanding customer needs, behaviours, motivations and experiences, alongside the ability to connect insight to customer experience design and business transformation.
You will have a genuine mixed-method research background with deep, hands-on expertise across both qualitative and quantitative methods, with the ability to design and integrate them within a single programme.
You will have strong experience in statistical modelling and advanced analytics, with a proven ability to turn data into commercial insight.
You will have hands-on proficiency in research and analysis tools - including Q/Displayr, SPSS and Qualtrics – and be be familiarity with behavioural science, systems thinking and social listening methods.
You will be experienced in using AI in research and as an output - applying AI tools to accelerate analysis, synthesis and the creation of research deliverables.
You will have experience leading cross-functional teams and workstreams - with experience of helping set direction and delivering through multidisciplinary teams spanning customer insight, analytics, strategy and customer experience design, while mentoring and growing high-performing practitioners.
You will have a consulting, professional services or agency background, with a track record of managing complex client workstreams or engagements with strong senior-stakeholder communication, storytelling and stakeholder-management skills.

To qualify for the role you must

Be able to describe EY Studio+ UK capabilities and commitments accurately when discussing possible business opportunities with external contacts
Show that you have consistently produced research & insight work of high quality in regulated sectors that is accurate, complete and compelling
Be holding of a Degree level qualification in a relevant field (e.g. social sciences, statistics, psychology, market research, data science).
Ppreviously obtained an industry-recognised research or analytics accreditation (e.g. MRS), or relevant platform/AI certification.
Be able to create presentations that are clear and impactful, translating EY Studio+ UK ’s services into meaningful value propositions for clients
Show how you have contributed to a positive design team environment

 
What working at EY offers
 
We offer a competitive remuneration package where you’ll be rewarded for your individual and team performance. Our comprehensive Total Rewards package includes support for flexible working and career development, and with FlexEY you can select benefits that suit your needs, covering holidays, health and well-being, insurance, savings and a wide range of discounts, offers and promotions. Plus, we offer:
 

Support, coaching and feedback from some of the most engaging colleagues and practitioners around
Opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

 
About EY
 
As a global leader in assurance, tax, transaction and advisory services, we’re using the finance products, expertise and systems we’ve developed to build a better working world. That starts with a culture that believes in giving you the training, opportunities and creative freedom to make things better. Whenever you join, however long you stay, the exceptional EY experience lasts a lifetime.

Desired Skills

We are running an engagement to design and build an AI agent system that manages a complex, high-value transaction workflow for a large enterprise client, from initial engagement through close-out, across a multi-stage process.

ABOUT GIGS

At Gigs, we're building the operating system for mobile services—a platform that lets tech companies embed global connectivity into their products effortlessly.

Just as Stripe lets any business add a payment button in seconds, Gigs empowers platforms to weave in connectivity—bridging the traditional world of telecom with modern tech. From fintechs launching mobile services to HR platforms offering work phone plans, we automate provisioning and remove telecom complexity.

Our team of around 150 people across the US and Europe, backed by nearly $100 million in funding from Ribbit Capital, Google, and Y Combinator. As one of the fastest-growing tech companies, bringing together early-stage engineers, product builders, and business athletes from companies like Stripe, Airbnb, and Shopify. We’re tackling deep technical and regulatory challenges to make connectivity truly seamless.

If you’re driven by curiosity, creativity, and the chance to shape the future of telecom, we’d love to hear from you.




THINGS WE CARE ABOUT

We are building in a highly complex space and tackling a massive problem. We want people who lean in when things get hard.

 - Speed. We move and we ship. We set bold deadlines and treat every week like it matters.

 - Ownership. If you see something broken, fix it. We don't wait for permission.

 - Customer Obsession. Our customers' product is our product.

 - Ambiguity. We're building frontier technology in a complex domain. You'll need sound judgement and good instincts to make decisions without complete information.

 - First principles. We don't ask how things have been done before. We ask why they were done that way at all.


THE ROLE

Gigs signed several major partners this summer, and each one needs someone on the ground to turn the contract into customers. That someone is you.

You'll report to our Head of Marketing and own partner marketing for one market. Your partners include banks, fintechs, retailers and the carriers that supply local lines.

Partners run their own apps, calendars and budgets. You get them to spend on Gigs by showing up with a clearer view of what works than they have, and by getting commitments written into the contract before launch. The best time to shape a partner’s marketing plan is before launch, so you’ll be involved early in the deal.  

Nobody has done this job at Gigs in your market yet. We want a new kind of partner marketer for it: local, close to consumers, and happy to build things with their own hands. You'll do it from scratch, and quickly.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own partner go-to-market. Once a partner integrates, the launch plan, joint calendar, local positioning, budget and results are yours. You also review the creative. You decide what gets made and why.

 - Get marketing into the deal early. Our best leverage comes before signing. You research prospective partners and give a view on whether they'll work. Channels, user reach, lifecycle emails and promo budgets get written into the contract at that stage.

 - Use the partner's own surfaces. In-app placement, push notifications, deep links and rewards programs move attach rate. You find the ones that matter for each partner and persuade them to use those.  

 - Run MDF like an investor. We co-fund a promo only when it brings in new activity, and the partner pays for paid media alongside it. Money is released as milestones are hit. You work with our analytics lead on pre/post and A/B tests so we never pay for sales that would have happened anyway.

 - Adapt the story to your market. A message that lands in New York can fall flat in Paris, London or São Paulo. You decide what carries over and what gets rebuilt. AI can draft, and a native speaker reviews anything going to a wide audience.

 - Be the local voice. You work with PR agencies, local press and podcasts to get the Gigs and partner story out. Carrier launches need legal, comms and compliance sign-offs that can take weeks, so you plan early.

 - Build the playbook for smaller partners. Our biggest partners get a proactive strategy from you. Everyone else gets help on request or a self-serve library covering promotions, social, paid and affiliate, and you help write it.

 - Work with the rest of Gigs. Sales, Partner Success, Product and Design all touch the partner story, as do partner marketers in the US and UK. You keep the story consistent, send local learnings back to the global playbook, and use the intake process so requests arrive scoped.

 - Report on results. Each week you update our growth levers tracker with campaign status and incremental ARR. You carry your share of the marketing incremental ARR target.

 - Use AI daily. It speeds up your drafting and research. You'll also help shape how Gigs and our partners show up in LLMs and other AI-driven channels.

 - Prepare for APAC. As we move into Asia, you turn what works in your market into toolkits that regional leads can pick up.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Selling through partners. You know how to move people you don't manage, such as a bank's marketing head or a carrier's comms team. You're strong before the deal, when positioning and the marketing case get set, and after it, when activation happens. This is the heart of the role.

 - A consumer marketer's instincts. Audience research, lifecycle, CRM, push and in-app messaging are second nature. You know LTV, attach rate, ROAS and incrementality cold. Telco experience is a bonus, and we teach the model. People with a B2B2C background are rare, so consumer subscription, payments and marketplace candidates do well here.

 - Roots in your market. Native French or Portuguese, strong English. You know the local press, the carriers and the banks. You can tell when a message needs translating and when it needs rewriting.

 - Zero-to-one experience. No playbook, no team and no templates existed, and you built the thing anyway. You write the brief and ship the asset yourself. A team may come later.

 - Commercial sense. You understand co-funding, milestone-based spend and the limits of attribution. A revenue play, where co-funding makes sense, looks different to you from a loyalty play, where the partner should pay. We judge this role on your judgment and partner instinct more than on dashboards.

 - Daily AI use. It makes you faster and more creative, and you know which output needs a human reviewer.

 - Startup or agency background. Fintech, payments, marketplaces and consumer subscriptions all translate well. High-growth experience helps.

Bonus points for experience with carriers, eSIM or travel products, merchant-led programs like Apple Pay, or partner programs at a scale-up. Time spent watching a global brand adapt across Latin America, Europe or Asia helps too.

 


WORK AT GIGS

At Gigs, we value in-person collaboration. We believe the best ideas, decisions, and relationships are built when teams spend meaningful time together, and our culture is designed around that belief. We support flexibility where it makes sense. Some focused work can be done remotely, and not every role or week looks the same. You should expect regular time in one of our hubs, as well as occasional travel for team workshops, customer meetings, and Gigs Republic, our bi-annual company off-site. Our offices are designed to feel like home-inspired workspaces, with plants, thoughtful tools, and small, tight-knit teams that make collaboration feel natural, energizing, and effective.




WHAT WE OFFER

At Gigs, we believe in rewarding excellence. We offer competitive compensation and stock options because we see you as a true partner in our growth. We also provide stipends for your home office or work setup, a budget for learning and development to fuel your career, and of course, a free phone and international data plan

Want to learn more about our benefits, hubs, and what it’s like to work at Gigs? Check out our Careers https://gigs.com/careers page.

Affiliate Executive
Department: Marketing
Employment Type: Full Time
Location: London
Reporting To: Angela Brown
Compensation: £34,000 - £38,000 / year

Description

Go City is transforming the way people see and experience the world’s greatest destinations.

We give our customers total flexibility to choose the experiences, tours and activities they want to visit at incredible savings.

The Affiliate Executive supports the day-to-day management, growth and optimisation of the affiliate marketing channel. This is a junior role suited to someone early in their digital marketing career who is organised, commercially curious and eager to develop specialist knowledge in affiliate partnerships, publisher management and performance marketing.

The role reports directly to the Head of Affiliates and works closely with internal teams, affiliate networks, publishers, partners and agencies to help deliver channel targets, improve partner performance and maintain high standards of campaign execution.

This role offers hands-on exposure to affiliate strategy, partner management, reporting, campaign execution and commercial analysis. Over time, the Affiliate Executive will be expected to take on more ownership of partner relationships, campaign optimisation and performance recommendations, with a potential progression path into a more senior affiliate or partnerships role.

What you'll own
Programme delivery & partner management

• Support the Head of Affiliates with the daily running of the affiliate programme, including partner communications, campaign set-up, reporting and administrative tasks

• Help recruit, onboard and activate new affiliate partners, ensuring they understand programme terms, commission structures, tracking requirements and brand guidelines

• Maintain strong relationships with existing affiliates, publishers and network contacts by responding promptly, sharing updates and supporting promotional opportunities

Campaigns & collaboration

• Support campaign planning by coordinating promotional calendars, partner placements, creative assets and tracking links

• Work with internal teams such as marketing, trading, brand, creative, CRM and analytics to align affiliate activity with wider business priorities

• Carry out competitor, publisher and market research to identify new partnership opportunities and channel improvements

Reporting, tracking & compliance

• Assist with weekly and monthly performance reporting, highlighting trends, risks, opportunities and recommended actions

• Monitor affiliate activity to ensure offers, codes, messaging and brand representation are accurate and compliant

• Help validate affiliate transactions, resolve tracking queries and escalate issues where needed

• Keep accurate records of partner activity, agreed placements, commission changes, invoices and campaign performance

Minimum role expectations
Daily

• Clear through the affiliate inbox and ensure every email is responded to appropriately; pass on anything you feel requires the attention of the Head of Affiliates

• Allocate time to work on assigned tasks within the roadmap and flag any issues as soon as they arise to prevent them becoming project blockers

Weekly

• Clear through the publisher approvals on the Partnerize platform and provide a list of who has been onboarded to the Head of Affiliates

• Communicate promotions, terms changes and new business activity to the entire partner base

Monthly

• Validation of pending commissions

• Auditing of partner sites to ensure that content/branding for Go City is compliant

What you'll bring
Essential

• Some understanding of affiliate marketing, digital marketing, partnerships or performance marketing.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to liaise professionally with partners and internal stakeholders.

• Excellent attention to detail, especially when checking tracking links, promotional codes, partner exposure and performance data.

• Comfortable working with numbers, spreadsheets and basic performance metrics such as clicks, conversions, revenue, commission, CPA and ROI.

• Organised and able to manage multiple tasks, deadlines and stakeholder requests in a fast-moving environment.

• Curious, proactive and willing to learn about affiliate networks, publisher models, partner negotiations and channel optimisation.

• Competent with Microsoft Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint.

• Commercial mindset with an interest in how partnerships drive customer acquisition, revenue and brand awareness.

Bonus, not essential

• Internship, placement or relevant coursework experience in affiliate, digital or performance marketing.

• Experience with affiliate platforms, analytics tools or CRM systems.

This role is for you if…

• You demonstrate reliability, accuracy and ownership of assigned tasks, escalating blockers early and clearly.

• You build positive working relationships with affiliates, networks and internal teams.

• You want to develop a clear understanding of the affiliate programme, key partners, commission model, reporting cadence and performance objectives.

• You use data to support recommendations, spot changes in performance and identify opportunities for optimisation.

• You maintain high standards of brand, compliance and promotional accuracy across all affiliate activity.

• You show a learning mindset by asking thoughtful questions, staying close to industry developments and applying feedback quickly.

We own the whole stack that powers Go City — from our passes (pre and post purchase) to order management, from attraction lineups to reservation rules, from payment provider integration to Trade partner management. Our systems include reservations APIs, B2B reseller APIs, pass validation systems and pricing systems, to name a few.

What you'll own
Delivery & business impact

• Plan and own delivery of your backend projects end-to-end — design, build, release and production monitoring

• Break ambiguous or large pieces of work into thin, releasable slices, managing dependencies with other teams (e.g. [name specific teams]) to keep delivery unblocked

• Connect your technical work to the business outcomes it serves, from pass sales to partner transactions, and challenge requirements that don’t serve the intended outcome

• Build working knowledge of adjacent disciplines so you can spot problems or improvements that cross team boundaries

Technical craft

• Design backend solutions that span multiple services or components, documenting the trade-offs you considered

• Produce code and designs used as the quality reference for others — testable, secure, observable and performant by default

• Define the test strategy for work you lead, treating security, performance and accessibility as design inputs, not afterthoughts

• Unblock colleagues on hard technical problems, including outside your immediate area when needed

Operational excellence

• Build observability into every change by default

• Lead diagnosis of complex production issues through to root cause, and lead incident response for the team’s services

• Facilitate post-incident reviews and act on what comes out of them

What you'll bring
Essential

• You design backend solutions across multiple services or components, with trade-offs made explicit.

• Your work is used as the quality reference in teams you've been part of — testable, secure, and observable by default.

• You've owned testing, release reliability and monitoring on work you've led.

• You're comfortable working in our stack: Java / Spring Boot, TypeScript, AWS, Kubernetes.

• You communicate technical context clearly to engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike.

• You mentor colleagues and raise team standards through code review feedback and knowledge sharing.

• You unblock colleagues on hard technical problems.

• 
Databases — PostgreSQL and/or DocumentDB: schema design, query optimisation, indexing, data modelling at scale.

• 
Kafka / event streaming — topic design, consumer group management, ordering guarantees, failure handling.

• 
Other backend infrastructure — equivalent depth in distributed systems, API design at scale, or platform reliability.

• Some frontend exposure (React, Node).

• "You build it, you run it" is how you already think.

job_description:
For candidates seeking to be located at our Stevenage site, this role will temporarily be based at Stevenage. However, the Company plans to relocate its offices to Cambridge, UK. The location of this role will therefore subsequently change to Cambridge, UK in accordance with timelines to be set by the Company. As VP Medicine Development Leader (MDL) - Oncology, you will strategically lead the optimal global development of a medicine at an asset level, acting as the single point of accountability for the medicine from clinical Proof of Concept (PoC) to Approval in the first major market(s).

By working with the various stakeholders across GSK’s Medicine Development matrix (R&D, Manufacturing, Commercial, etc.), you will define the strategic vision and operational plan for the medicine, aligning it with the overall organizational strategy. You will create and lead the matrixed Medicine Development Team (MDT), which is responsible for representing the various disciplines required to optimally deliver the development of the medicine including Clinical Development, Medical, Commercial and Manufacturing, amongst others.

Accountability and key responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Acting as a single point of accountability in GSK for all aspects of a medicine being developed globally, from clinical PoC to Approval in the first major market(s)
• Working closely with the Early Development Lead (EDL) and Medicine Commercial Lead (MCL) to ensure a smooth transition of the lead indication(s) from the EDL upon achievement of clinical PoC and to the MCL upon Approval in first major market(s)
• Post-approval, provides key support to the Medicine Commercial Team (MCT) in the first major markets ensuring the MDT provides optimal support to registration, including Post-Marketing Requirements (PMRs) and life cycle management (LCM) in the major markets
• Works with the functional line Heads supporting RIIRU to select MDT members and leads this multi-disciplinary matrix team, supporting differentiated development for team members, owning the performance of the MDT and partnering with Line Managers to drive performance
• Partners with the Pipeline Project Manager (PPM), energizes and motivates the MDT to drive a high performing team and operational delivery of the project, including setting team objectives to ensure successful project delivery, including options for acceleration, parallel indication development and smart risk-taking.
• Partners with R&D Business Development, leading the development planning for a prospective in-licensed asset by bringing together input from the relevant functions and TA experts to develop a Medicine Profile (MP) and development plans including but not limited to clinical feasibility, regulatory planning and CMC risk mitigation
• Leads the cross-functional MDT to:
• • Establish a compelling vision for the medicine and MP which positions the medicine within the R&D strategy taking the competitive landscape into account, translating GSK’s strategy into asset strategy and actionable plans for multiple areas or functions

• • Deliver differentiated medicines of value for patients, stakeholders and markets through an evidence package that supports regulatory approval, market access and the product’s life cycle

• • Prioritize and maximize the asset’s development options including developing multiple indications

• • Partner with the Global Medical Lead (GML) and MCL to develop an indication expansion and LCM plan for the asset.

• • Make clear evidence-based go / no go / accelerate decisions and identify clear inflection points, based on whether the results fulfil the strategy set out for the medicine

• • Ensure excellence in execution of all governance processes, including MDT members, e.g., the Clinical Development Lead (CDL) partnering with other matrix Leads, such as the Global Regulatory Lead (GRL), the GML, etc. on oversight of clinical studies, patient safety & pharmacovigilance, scientific engagement and promotional practices

• • Enhance patient focus by incorporating the voice of the patient into development plans

• • Increase visibility amongst the external communities (physicians, regulators, patients, payers) to bring medical solutions to patients with unmet medical needs, thereby enhancing GSK’s reputation and showcasing our ambition for patients

• Serves as the asset’s single point of contact and spokesperson to Senior Management, senior boards, other relevant internal governance committees and external Advisory Committees, as needed, e.g., Chief Scientific Officer, TA Head, Chief Medical Officer, TA Development Review Board and Portfolio Investment Board
• Delivers and manages the asset resourcing plan (people & finances), including serving as the single point for accountability for managing the asset budget to the agreed variance, working closely with the PPM and Finance Partner to do so

This position is offered as a hybrid position with a required on-site presence at least two days per week at one of GSKs US (Waltham, MA or Upper Providence, PA), Switzerland (Zug) or UK (GSK HQ or Stevenage/Cambridge) sites.

Why You?

Basic Qualifications:

• Advanced degree including MD, PhD, PharmD, MBA, MS
• Oncology drug development experience within the global pharmaceutical and/or biotechnology industry
• Filing experience with BLA/NDA/MAA submissions as a core responsibility 
• Experience in the entirety of oncology drug development across the R&D/commercial life cycle including Discovery, late-stage Development, Regulatory, Manufacturing, Medical and Commercial
• Experience in oncology product development and/or commercialization, in late phase development (from clinical PoC onwards), clinical trial management, post-approval studies, regulatory and manufacturing compliance 
• Experience leading teams in a complex, matrixed, global and multi-disciplinary organization with high accountability, minimal authority and multiple lines of reporting 
• Experience working with regulators and with regulatory requirements including legal and government frameworks within and across global geographies 
• Experience creating the strategy for pre- and post-marketing studies and driving the lifecycle process 
• Experience building budgets and leading the strategic and budget planning process 
• Experience in the healthcare environment, and access in all major markets

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience leading oncology drug development programs in gastrointestinal (GI) or pancreatic cancers is preferred
• Highly developed ethics and integrity, with demonstrated ethical medical decision-making skills 
• Strong matrix leadership and motivational skills 
• Ability to work collaboratively and successfully across functions – Research, Commercial, Regulatory, Global Medicine Supply, Legal, regions etc.

Business Strategies, Collaborative Partnerships, Commercial Acumen, Digital Fluency, Drug Development, Drug Regulatory Affairs, Evidence Based Decision Making, Executive Presence, Hematology and Oncology, Innovative Leadership, Matrix Leadership, Prioritization, Scientific Data Analysis, Scientific Presentations, Team Development

Creating the Extraordinary, Together.

Role Purpose 
The FMUK AI Lead sets the vision for how AI can make Fremantle UK a more competitive and future-ready business. They own the resulting AI strategy and is accountable for turning it into measurable value across programme-making and the wider business.
The role spans two connected areas: production enablement, from creative development through to delivery, and productivity enablement across FMUK's corporate and operational functions. The Lead sets an ambitious direction, decides where to invest, champions new ways of working, and holds the relationships that make adoption possible: with MDs and CEOs, senior editorial, Heads of Production, functional leaders and the Global AI team.
The Lead will shape how FMUK's producers, editorial teams and storytellers use AI to originate, develop and make better programmes, explore new formats and new ways of engaging audiences, and open up new creative and commercial opportunities, while protecting the creative integrity, talent relationships and intellectual property on which the business depends.
The ideal candidate is an imaginative and credible leader who understands how programmes are made and the pressures production teams face, who can inspire creative and production teams to see what AI makes possible, who can weigh creative ambition against commercial, legal and operational realities, and who can build engagement across a federated group of companies.

• Vision, creative leadership and innovation
• Articulate a compelling, ambitious vision for how AI can enhance creativity and storytelling at FMUK, from originations and development through to delivery and audience, and bring editorial, production and executive leaders with you.
• Champion creative innovation: explore how AI could open up new formats, creative workflows, ways of developing and pitching ideas, and new audience and commercial opportunities, in partnership with creative leaders, talent and buyers/clients.

• Strategy, governance and the Group
• Own FMUK's AI strategy, setting a bold multi-year vision, and translate it into a prioritised roadmap that balances quick wins with longer-term, transformational bets, with clear objectives, owners, milestones and measures of success.
• Advise and challenge the FMUK Executive Team on strategic opportunities, how AI could shape FMUK's competitive position and ways of working, investment, dependencies and risks, and report regularly on progress, benefits and decisions required.

• Own responsible-AI governance for FMUK: set a clear, principled position on the creative and ethical use of AI that protects talent, contributors and IP, and ensure compliance with Group policy, legal requirements and production obligations, working with Legal and Business Affairs, Data Protection, Information Security and HR.
• Scan developments in AI, creative technology and the wider industry, anticipate emerging opportunities and risks, and turn them into clear, timely perspectives and strategic choices for FMUK.
• Enablement
• Direct the identification and prioritisation of production use cases where AI or automation enhances creativity and quality or improves speed, efficiency or cost, across development, scheduling, budgeting, production paperwork, archive, post-production, graphics, transcription, logging and content creation.
• Create space for creative experimentation: sponsor pilots, labs and showcases that let producers, editorial and creative teams explore what AI can do for their programmes in a safe, supported environment, and amplify what works.

• Ensure every initiative is grounded in a genuine production need and reflects creative judgement, production realities and buyer/ client requirements.
• Ensure implementation includes process redesign, training, creative upskilling and change management, not just tool deployment, and that successful approaches are scaled across FMUK.
• Hold the senior relationships with company CEOs, editorial leaders and Heads of Production, acting as a trusted thought partner who brings ideas and inspiration as well as delivery.
• Team, investment and adoption
• Lead, inspire and develop the FMUK AI team, setting a clear vision and objectives, managing performance, creating clear accountability across production enablement, productivity enablement and technical delivery, and fostering a culture of curiosity and ownership.
• Oversee local investment in tools and initiatives, with clear criteria for prioritisation, production impact, deliverability, cost and risk, visibility of benefits realised, and space for exploratory, higher-risk innovation where the learning is the value.
• Chair the FMUK AI Champion Network and, with Internal Comms and the People Team, build engagement, confidence and enthusiasm among colleagues with varying levels of AI knowledge, inspiring them to experiment and share what they learn.
• Coordinate with Global AI, IT, engineering, procurement and external partners where specialist capability is needed, and foster a culture of curiosity and responsible experimentation with clear accountability.

Job Description:
Customer Experience Strategist
CX, Service Design & UX | UK Hybrid

We’re looking for a Customer Experience Strategist to join Remedy Edge’s growing Experience team.

This is a hands-on strategy role sitting across customer experience, service design, digital product thinking and UX.

You’ll help us understand what patients, HCPs and other healthcare audiences need, identify where experiences aren’t working, and translate those insights into better journeys, services, tools and digital experiences.

What makes the role different?
Our Experience team often works upstream of traditional creative and production.

One project might involve understanding friction across a complex patient or HCP journey and redesigning the service around it. Another might involve helping define a new digital tool, platform or support experience, developing its architecture and user flows, prototyping how it could work and testing the concept before it moves into full design and build.

So we’re looking for someone comfortable moving between: research → CX strategy → service design → UX → prototypes → testing.

You won’t need to be a UI designer or developer. But you should understand experience and UX deeply enough to help define what should be created, why it matters and how it should work.

What you’ll be doing:
· Develop customer journeys and experience strategies.
· Identify customer needs, behaviours, barriers and opportunities.
· Create journey maps, service blueprints and future-state experiences.
· Help design new services, tools and digital experiences.
· Develop UX principles, information architecture and user flows.
· Work with wireframes and prototypes to make ideas tangible.
· Contribute to concept and usability testing.
· Facilitate workshops and confidently work directly with clients.
· Collaborate with designers, creatives, technologists and developers.
· Work on global programmes that create master experiences for local markets to adopt and adapt.
· Contribute to pitches and the continued growth of Remedy Edge’s Experience offer.

What we’re looking for:
You will have extensive relevant experience across areas such as Experience Strategy, CX, service design, UX strategy, digital product or service design, or digital transformation.

You’ll have strong human-centred thinking and be comfortable taking work from an ambiguous customer problem towards a practical experience solution.

We’d particularly like to see experience in:
· Customer or user research.
· Journey mapping.
· Service design.
· UX principles.
· Information architecture and user flows.
· Wireframes or prototyping.
· Client-facing strategy and workshops.
· Collaborating with design and technology teams.

Experience with Figma or similar design and prototyping tools is useful. Curiosity about AI-enabled prototyping and new ways of making and testing ideas is encouraged.

Healthcare experience would be helpful, but it isn’t essential. We’re also interested in people from agencies and consultancies working across complex, service-led or regulated industries.

Why Remedy Edge?
We’re building Experience as a strategic capability that connects CX, service design, product thinking and UX, rather than treating UX simply as downstream design or production.

That means you’ll get the opportunity to help clients decide what experience should exist and how it should work, then make that strategy tangible enough to prototype, test and ultimately build.

Job Description:
The Media Intelligence Manager sits at the intersection of media operations, data, reporting and decision support. The role is accountable for making media data more complete, accurate, usable and actionable, while helping evolve the operating model from report production toward intelligence-led operations.

The role should create leverage for Global and Regional teams: less manual intervention, clearer signals, stronger data confidence and faster translation of information into action.

Core Accountabilities:

Media Intelligence Operations
Provide senior oversight of day-to-day intelligence workflows, priorities, service quality, issue resolution and stakeholder responsiveness across the remit.

Data Quality & Governance
Drive standards, QA and exception management across media data, with a focus on completeness, consistency, accuracy and correct application of key metadata and taxonomy.

Reporting & Insights
Oversee recurring reporting, scorecards, performance views, alerts and insight outputs; continuously improve relevance, usability and actionability.

Stakeholder Enablement
Work with Global, Regional and Local teams to understand needs, improve adoption and translate complex data into clear guidance and actions.

Transformation
Lead contribution to future-state intelligence initiatives, including any discovery, requirements, prioritisation, testing and transition planning, while protecting continuity of current services.

Continuous Improvement
Identify recurring pain points, automate repetitive work, improve workflows and feed learnings into product, process and governance roadmaps.

Key Responsibilities:

• Help lead delivery of priority Media Intelligence workflows across Global and Regional stakeholders, ensuring clear ownership, timing and service standards.

• Establish and maintain robust data-quality checks, exception processes and issue-resolution routines across media data inputs and reporting workflows

• Translate business and media requirements into practical reporting, insight and data solutions in partnership with data, technology and product owners.

• Manage the quality and relevance of scorecards, dashboards, alerts and insight outputs, ensuring they answer real planning, activation and governance questions.
• Partner with Digital Operations and Governance teams to connect data quality signals to operational actions, including taxonomy, platform setup and campaign governance.
• Use recurring reporting and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, root causes, recurring exceptions and opportunities for process improvement.
• Support the development of automation and AI-enabled intelligence use cases where there is a clear business need, measurable benefit and appropriate governance.
• Contribute to MIQ discovery and future-state design by defining user needs, data requirements, operational dependencies, acceptance criteria and transition considerations.
• Maintain a structured backlog of intelligence improvements, prioritising work against business impact, user value, operational risk and scalability.

What You Will Bring:
• Experience in data platforms, reporting infrastructure, cloud architecture, or related technology leadership roles.
• An understanding of modern data architectures, cloud platforms and the technologies that underpin data transformation and automation programmes.
• An understanding of media investment, marketing technology, reporting platforms, and measurement ecosystems.
• A curious, analytical mindset with the ability to turn complex media data into clear conclusions and practical actions.
• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy, quality, governance and continuous improvement.
• The ability to work confidently across Media Operations, Planning, Activation, Marketing Effectiveness, Data and Technology teams.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively, simplify complexity and build trust with Global, Regional and Local teams.
• A practical approach to problem solving: able to identify root causes, prioritise opportunities and translate requirements into scalable solutions.
• An interest in emerging technology, automation and AI, with the judgement to understand where new capabilities can create meaningful business value.
• A collaborative and proactive mindset, sharing learnings openly and helping build a consistent Media Intelligence capability across the wider organisation.

• Develop strategic media plans, including budget recommendations, forecasting and investment allocation.
• Take ownership of day-to-day client relationships, leading performance discussions, reporting calls and presenting actionable recommendations.
• Drive campaign performance through advanced optimisation techniques, including value-based bidding, audience strategies and testing.

Senior Finance Business Partner

London (Hybrid Working)

About McCann

McCann, part of the Omnicom Group (NYSE: OMC), is one of the world's largest advertising agencies. McCann’s operations are united across 5,000+ employees in 120 countries by a single mission: to help brands play a meaningful role in people’s lives. This commitment focuses on creating work that earns a role in people’s lives by being interesting, evocative, and useful. McCann achieves this mission through building brand platforms that last, powered by the creative philosophy “Truth Well Told”).

Job overview

The primary focus of the Senior Finance Business Partner role is the management of the McCann London revenue position. The SFBP is a senior role in the commercial team with three core responsibilities; ensuring revenue is booked in the OMC financial system monthly in line with compliance requirements, accurately forecasting revenue for future periods and assisting account teams with the objective of delivering revenue in a profitable way. The SFBP is supported in these goals by Client Finance Managers (CFMs). People management is, therefore, a key requirement for this role.

Key Responsibilities

• Month end reporting – prepare and manage the month end revenue position by client, ensuring all revenue booked is compliant with OMC revenue recognition policies and posted in the finance system. By exception post revenue by journal, if PE is obtained and system entry is not possible, and reconcile the overall position - forecast file to system entry. Provide variance analysis commentary as required.
• Revenue forecasting – work with the client Business Leads to maintain the ongoing forecast revenue position for forward months by client, ensuring that all material movements are shared and explained to the CFD. Assist the CFD and the FP&A/MI Lead with any information required for upward revenue reporting into OMC.
• Receivables – regularly review EBU, pre-bill, WIP and debtor balances to ensure accuracy and work with CFMs to take timely actions to minimise aging, clear as required and ensure collectability.
• Workflow – from new client and job set up to work delivery and job closure, all project workflows need to be managed to ensure all elements of revenue, interco revenue, third party costs and expenses are correctly recorded and managed through our financial system. The SBP oversees this process to ensure all parties (CFMs, BL & PM and shared services) do the right things at the right time in a compliant manner.
• Profitability – using information prepared by the FP&A/MI Lead, work with the BL & PM teams to affect change and profitability improvement through pricing review and changes to ways of working. Assist the CFD or CFO with client facing discussions to improve commercial terms as required.
• Client contracts and reporting – manage ongoing client contractual compliance including any reporting requirements agreed in contracts and SOWs. Assist with management of client audits or ad hoc client information requests as required. Ensure all client PRPs, volume rebates or other such variable compensation arrangements are correctly calculated and accounted for.
• Internal and external audits – manage the preparation of all revenue related information to internal and external auditors and promptly respond to all related queries. Ensure all McCann London revenue recording and revenue procedures are S-Box compliant.
• Skills development – manage the new staff induction process for all relevant employees – BL, PM and finance – to ensure they are up to speed with our procedures as soon as possible. As ways of working are refined and developed ensure all relevant employees are kept abreast of process changes and we continue to operate commercially in a compliant manner with best in class practice the goal.
• Ad hoc support to CFD – support the CFD as required on new business pitches and any other finance projects and initiatives from time to time.

Required behaviours and competencies
Essential:
• Previous experience in a similar role in finance or accounting
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Excellent attention to detail and organisational abilities.
• Effective communication and teamwork skills, including people management
• Ability to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.

Nice to have:

• Previous experience within an advertising / marketing agency is highly advantageous
• Vantage (SAP) knowledge is desirable but not essential
• ACCA/CIMA qualified or working towards qualification

The Role

We are looking for a Data Management and Visualisations Snr Manager to join our growing Data Management and Visualisation team.
We are increasingly involved in ensuring all media activity is delivered following not only overall best practice guidelines, but also with complex and detailed processes and rules. We require an experienced candidate with a high level of understanding of the media environment to not only devise and support these processes, but to also ensure that these are being observed throughout the OMD network in EMEA and beyond.
This role would ideally be best suited to someone who has strong media experience with reporting or data management on large scale campaigns on multiple ad-servers across EMEA, and who is now looking to take that experience into a wider leadership role. There will be a focus to lead operations for necessary communication across OMD markets & partner agencies to manage data governance, quickly resolve errors and identify opportunities to evolve projects.

They will use a variety of tools, practices, and processes to deliver best in class data governance across our client base. You should also be comfortable with ETL processes and be familiar with cloud-based backend data architecture.
We are looking for a strong leader, with an entrepreneurial spirit, who is as comfortable in front of a client as they are mentoring and growing more junior members of the team. Having excellent communication skills with ability to showcase achievements and promote solutions to the wider agency with a positive motivational team ethic. Ideally, your career experience has been gained in media agency/marketing agency, and you are comfortable dealing with multiple stakeholders and juggling priorities. 
This is an exciting role with excellent career opportunities and benefits within a high-profile team. To that end, we are looking for someone who can hit the ground running, define their work efficiently, and drive the visualisation and data performance reporting practice area within the overall team and agency.

Senior Strategist

You play a crucial role in delivering brand strategies. You will use your knowledge and experience to think about how we could do things differently, try new approaches and put them into practice. 

27 years young with a head full of big brand experience and a gaze fixed firmly on the future, our work over the last two decades has changed the brand landscape today. What we do next will change tomorrow.

We’re based in some of the most exciting and vibrant cities on the planet, balancing global scale with cultural connection. That means we’re on the doorstep of many of the world’s biggest brands, and within reach of the very best talent around.

Together, we are a diverse brand, experience and design community who believe that brand is how a company’s people, products and services behave wherever and whenever they show up in the world. Our work focuses on measuring and maximizing brand behaviour by connecting corporate purpose with everyday lived experience.

It's through this work that we deliver our purpose: To transform the future of businesses by changing how their brands behave today.

And because we believe strongly that the future our brands create must be a future for us all, our shared values - Progressive, Adaptable, Collaborative and Empowering - put difference and diversity at our core.

• Develop a point of view as to how to use a future brand strategy to deliver a more connected brand experience
• Bring in leading edge thinking and ideas from the world around us to develop projects, seen as a thought leader you develop and drive the narrative arc of projects
• Bring in ideas and influences from the outside world and apply these into projects
• Experiment with new approaches and create new opportunities within projects to develop our offer and broaden / deepen our relationships with clients
• Provide inspiration for building future brands, generating hypotheses 
• Steer and shape the internal building and testing of those hypotheses, providing relevant reference points from inside and outside the category 
• Crystallise your thinking and provide thought leadership 
• Build strong relationships and collaborate within the strategy team and across the agency
• Ensure that our work and ideas will be practical and impactful 
• Lead a full breadth of strategy projects (i.e. positioning, architecture, naming, design, activation) across multiple industries
• Contribute to a highly collaborative and energized atmosphere in which collaboration and positive disruption are encouraged
• Develop a strong understanding of the FutureBrand offering and disciplines and of our clients’ business and clearly articulate this
• Participate in and lead new business pitches
• Nurture, mentor and support junior team members. Use your experience to advise the team on how to shape and deliver great work.

 Skills and Competencies

• Proven experience delivering brand strategies
• Able to clearly communicate ideas and have strong verbal and written skills
• Able to build strong, personable and effective working relationships at all levels, both internally and externally
• Experience mentoring team members
• Delivers results through teamwork
• Proactive, involves others and communicates with others to make things happen
• Problem-solving approach
• Forever curious and ask questions to help you develop
• Excellent attention to detail
• Confident presenting
• Keen to develop and seek opportunities to take on more responsibility
• Open to feedback so that you can build and develop
• Remain calm when working under pressure and encourage the team to do so
• Able to interpret large amounts of information and effectively communicate findings and conclusions 

FutureBrand Values

Progressive
Being progressive has always been about optimism, momentum, and openness. Staying progressive means also ensuring what we do s underpinned by embracing a rich diversity of talents, perspectives, and ideas. Only when we have heard from all can we be sure what we do and who we have what it takes to stand out and be truly future proof.
Adaptable
We are comfortable with and open to challenge and change. We live and work in a vibrant, diverse, and dynamic world. To thrive, brands need to balance the time-less and the contemporary, art with science and continually step between facts, data, and creativity – which means we must too.
Collaborative
We believe that ideas get better when they are inherently diverse and shared in highly inclusive ways. We reject traditional hierarchies and what to hear from those who think differently from us, both inside and beyond our businesses. We truly believe that bringing different people together makes great things happen. This is a fundamental benefit of being a global business and we need to make it count.
Empowering
We champion the diversity and equity of opinions, ideas, skills, and perspectives for the difference it brings and the value it creates for all. We believe that diversity, equity and inclusion empowers and are therefore core to our people and our business. We invest in each other’s growth and ensure every person’s professional path is well paved. We welcome frank conversations about where we can do better, and we push ourselves and our clients to adopt more inclusive practices.

Working with clients and brands.
At FutureBrand, we work with clients across various industries and geographies, including tobacco, gas and oil. We're committed to creating meaningful change with the brands we work with, but we understand people have different values and comfort levels.

At Hyperbolic, we’re making global AI compute liquid. We bring fragmented, heterogeneous GPU capacity together into one unified, productive platform, making it easier to access, sell, resell, manage, and orchestrate the resources that power AI. For neocloud, we turn GPU capacity into productive infrastructure that delivers lasting value and accelerate their time to market.

We believe bold ideas deserve the computing power to become reality. We’re building toward a future where compute flows as freely as electricity, available when and where it’s needed, so builders everywhere can turn their most ambitious ideas into breakthroughs.

We’re looking for curious, driven people who take ownership, challenge assumptions, and care deeply about what they build. If you’re energized by hard problems and want to help shape how the world accesses AI, we’d love to build with you.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Our reserved customers run large multinode GPU clusters, and when those clusters misbehave the problem is rarely simple. You are the engineer embedded with those customers: you stand their cluster up, you hand it over, and you stay with it.

You do not own tickets. You own environments. Technical Support Engineers own the ticket lifecycle and pull you in when an issue needs real depth: multinode collective performance, hardware faults, fabric problems, or a provider who needs to be told what is wrong with their hardware.

One thing we will be straight about, because it shapes the job. We aggregate capacity from suppliers rather than owning most of the hardware ourselves. That means a real part of this role is technical liaison work: proving where a fault actually lives, taking it to the provider with evidence, and coordinating the fix on the customer's behalf. The engineers who enjoy this role are the ones who find that interesting rather than frustrating.



Who You Are

 - Cluster stand-up and handoff. Build, validate, and benchmark new customer clusters, then hand them over with documentation the customer's own engineers can work from.

 - Deep escalations. Multinode and NCCL performance debugging, GPU and hardware faults (XID and ECC errors, lspci, dmesg), driver and fabric issues, container and scheduler problems.

 - Provider escalation and coordination. Maintenance windows, RMAs, hung nodes, and disputed fault attribution. You bring the evidence that makes the provider act, and you keep the customer informed while it happens.

 - Embedded ownership of named accounts. You are the engineer your customers know by name. You learn their workload, not just their infrastructure, and you tell them what to change before they hit the wall.

 - Proactive monitoring. Own the monitoring and alerting we put in front of customer clusters (Grafana, Prometheus) so we find faults before the customer reports them.

 - Tooling and pushing work down. Automate the repeat work and turn your own escalations into runbooks the L1 tier can run. Anything you fix three times should stop reaching you.

 - Deep Linux experience and total comfort in the CLI, including in someone else's broken environment.

 - Hands-on multinode GPU experience: NCCL, InfiniBand or RoCE, collective performance debugging, topology and placement.

 - Hardware fault triage on GPU nodes: XID and ECC errors, dmesg, lspci, nvidia-smi, thermal and power faults.

 - Experience provisioning and operating GPU clusters with Kubernetes, Slurm, or both.

 - Genuinely comfortable customer-facing, including delivering bad news and saying “this is ours” or “this is the provider’s” with confidence.

 - Sound judgment on when to keep digging and when to escalate.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with parallel filesystems (Weka, Lustre, GPFS) and high-performance storage.

 - Grafana, Prometheus, or similar observability stacks in production.

 - Prior forward deployed engineer, solutions architect, or technical account manager experience.

 - Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible) and CI for cluster provisioning.

 - Exposure to model training or inference workloads from the practitioner side.



Hyperbolic is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

ABOUT HYPEREXPONENTIAL (HX)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.




HOW WE WORK

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 2, that looks like this:

 


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

 - Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

 - Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

 - Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

 - Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

 - Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO HAVE DONE

 - Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

 - Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

 - Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

 - Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

 - Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

 - Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

 - Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

 


YOU’RE UNLIKELY TO THRIVE HERE IF

 - You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

 - You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

 - You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document https://hx.wiki/ leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 


COMPENSATION

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.




BENEFITS

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life http://Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. Initial chat with our Talent team

 2. Lead Hirer Interview

 3. Live AI Skills Assessment

 4. Values Interview with the CPTO

 5. Meet the CEO

 


OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 


NEXT STEPS

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.
