job_description:
Who we are 🌍
We’re IAG Loyalty - one organisation with two ambitious, growing divisions across Loyalty and Holidays. Each has its own goals, strategy and team, but together we’re united by a shared vision to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences.

Our Loyalty division is home to Avios, the global loyalty currency, enabling millions of members to collect and spend rewards across travel, retail and financial services.

Our Holidays division, including British Airways Holidays and Iberia Vacaciones, brings together trusted brands, connecting customers to thousands of destinations worldwide through seamless, end-to-end travel experiences.
We’re on an exciting journey of growth and transformation – we’re going places.

The opportunity ✨
Are you a hands-on engineering leader who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, shaping architecture and helping developers do their best work?
At IAG Loyalty, we're looking for a Tech Lead to help shape the future of our customer contact technology, building scalable, cloud-native solutions that connect our customers, colleagues and digital products.

This is an opportunity to take real ownership of technical design and delivery. You'll be making architectural decisions, getting hands-on with code and guiding engineers to build secure, reliable and high-performing solutions that make a genuine difference to how we support millions of Avios customers.
Working with technologies including Node.js, React, TypeScript and AWS, you'll help evolve our technology, tackle complex integrations and introduce new capabilities that improve both the customer and colleague experience. You'll have the freedom to challenge existing approaches, influence technical direction and drive engineering best practices.

Our customer contact technology includes Amazon Connect, alongside integrations with our wider Loyalty Platform, web and mobile channels. You don't need contact centre or Amazon Connect experience to succeed here. We're much more interested in your software engineering background, architectural thinking and ability to lead technical delivery.

What you'll be doing 🚀
As our Tech Lead, you'll be the technical driving force behind our Customer Contact products, combining hands-on software engineering with architectural ownership and technical leadership.

You'll design, build and evolve scalable, cloud-native applications and services using modern technologies including Node.js, React, TypeScript and AWS. Working closely with our Product Manager, you'll translate product ambitions into practical technical solutions, making architectural decisions that balance customer needs, security, performance and long-term maintainability.

You'll take ownership of complex technical challenges, from designing APIs and integration patterns to connecting our customer contact technology with the wider Loyalty Platform, web and mobile applications, and third-party systems. You'll help evolve our existing capabilities and shape new solutions that improve efficiency, reliability and the overall customer and colleague experience.

Remaining close to the code, you'll contribute to development, review technical solutions and champion high engineering standards. You'll help improve testing practices, CI/CD pipelines and system performance, ensuring the technology we build is secure, maintainable and ready to scale.

Beyond hands-on delivery, you'll guide and mentor engineers, share knowledge and encourage fresh thinking across the team. Working collaboratively with Product Managers, architects and engineering teams across IAG Loyalty and the wider group, you'll help shape technical direction, challenge existing approaches and continuously improve how we design and deliver software.

What you'll bring ⚡
We're looking for someone with a strong software engineering background who enjoys being hands-on, solving complex problems and taking ownership of technical decisions.

• Software engineering expertise – strong hands-on experience designing, developing and delivering modern applications, ideally using Node.js, React and TypeScript, with a solid understanding of frontend and backend development, APIs and software design patterns.
• Architecture and technical design – experience designing scalable services, APIs and distributed systems, with the ability to evaluate technical options, make sound architectural decisions and consider long-term maintainability.
• Cloud and DevOps experience – practical experience building and operating cloud-native applications, ideally within AWS, alongside an understanding of CI/CD, infrastructure as code and modern development practices. Experience with GitHub and Terraform would be advantageous.
• Integration and security – a solid understanding of API design, system integration patterns and security principles, with experience connecting services and third-party platforms.
• Technical leadership – experience guiding engineers, reviewing code, sharing best practices and raising engineering standards. You don't necessarily need to have held a formal Tech Lead title.
• Collaboration and delivery – the ability to work closely with Product Managers, engineers and wider stakeholders, translating business challenges into technical solutions and delivering value in an agile environment.

Experience with Amazon Connect or contact centre technology would be a bonus, but it's not essential. We're open to engineers from different industries who bring strong engineering fundamentals, architectural thinking and a passion for building great products.

We might not be right for you if:
• You only want to focus on your to-do list; we’re a small, high-performing team, we help each other to succeed.
• You value perfection over fast iteration and progress; IAG Loyalty moves fast, we learn and iterate as we go; our environment isn’t right for everyone.
• You’re looking to create but not build; this is an end-to-end role, you need to be comfortable owning your space, from ideation through to delivery and review.

If you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please do still apply. We'd love to chat and see if you could be a great fit.

The Blend 📍
This role will work as part of our Loyalty Division and is based out of our London office. We call our approach to hybrid working The Blend — it’s about giving you the flexibility to choose where you do your best work, while staying connected with your team and the wider business. This means you will be required to spend at least two days per week in the office, with the rest of the time working from home. You may also be required to work from one of our other office or partner locations, based on your role and 'to do' list

Diversity and Inclusion 

Our vision is to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences. Delivering that requires diverse thinking and inclusive leadership.

We are committed to building a workplace where people feel they belong and are valued for their perspective. Inclusion drives better decisions, stronger performance and more innovative outcomes.

We actively encourage applications from people with different experiences and backgrounds, and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is fair, inclusive and accessible.

Job Title
Senior Software Engineer - (Java/AI) Brokerage Services
Job Description
So, who are we? 
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses. 

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next. 

Join us at IG – the future gets built here. 

Your team
We’re looking for a Senior Engineer to join our Brokerage Services team to push hard on AI across Brokerage Services engineering: AI-assisted coding, testing and deployments, shift left on security, defect triage and observability, and the internal tooling that connects our AI tools safely to Jira, GitLab, and our CI/CD pipeline. This is a hands-on role. You’ll build tooling yourself, and you’ll help set how your team adopts it.

Your role in the Team’s Success
This role suits engineers with a strong grounding in software engineering practice: test-driven development, pair programming, and real ownership of systems from design through to production support, with real depth in Java or a comparable backend service ecosystem. The fundamentals matter most: engineers who can write their own tests, review their own designs, and catch their own defects, and who use AI to extend that practice further and faster. Growing into the person the whole group comes to for technical judgement is part of the role.

Our ambition: engineering that runs itself
The long-term goal is a pipeline where AI agents handle the bulk of coding support, testing, and triage end-to-end, largely unattended, with engineers stepping in for genuine judgement calls and exceptions. We’re early on that path today, and we want someone in this role who treats the destination as real and pushes their team toward it deliberately.

What you’ll do 
• Build and maintain internal tooling that embeds AI into day-to-day engineering work: coding assistants, AI-assisted test generation, deployments, and defect triage.
• Contribute to observability in the AI-assisted pipeline, so every stage shows what the tooling is doing, catching, and missing.
• Identify manual steps in coding, testing, and release that can run largely unattended, and help build the automation to get there.
• Split work into small, releasable pieces that ship continuously.
• Work closely with a product person on your product domain, so what you build is grounded in real delivery.
• Treat improving ways of working and driving AI adoption as a fundamental, ongoing part of delivering value.
• Work with the test and PM function to bring AI into the testing pipeline: exploratory test generation, defect clustering, flaky-test detection, and smarter prioritisation of what to test.
• Evaluate and help roll out LLM-based developer tools, for example Claude Code and similar, integrating them safely with our Jira, Confluence, and GitLab environments.
• Follow and help refine standards for responsible AI use in the SDLC: data handling, prompt hygiene, and guardrails around production and customer data.
• Mentor less experienced engineers on effective use of AI tooling.
• Work with security and compliance to make sure AI tooling meets IG’s regulatory and data-handling requirements.
• Track the metrics that show whether AI tooling is helping: cycle time, defect escape rate, test coverage, delivery turnaround. Iterate based on what the data shows.

What you’ll need for this role 
• Extensive background as a Software Engineer, with demonstrated technical judgement on production systems.
• Solid, hands-on expertise in Java or a comparable backend service ecosystem.
• Strong fluency in test-driven development and pair programming as working disciplines.
• Real ownership experience: you’ve designed features or systems, built them, deployed them, and supported them in production.
• A genuine appetite for aggressive automation. You get energised by removing manual steps entirely.
• Some experience evaluating or using LLM-based developer tools in a real engineering environment.

Preferred
• Experience with MCP, agentic tooling, or Spec Driven Development.
• Familiarity with the Atlassian ecosystem (Jira, Confluence) and its APIs.
• Prior experience in financial services, trading platforms, or another regulated, high-reliability environment.

The Perks 
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.

job_description:
**This role is based within the UK only and you need to have the Right To Work without Sponsorship to be considered**



A platform you can believe in: Immersive One is the leading cyber resilience solution across the globe.

Build and scale a best in class platform alongside a team of the brightest minds in cybersecurity! At Immersive, we’re uniquely positioned to future-proof organizations against any cyber challenge. If that excites you, read on!


Immersive is the cyber proving ground for the AI enterprise. Through Immersive One, organizations can test whether people, AI-enabled workflows, cyber security teams, agents, and leaders can perform securely under realistic pressure, then turn that performance into evidence they can use to improve, benchmark, and report readiness.

Trusted by 30%+ of the Fortune 100 and ranked #1 in the Forrester Wave™ 2026, Immersive helps organizations prove AI can be adopted safely, teams can develop and defend at AI speed, leaders can lead through crisis, and AI agents can be validated before they are trusted in live workflows

https://www.immersivelabs.com/why-immersive-labs

We help the world’s biggest brands like Citi, Pfizer, Humana, and HSBC, protect their revenues and brand reputations.

Immersive was founded in 2017, from a cargo container in Bristol, UK we’ve grown to over 300 employees globally, announced funding of more than $180 million and been voted a Best place to work on multiple occasions!

https://www.immersivelabs.com/company/our-story



Lead Product Designer -Platform Experience - UK (Remote)

We’re looking for experienced, customer-centric and data-driven individuals to join our Product team as a Lead Product Designer - Platform Experiences based out of the UK.

You will help shape a connected, intuitive platform that simplifies complex workflows and makes insights more actionable. This is an ideal role for someone who loves information architecture, systems thinking and creating seamless experiences across products.

Beyond the product, you'll help shape how we work as a design team, raising the quality of our thinking, craft and collaboration.

As an advocate for Product Design excellence within Immersive, you will shape the next generation of AI-powered and agentic experiences within our enterprise cybersecurity platform, Immersive One. You'll help design intelligent, trustworthy workflows that bring together human expertise, AI-assisted decision-making, and increasingly autonomous capabilities.


Reporting to the Director of Product Design, you’ll own product problems from early discovery and definition through to validation, detailed design, delivery and iteration. You’ll work closely with Product and Engineering, using research, data and strong product judgement to shape experiences that work for customers and the wider platform.


This is a role for someone who thinks beyond individual screens — considering end-to-end journeys, information architecture, workflows, reusable patterns and how decisions scale across a complex B2B product.


You will be instrumental in shaping the future of our products, designing flexible, intelligent frameworks rooted in object-oriented thinking and guided by customer and user feedback and research. Your product output will drive measurable business outcomes that shape the evolution of our design system to define how cyber resilience comes to life across the Immersive One platform.


Our most successful product designers here bring a potent mix of strategic vision, user empathy, and analytical rigor to their work, while constantly expanding their knowledge through cross-team collaboration. You are the sparring partner for the Product Managers and Engineering teams with a close eye for scalability and commerciality - a true consultant who brings both research and evidence to the table and is able to articulate the ‘Why’ to validate design decisions through experimentation, metrics, and real-world usage.



As the most senior individual contributor in the team, your main responsibilities will include:

 - Lead the design of thoughtful, high-quality and scalable product experiences, from defining the right approach through prototyping, validation and detailed design execution.

 - Pioneer the integration of intelligent automation and generative AI into user flows to dramatically boost efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making speed.

 - Transform complex, technical cybersecurity data into clear, intuitive user interfaces that facilitate effective investigation, analysis, and response.

 - Partner closely with research teams to synthesize qualitative and quantitative insights, grounding all design decisions in solid data.

 - Champion Object-Oriented UX (OOUX) to create reusable components and streamlined workflows aligned with core platform entities.

 - Govern the evolution of our design system to guarantee cross-product consistency, accessibility, and intelligent adaptability.

 - Leverage customer insights, behavioural analytics and success metrics to inform product priorities, guide design decisions and measure the real-world impact of our solutions.

 - Collaborate with engineering partners to ensure the thoughtful, consistent, and scalable implementation of all product features.

Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas, but don’t worry if you don’t hit each one exactly:

 - Extensive experience in product or UX design, particularly within complex SaaS enterprise, data-driven, and platform environments. Ideally, you have worked on AI-powered features, intelligent automation, agentic workflows, or AI-native products

 - Demonstrated track record designing for complex enterprise UX – ideally B2B SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools, infrastructure, or technical platforms.

 - Experience shaping design direction across complex products, making informed design decisions, bringing others along and remaining hands-on in execution.

 - Exceptional collaboration skills to strategically partner with product, engineering, and research to align design outcomes with core business and user objectives.

 - Expertise in systems thinking, sophisticated interaction design, and establishing robust, data-connected workflows.

 - Comfortable using emerging AI tools and rapidly testing ideas with Product and Engineering.

 - Familiarity with or a strong interest in Object-Oriented UX (OOUX), advanced information architecture, and data modeling principles.

 - Ability to define, track, and analyze success metrics to measure the tangible impact and effectiveness of design solutions.

 - Excellent communication, presentation, and storytelling skills, with a proven ability to influence and align diverse, senior-level stakeholders
   
   
   
   We are looking for our Product Designer to be based in the UK, and we offer both remote and hybrid working options.

Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role:

 - Driven - We push the boundaries of innovation, acting swiftly to achieve ambitious outcomes. Our drive embodies a culture of ambition, where challenges are stepping stones to excellence.

 - Inclusive - Our strength lies in diversity, fostering a culture where every individual contributes to our collective strength. We champion open dialogue and empathy, ensuring a collaborative, inclusive workplace.

 - Customer Centric - We seek to develop deep relationships with our customers to help them achieve their business outcomes. We exceed our customers and partners' expectations by crafting products, services and experiences that surprise, delight and ensure they feel valued and supported every day.

 - One Team - We are a talented global team working together to achieve our vision. Central to our ethos, resilience means adapting and thriving in adversity. It guides our innovation, ensuring we and our clients are prepared for the future.

We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work.

Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application!


As well as an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you. We offer an extensive range of benefits so you can do your very best work:

 - Time off, flexible and remote working so you can work when is best for you, includes 25 days annual leave + 2 volunteering days and birthday day off

 - Look after your family and yourself with enhanced parental leave, mindfulness groups, critical illness cover,

 - Career and learning development through the platform and our ‘Learn Anything’ fund

 - Share in the companies success with share options, sales incentives and Recognition & Rewards for doing great work and living our values and behaviours

 - Informal or formal flexible working options, e.g. flexible start and finish times, reduced hours, job share, remote working

 - We’re a sociable, tight-knit team with monthly socials, and sports clubs. Our socials have included everything from pottery painting and paper mask making, to movie nights and escape rooms

 - While this is a remote position, we do all meet in our EMEA HQ on a bi annual basis and regularly in person in region.

Find out more about life at Immersive Labs https://careers.immersivelabs.com https://careers.immersivelabs.com


Cyber threats wait for no one and neither should you. Apply now!


If you would like to read more about what you can expect from our recruitment process, you can visit our dedicated interview process https://www.immersivelabs.com/company/careers page.

Who we are 
Isla Health is a venture-backed health-tech scale-up, supporting partners across the UK, EU and internationally. We’ve built a new category of healthcare technology which we refer to as the Digital Pathway Platform (DPP). Founded in 2019, we now support 25% of NHS Trusts and see 2 million submissions on the platform every year.
As a company, we’re laser focused on enabling a scalable model of care which empowers healthcare staff and improves patient outcomes. The DPP supports this by setting up digital pathways which are remote-first and asynchronous. As pathways harness sophisticated automation, clinical algorithms and intelligent cohorting, patients always take the optimised route through their pathway, thereby delivering a step change in clinical productivity.

The role
We're looking for an Analytics Engineer to take ownership of how we structure, manage and use data across Isla.
As our platform scales, we have a huge opportunity to use our data to demonstrate clinical impact, improve our product and help teams make faster decisions. You'll be responsible for building the foundations that make this possible.
You'll own our BigQuery warehouse end to end: how it's modelled, what it costs and how Delivery and Product teams use it. You'll work out how our data should be structured to measure Isla's company metrics, and you'll do analysis yourself when it's needed. You'll report to the Director of Product and work closely with Engineering on how data is captured at source and on infrastructure decisions. This is a role for someone who cares as much about what a metric means as how it's built.

What you’ll do
• Make impact measurable. Work with Product and Engineering teams to identify what data needs to be captured and how it should be structured to reliably measure Isla's impact, including waiting-list reductions, referral-to-treatment (RTT) performance, clinical efficiency and patient outcomes.
• Own our data model. Design and maintain how data is structured in BigQuery, from raw sources to clean, documented, trusted tables. Set consistent definitions so everyone gets the same answer to the same question.
• Own BigQuery costs. Monitor, forecast and reduce spend, and set the practices that keep it under control as we grow.
• Serve Delivery and Product. Build the datasets and dashboards teams use for BI, client reporting and product insight, and help them self-serve safely.
• Advise on new projects. Shape how data is designed into new features and pathways from the start, so we can measure them from day one.
• Support analysis. Answer product and client questions with data, from feature adoption to pathway outcomes.
• Keep data safe. Apply access controls, quality checks and documentation suited to sensitive healthcare data.
Tech stack
Isla's DPP is built using modern cloud technologies, including Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Firebase, Node.js and TypeScript. We currently use BigQuery for analytics and reporting.
We're open-minded about how our data stack should evolve and are looking for someone with the experience and technical judgement to help us make the right decisions.
We also lean heavily into AI, and you'll be encouraged to explore tools that improve your own productivity and help us build smarter, more efficient workflows.
Requirements
We're looking for someone with 4+ years experience in analytics engineering, BI or data roles where you've owned how data is modelled, not just queried it. You can move between a product conversation about what to measure and the SQL that measures it.
• Strong SQL: complex queries, window functions, and investigating messy data to find out what's really going on.
• Data modelling: you've designed analytical layers (e.g. dimensional or layered staging-to-mart models) and can explain the trade-offs.
• Metric design: you can turn a business question into a precise definition, and spot where the data can't support it yet.
• Cloud warehouses: hands-on with BigQuery or a similar platform (Snowflake, Redshift), including managing cost and performance.
• Communication: you can explain data limits and trade-offs to product managers, delivery teams and clients without jargon.
• Ownership: you'll find what needs fixing and drive it without detailed direction.
Desirable experience
• Experience building or maintaining ELT pipelines; Python for data work
• Experience working in a startup or scale-up where you've built or significantly improved data infrastructure.
• Familiarity with version control, CI/CD, automated testing and infrastructure-as-code.
• Experience working with Firebase, Firestore or other NoSQL databases.
• Experience supporting customer-facing analytics products alongside internal reporting.
• Exposure to healthcare data, sensitive information or regulated environments.
• Experience with data governance, access controls and security practices.

The AI Engineer designs, builds and operates scalable, secure AI solutions for JCDecaux UK, with a focus on Copilot implementations and agentic AI that augment users and automate complex workflows. The Account Planner turns commercial commitments into technically deliverable campaigns. The role combines campaign planning, trading, technical troubleshooting and client communication, with training and support as you build your skills.
This is an entry-level opportunity to learn how programmatic advertising campaigns are planned, launched and managed across our digital advertising screens. Programmatic advertising uses technology to buy and deliver advertising. You’ll support the team in turning client briefs and commercial commitments into campaigns, building your skills through training, guidance and hands-on experience. You do not necessarily need previous programmatic experience, or knowledge of our digital estate before joining.

Your work will help campaigns launch smoothly, deliver against client commitments and support revenue and a positive client experience. Accuracy matters, and you’ll learn how to use checking processes, spot potential issues and ask for support. As your knowledge develops, you’ll take on more responsibility for planning, campaign delivery and problem-solving.

What you'll be doing...
Contributions
• Campaign planning and activation: support campaign planning and set-up, learning about our screens, formats, locations, availability and delivery rules. Use this knowledge, with guidance, to help check that proposed campaigns can be delivered.
• Audience recommendations: help interpret client briefs and explore audience information using our data management platform. Learn to assess whether audience groups are relevant and large enough for a campaign, and support targeting recommendations.
• Creative checks and approvals: learn our digital artwork specifications, brand requirements and approval processes. Check campaign assets against these guidelines and work with colleagues to resolve issues.
• Troubleshooting and testing: support the investigation of campaign delivery issues by checking information, following agreed processes and involving colleagues when needed. Through training, learn how platform settings, bidding activity, competition and creative requirements affect delivery, and help test dynamic creative optimisation, which adapts advertising content using data.
• Data and insight: help organise and check campaign data, identify patterns or unexpected results, and explain what they could mean for campaign delivery. With guidance, recommend practical next steps. Develop your Excel and analytical skills as you work with larger datasets.
• Client and colleague communication: learn to provide clear campaign updates, explain issues and next steps, and keep clients and colleagues informed, with support from the team.
• Programmatic activation: setting up, optimising and evaluating programmatic campaigns that we run in-house using a DSP (Demand Side Platform)

What You’ll Learn
Through training and hands-on experience, you’ll learn about our digital estate and delivery rules; the platforms used to buy, sell and deliver advertising and manage audience data and workflows; audience selection; creative specifications and approvals; and campaign troubleshooting. You’ll learn how our advertising platforms connect, how information moves between them and how changes in one system can affect campaign delivery. You’ll also build your understanding of pricing, deal structures, sales policies, revenue risk and partner commitments, including pricing by time of day, barter arrangements and managed services.
A little bit about you...
Skills You’ll Bring
• Willingness to learn: an interest in learning new tools and processes, asking questions and applying feedback. Previous experience with advertising platforms is not required.
• Learning and applying information: the ability to build knowledge over time and use guidance when completing tasks. You’ll learn about our digital estate on the job.
• Commercial curiosity: an interest in how advertising supports clients’ objectives and how accurate campaign delivery contributes to the business.
• Analytical thinking: an interest in using information to answer questions, compare options and explain your reasoning.
• Attention to detail: care when checking information and following guidelines, using agreed checks to identify and correct mistakes.
• Problem-solving: a logical approach to checking what has happened, gathering information and asking for help when needed.
• Organisation: the ability to keep track of tasks, work towards agreed deadlines and flag when changing priorities or workloads need support.
• Clear communication: the ability to share information clearly, listen, ask questions and keep colleagues updated.
• Working with numbers: willingness to work with numerical information and check accuracy. Basic to intermediate Excel skills, including entering, sorting and checking data, to develop formulas, charts and pivot tables.

Qualifications and Experience
No previous media or programmatic advertising experience is required. We’re looking for the skills and willingness to learn described above, rather than prior knowledge of our industry, systems or products.

We're looking for a BIM Coordinator to join our KierBAM team based in Plymouth – Devonport Royal Dockyard.

Location: Plymouth – Devonport Royal Dockyard
Hours: 42.5 hours per week

We are unable to offer certificates of sponsorship to any candidates in this role.

KierBAM is a Joint Venture partnership between Kier and Bam Nuttall, currently delivering an exciting redevelopment project at a Royal Navy site in Plymouth. We're seeking a talented and detail-oriented BIM Coordinator to coordinate, manage and assure project information and model-based deliverables to support safe, efficient and compliant project delivery. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a dynamic team environment whilst supporting multidisciplinary teams and implementing information management processes.

What will you be responsible for?

As a BIM Coordinator, you'll be working within the KierBAM team, supporting them in delivering digital construction and information management excellence. Your day to day will include:

- Working collaboratively with project teams and stakeholders to support the successful delivery of BIM and information management requirements across the project
- Supporting compliance with project BIM standards, information management processes and ISO 19650 requirements
- Coordinating, reviewing and maintaining project information models, supporting multidisciplinary coordination and information exchange activities
- Undertaking information quality assurance activities to verify that graphical and non-graphical information meets project requirements
- Providing training, guidance and technical support in BIM, digital construction and information management practices to project teams and supply chain partners

What are we looking for?

This role of BIM Coordinator is great for you if:

- You hold a CSCS Card – White/Yellow
- You have demonstrable experience in digital construction and information management, including BIM coordination and model federation
- You have a working knowledge of ISO 19650 information management principles and can interpret key information management documents
- You're proficient in the Autodesk suite, including Revit, Navisworks, and AutoCAD
- You're a strong collaborator with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, able to work effectively within a multidisciplinary and diverse team

job_title: Head of Financial Planning and Analysis
job_description:
At Kroo Bank, we’re building a better bank from the ground up. One that puts customers first, treats money responsibly, and uses technology to make everyday banking simpler, fairer and more transparent. We’re a fully regulated UK bank, backed by long-term investors, with a growing customer base and big ambitions. We move fast, think carefully, and hold ourselves to high standards, whether that’s how we build products, manage risk, or look after our people.

How you will contribute:
As a Head of Financial Planning and Analysis, your key responsibility will be to lead Kroo Bank’s forecasting, planning, and performance insight across the business, helping to shape strategic decisions through high quality models, robust analysis, and clear storytelling. This role is hands-on and execution focused, requiring you to build and run your own financial models and planning tools, often from scratch, in a fast growing challenger bank environment. You will partner closely with senior stakeholders across Finance, Risk, Product, and Operations to develop scalable forecasting and budgeting capabilities, while ensuring alignment with banking specific drivers including balance sheet dynamics, capital, liquidity, and regulatory expectations. Other responsibilities include:

- Build, own, and continuously improve end to end financial models covering P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow, ensuring they are transparent, well controlled, and scalable.
- Lead the Bank’s forecasting and planning cycles including annual budget, reforecasting, and multi year planning, producing clear outputs and variance explanations.
- Develop driver based forecasting frameworks for key banking metrics including net interest income, cost of funds, credit performance, operating costs, and customer growth.
- Produce high quality management information and performance insight for senior leadership, including commentary on key movements, risks, and actions.
- Partner with Treasury and Risk stakeholders to ensure planning reflects balance sheet composition, interest rate dynamics, and capital and liquidity considerations.
- Build and maintain planning tools in Excel and Google Sheets, improving automation and control through advanced formula design, VBA where appropriate, and structured model governance.
- Use data and scripting tools such as Python to automate repeatable analysis, improve data quality, and accelerate forecasting and reporting processes.
- Support the development of capital and regulatory aware planning, ensuring assumptions and outputs are consistent with the Bank’s prudential framework and internal risk appetite.
- Work with business owners to challenge assumptions, embed accountability for budgets, and improve the quality of forecasting inputs across the organisation.
- Contribute to the build out of FP and A processes, templates, and controls suitable for a regulated challenger bank, including documentation and audit ready working practices.
- Support investor, Board, and committee reporting requirements through high quality packs, scenario analysis, and sensitivity modelling.

Required skills:

- Ability to build, run, and maintain end to end financial models independently, with strong structure, controls, and transparency.
- Ability to deliver accurate forecasting, budgeting, reforecasting, and multi year planning in a banking environment using driver based methodologies.
- Ability to demonstrate advanced Excel capability and strong proficiency in Google Sheets, including complex modelling, scenario analysis, and robust model control.
- Ability to improve efficiency through automation, including VBA and repeatable tooling and templates.
- Ability to use Python to automate analysis, improve data integrity, and build scalable forecasting and reporting workflows.
- Ability to demonstrate strong understanding of banking financial drivers including P&L, balance sheet, net interest income, cost of funds, and operating cost levers.
- Strong knowledge of capital and other prudential concepts and their impact on planning and decision making and the ability to model accordingly.
- Ability to work effectively in a challenger bank or high growth environment, showing initiative and ownership and being comfortable building processes from scratch.
- Ability to partner with senior stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively, and drive accountability for inputs and outcomes.
- Ability to communicate complex analysis clearly, producing concise performance insight and recommendations for senior leadership and governance forums.

Required qualifications:

- Degree level education or equivalent practical experience in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics, Data Analytics, or a related discipline.
- Professional accounting qualification is required, for example CIMA, ACA or ACCA.
- Evidence of ongoing professional development in financial modelling, forecasting, planning, data analytics, banking capital, or prudential regulation.
- Previous experience in a challenger bank, fintech, or high growth financial services environment where building from scratch is required is highly desirable.

What we offer:

At our cutting-edge fintech company, we know that attracting and retaining the best talent means offering top-notch benefits that help our employees thrive both in and outside of work. Check out what we currently offer:

- Generous holiday time: 25 days annual leave, 8 bank holidays, 1 Kroo bank holiday (June 24th), and 1 day off during the week of your birthday.
- Personal days: We know that life can be unpredictable, so we offer 3 personal days to use as needed.
- Employer-sponsored volunteer program: We're passionate about giving back to our community, and we support our employees in doing the same with up to 4 hours per month of employer-sponsored volunteer time.
- Mental health support: We care about the mental health of our team members and offer access to Spill, our mental health support partner.
- Workplace pension: We want you to feel secure about your future, so we offer a workplace pension with a 5% employee contribution and a 3% employer top-up.
- Top-notch equipment: We provide top-of-the-line equipment necessary for smooth hybrid work, including a MacBook laptop. Additionally, we also offer support in establishing your home office by contributing towards your setup if required.
- Modern office: When you're in the office, you'll enjoy access to our modern, bustling workspace in Farringdon (Central London).
- Cycle to Work scheme: We encourage sustainable transportation with our Cycle to Work scheme.
- Electric Car scheme: We're committed to reducing our carbon footprint, and our Electric Car scheme makes it easy for our employees to do the same.
- Enhanced parental leave: We know that family comes first, and we offer an enhanced parental leave policy to support our employees in starting and growing their families.
- Room for growth: As a fast-paced, high-growth start-up, we're dedicated to providing our employees with room to grow and excel.
- You get full healthcare for you and your nuclear family via Vitality.

Hybrid Working:

At Kroo Bank, we have a hybrid policy that gives both individuals and teams a lot of freedom when it comes to using the office space to boost productivity. Our London office is a great resource when used effectively. So, employees who can occasionally come to the office are a good fit for how we work right now. Keep in mind that this job involves working from Monday to Friday, with a mix of remote and office work, so you won't need to be on-site all the time.

Apply systems engineering across the ESCS lifecycle, translating business and operational needs into coherent, traceable system requirements, interface specifications and model artefacts. The Systems Engineer will support the definition, analysis, integration and verification of ESCS capabilities, working across architecture, software, data, cloud, test and supplier teams to maintain the technical integrity of the end-to-end solution.

The role you will play

Develop and maintain clear, testable and traceable system requirements, interfaces and engineering artefacts.
Model and analyse the behaviour, interfaces and non-functional characteristics of the ESCS solution to support evidence-based engineering decisions.
Support system integration and verification by ensuring requirements, interfaces, dependencies and acceptance evidence remain coherent throughout delivery.

What will I be doing?

Elicit, analyse, decompose and manage functional and non-functional system requirements, maintaining traceability through design, integration, verification and acceptance.
Develop and maintain system models, functional and logical views, interface definitions and Interface Control Documents (ICDs).
Analyse end-to-end system interactions, data flows, dependencies, constraints and behaviours across ESCS capabilities and external systems.
Undertake system-level analysis and modelling of non-functional characteristics, including availability, reliability, performance, capacity, resilience and recoverability.
Work with architects, software, data, cloud, security, test and supplier teams to ensure designs and implementations remain aligned with system requirements and defined interfaces.
Support verification and validation activities, including definition of acceptance criteria against requirements and requirements-to-verification traceability, and verification through the means of analysis and inspection techniques.
Identify, analyse and manage technical risks, assumptions, dependencies, issues and opportunities within assigned areas.
Contribute engineering evidence to technical reviews, design reviews, integration readiness and capability acceptance.
Maintain systems engineering artefacts under appropriate configuration and change control.

Required skills and capabilities

Systems engineering across the engineering lifecycle
Requirements engineering, decomposition and traceability for both functional and non-functional domains
System architecture and functional analysis
Interface definition and production of interfaces specifications (Interface Control Documents)
System modelling and Model-Based Systems Engineering principles
Functional and non-functional requirements analysis
Availability, reliability, performance and capacity analysis
Application and planning of verification and validation methods for requirements
Technical risk, assumption and dependency management
Strong use of engineering best practice, including engineering methodologies, expert configuration and change control and secure systems engineering principles.
Clear and proficient written and verbal communication


Required experience
Systems engineering experience on complex, software-oriented systems self-hosted within public and private cloud platforms.
Experience developing and managing system requirements in line with INCOSE best practice and maintaining traceability to design and verification compliance evidence throughout the engineering lifecycle.
Experience defining interfaces between systems, applications or services and producing associated interface documentation.
Experience applying modelling or analytical techniques to understand system behaviour, dependencies or non-functional characteristics.
Experience supporting system integration, verification and technical assurance in a multidisciplinary engineering environment.
Ability to work independently within an assigned engineering scope and collaborate effectively with architects, software engineers, test engineers, suppliers and other engineering disciplines.


Desired experience
Solutions hosted across hyperscaler platforms; preferably AWS.
Complex systems integration programmes that include enterprise SaaS and Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) systems.
Supply chain, procurement, order management, logistics or ERP-related systems.
Model-Based Systems Engineering and appropriate modelling notation/tooling, such as SysML 1.6, SysML 2.0 or Archimate.
·Availability, reliability, capacity or performance modelling of distributed systems.
Experience working within multidiscipline agile or hybrid engineering delivery environments.
Public sector, defence or security-conscious environments.
INCOSE ASEP/CSEP, Chartered Engineer or equivalent professional development towards recognised systems engineering accreditation.
Previous experience with business process modelling using BPMN 2.0.


Success in the role
System requirements are clear, consistent, testable and traceable through design, integration and verification.
Interfaces and dependencies are defined sufficiently early and clearly to support implementation and integration.
System models and analyses provide useful evidence for engineering and architectural decisions.
Non-functional requirements and system-level constraints are understood and reflected in the solution.
Integration and verification activities have a clear requirements, interface and acceptance basis.
Engineering risks, assumptions and inconsistencies are identified early and resolved collaboratively.
Systems engineering artefacts remain coherent, controlled and appropriate for technical assurance and acceptance.
Accurate and transparent reporting of progress, successes and impediments within designated team.

Our mobile app, Zable, is how most of our customers experience all of our products in one centralised space. It's written in React Native and TypeScript with a Kotlin backend, shipped to iOS and Android from a single codebase. We are now looking to level up the quality engineering so that we can raise release cadence without losing sleep over regressions.

This is an automation-first role. You'll spend most of your time writing code - test frameworks, CI tooling, helpers, rather than executing test scripts by hand. You'll work alongside software engineers, product, and design, setting direction.

You'll also be working at the frontier of AI-assisted quality, using LLMs and AI tooling to speed up test authoring, triage failures, and surface coverage gaps, while applying the engineering judgement to keep tests trustworthy.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Own the mobile test strategy:

 - Define and evolve a pragmatic test pyramid for React Native - deciding where E2E is worth the weight and where logic belongs in faster layers (Jest, React Testing Library, component tests).

 - Make deliberate calls about coverage, reliability, and speed trade-offs across the app.

 - Set the bar for what "ready to ship" looks like on mobile, and hold the line on it.
   
   

Build reliable E2E automation:

 - Create and maintain mobile E2E suites in Maestro, including the scaffolding around them - test data, device configuration, helpers, reporting.

 - Integrate suites into CI (GitHub Actions) so engineers get fast, trustworthy feedback on every PR and release candidates carry a signal people actually believe.

 - Drive flakiness down and time-to-diagnosis down. We treat a flaky test the same way we treat a broken test, and we expect root-cause work rather than retry-until-green.
   
   

Bring AI into the SDLC:

 - Use AI tools day-to-day to accelerate test authoring, cluster failures, surface coverage insights, and propose fixes.

 - Decide where AI adds leverage and where a human eye is needed. A suite that looks comprehensive but isn't trustworthy is worse than a smaller one we rely on.

 - Help shape how the mobile team uses AI-assisted workflows more broadly - prompts, guardrails, review patterns.
   
   

Prevent defects, not just catch them:

 - Partner with product and engineering on shift-left quality: join specs early, push back on ambiguous acceptance criteria, and surface risk before code is written.

 - Close the loop on production issues using our observability stack (Datadog, Sentry, Grafana) - tying test coverage back to real customer impact.

 - Run targeted exploratory testing on high-risk releases when it's the right call.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Essential:

 - Hands-on experience with Maestro or Detox.

 - 2-3+ years in quality engineering or test automation, with a track record of keeping automated suites stable rather than letting them rot into a graveyard of quarantined tests.

 - Experience introducing AI-assisted testing practices (test generation, failure clustering, coverage analytics) with sensible controls around review and trust.

 - Strong TypeScript and JavaScript - not just writing test scripts, but building helpers, tooling, and debugging into the app when needed.

 - Experience shaping CI/CD pipelines for test reliability (GitHub Actions or similar), including flakiness reduction, parallelisation, artefact management, and runtime control.

 - Comfortable with mobile E2E automation, or strong E2E experience on another platform plus a credible plan for getting productive on mobile quickly.

 - Able to operate independently and drive improvements end-to-end (frameworks, CI, test data, reporting).
   
   

Desirable:

 - Hands-on experience testing React Native apps.

 - Mobile performance and reliability work (crash reporting, startup time, memory and battery awareness).

 - API and contract testing experience, with a point of view on test data and environment strategy.

Mobile: TypeScript, React Native, Expo, EAS, GraphQL, Relay, Jest, React Testing Library, Maestro.

Backend: Kotlin, PHP 8 (Symfony), AWS, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes.

Tooling and observability: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, Confluence, Datadog, Sentry, Grafana.

Lenovo is seeking an experienced Senior Financial Regulatory Counsel to support and help shape its global asset finance and leasing platform within Lenovo Global Financial Services (LGFS). LGFS is a Lease Operations Team supporting Lenovo's Solutions and Services Group (SSG).

 * Provide senior-level strategic legal and regulatory advice across LGFS's global leasing and asset finance activities.

The Role
 A business spends serious money every month on digital marketing, and it brings in a strong return. But they're now asking whether it could do better. Thousands of customers move use their services each year, giving them loads of data points, the data exists but they need someone to drive the insights. we're helping them find an Insights Analyst who can help make sense of all the data.

Why this role is different
 You won't be joining a team of analysts or picking up someone else's reports. You'll be the first, with complete autonomy to shape the role as you see fit. You'll report directly to the CEO, and your findings will go straight to the people who make the decisions. If you show what insight can do, there's a clear path to growing into an Analytics & Insight Manager role and building a team around you.

The small in-house tech team (an Ops/Tech Director and two developers) will help you get the data you need. That means your time goes on finding out what the data means, not on writing queries all day. You'll also have access to AI tools, including OpenAI, and a leadership team that's open to new ways of working.

The questions you'll be answering
• Is the business getting the most from its marketing spend, and where could Google PPC and acquisition do better?
• What happens to customers once they start? Who stays on track, who falls behind, and why?
• Where do customers drop out of the journey, and is it because of what we said, or how and when we said it?
• What patterns show up across different customer demographics?
• How can the existing reports and dashboards be joined up into one clear picture?
• Where could processes, automation or AI make the biggest difference?

 What you'll bring
• At least 2 years in an insight-focused role, such as Commercial Analyst, Insights Analyst or BI Analyst
• Experience analysing customer behaviour, the customer journey, or marketing performance (Google PPC is a big plus)
• Experience with demographic analysis or customer segmentation
• Strong Excel skills, plus experience with Power BI or similar tools
• A habit of asking "why?" and the confidence to put that question to senior leaders
• The ability to turn analysis into a clear story and recommendations people can act on
• Experience in a regulated environment, such as financial services, fintech or gambling, which will help you settle in quickly
Pure SQL experience matters less here than commercial curiosity. They want someone who looks beyond the numbers.

The package
• £45,000 salary
• Monday to Friday, 9-5 (37.5 hours), with an hour of flexibility either side
• Hybrid working, 3 days in the office (once you've had time to get to know the business)
• 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays
• Company pension and an employee benefits scheme
• Free on-site parking (the office is best reached by car)

 If this of interest, submit your CV now to be considered. Or reach out for further information!

We're hiring a Founding BDR to build Lovable's business development motion from the ground up. The job is to find, qualify and open the right accounts using a mix of your own outreach and the automation and AI agents you build to run alongside it. You'll own a pipeline number, work closely with our Account Executives globally and build a lot of your own tooling on Lovable itself. WHY LOVABLE?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognised on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Evidence you can generate pipeline. That could be as a BDR or SDR, a founder, in sales or revenue ops, or by building something that found its own customers. We care about the outcome more than the job title, and we'll ask to see it.

 - You already use AI and automation tooling (LLMs, Clay, n8n or similar) to research, personalise and sequence outreach, and you have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

 - You'd rather automate a repetitive workflow than keep doing it by hand, and you can show us something you've built.

 - Comfortable running outbound into named accounts and getting past the first contact to the people who actually make the decision.

 - Disciplined about qualifying out. A fast, well-reasoned no is a win for the business, and you don't chase volume for its own sake.

 - Able to explain a technical product in business terms to both technical and commercial buyers.

 - You set your own priorities, manage your own pipeline and hold yourself to account.

 - You want to become an Account Executive and are prepared to earn it.

 - Fluent English. A second European language (German, French, Spanish, Italian) is useful.

 - Experience with Lovable, developer tools or a product-led growth motion is a strong plus.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and run outbound systems: signal-based targeting, AI-assisted research, personalised sequences and automated workflows. Measure what converts and improve it every week.

 - Build internal GTM tooling on Lovable, such as enrichment flows, qualification agents and meeting-prep automations. The tooling you build is what the team after you will run on.

 - Qualify inbound demand quickly and thoroughly, and convert the right leads into well-prepared first meetings for the AE team.

 - Multi-thread into target accounts to reach economic buyers and technical decision-makers, not just the first person who replied.

 - Own a pipeline number and report clearly on how much comes from your own outreach versus automation, so we can scale both.

 - Work with the Account Executives you support on account plans, meeting prep and keeping deals moving between touchpoints.

 - Qualify out early and clearly when an account isn't a fit, so the team's time goes where it will pay off.

 - Feed what you're hearing from the market back to Sales, Marketing and Product to sharpen messaging and positioning.
   
   


WHERE THIS ROLE GOES

This is a development role with a defined path to Account Executive. We expect the people who join as BDRs now to form our next AE team.

 - Structured coaching from day one: weekly call reviews with experienced AEs and your manager, and a curriculum that covers discovery, demo, commercial negotiation and deal management.

 - The expectation that you progress to running your own deals within 12 to 18 months, based on performance rather than tenure.

 - As the first BDR at Lovable, real influence over how the role, the playbook and the tooling are defined for everyone who follows.

Sustainability Risk Framework & Oversight

• Maintaining and improving LSEG's sustainability risk guidance, taxonomy and supporting methodologies.

• Reviewing risk assessments, controls, mitigation plans and reporting produced by the first line.
• Identifying common themes, interconnected risks and emerging concerns across divisions and functions.
• Supporting governance activities where sustainability risk input, review or approval is required.

Risk Appetite, Reporting & Insight

Strong communication skills will be important in helping senior leaders understand complex risk topics and make informed decisions.
Responsibilities include:
• Supporting the development of sustainability risk appetite measures, tolerances and key risk indicators.
• Monitoring risk exposures, highlighting significant issues and contributing to escalation activities where required.
• Producing reporting and analysis for management, governance forums and Board committees.

• Monitoring emerging trends, regulatory developments and external events.
• Assessing how these developments may affect the Group's risk profile.
• Contributing sustainability risk expertise to pivotal initiatives, acquisitions, new products and change programmes.
• Supporting scenario analysis and stress-testing activities.

• Partner with Group Sustainability, divisional risk teams and business stakeholders.

• Providing independent input into sustainability reporting and external disclosures.

You’ll own the quality of the Lyrebird platform, from the first commit to the release gate. This is a hands-on, code-first engineering role, not manual test scripting. You’ll also be the quality partner to our SRE function, giving them the health checks, synthetic monitors, load test results and post-deployment signals they need. When a release is ready to go, you’ll give a clear yes or no, backed by evidence.

The Role: Category Manager - HR, Recruitment & Contingent

Role Purpose
The Category Manager is the commercial owner of the HR, Recruitment and Contingent category and acts as an internal commercial consultant to the business. The postholder offers senior stakeholders three things: deep knowledge of the category and its supply market, strategic sourcing capability, and negotiation expertise. Using these, the postholder builds and owns the category strategy and savings plan, competes with vendors on commercial strategy, and influences how the business specifies and buys. Success is measured by realised cost reduction across the category and by the value the business places on Procurement’s advice.

Context
M&G Procurement is on a transformation journey, our objectives include: Identifying and delivering material, recurring cost reduction on M&G third-party spend; and materially improving how the business experiences Procurement, measured through an internal NPS. To achieve these objectives, Procurement is moving from a business unit aligned, generalist model to a category structure that operates as an internal commercial consultancy. The UK team offers the business deep category knowledge, strategic sourcing capability and negotiation expertise, so that M&G can compete with its vendors on commercial strategy.

Key Responsibilities

Category Strategy and Commercial Leadership
• Build, own and execute the category strategy for HR, Recruitment and Contingent, based on a detailed understanding of supply market structure, vendor commercial models, cost drivers and market trends. 
• Maintain living category plans covering market analysis, supply base segmentation, demand profiling, route to market and savings opportunities. 
• Develop commercial strategies for key vendors well ahead of renewal, so that M&G negotiates from a position of insight and has credible alternatives. 
• Lead high-value sourcing events and negotiations, including setting the negotiation strategy, BATNA and walk-away position, managing concessions and holding positions with incumbents. Manage senior supplier relationships under commercial pressure. 
• Design sourcing events and evaluation criteria, and decide how much process each event needs based on its value, risk and complexity. 
• Introduce competitive tension into renewals and new commitments, moving from single-source and incumbent renewal to structured market engagement, preferred supplier frameworks and normalised rate cards.

Savings and Value Delivery
• Build and own the category savings plan against an agreed share of the group cost reduction target, sizing and prioritising opportunities by value and deliverability. 
• Agree baselines and savings methodology with Finance before work starts, and follow savings through until they show in budgets and run rates. 
• Build total cost of ownership and should-cost models, model the budget impact of sourcing options and how savings will be recognised in each department’s P&L cost reports, and make sourcing recommendations on that basis. 
• Use price, volume and demand levers, including rate reduction, volume aggregation, supplier consolidation and specification change. 
• Challenge demand and specification using category and industry knowledge: question whether a requirement is needed at all, and at what volume, service level, specification and term; identify over-specification, duplicate purchasing and avoidable demand; and propose options such as a lower service tier, a shorter term or reuse of existing contracts, setting out the trade offs in commercial terms. 
• Report savings and cost avoidance separately and accurately, and maintain a forward pipeline that gives Finance and the business visibility of upcoming activity.

Internal Consultancy and Stakeholder Influence
• Act as a trusted commercial adviser to senior business owners across the HR, Recruitment and Contingent spend area, engaging early in their planning rather than at the point of purchase. 
• Influence stakeholder decisions on sourcing, demand and specification without formal authority, and present category insight, evaluation and commercial recommendations to governance forums. 
• Act as the Procurement relationship lead for nominated senior stakeholders where assigned, bringing in other category colleagues as their agenda requires. 
• Seek and act on stakeholder feedback, contributing to the improvement in how the business experiences Procurement.

Supplier Management
• Set the commercial direction for key suppliers in the category and lead the commercial input to vendor strategy. 
• Influence and partner with in-business vendor management and vendor performance teams so that supplier reviews, contract changes and renewals secure the strongest commercial outcome for M&G. 
• Find value in the existing supply base, including through rate review, supplier consolidation and contract optimisation.

Working with the M&G India Procurement Team
• Direct category execution work delivered by the India team, providing clear briefs, priorities and commercial context. 
• Review the quality of execution outputs and work with India leads to maintain a responsive, consistent service to the business.

Contract, Risk and Governance
• Shape commercial terms, including pricing mechanisms, indexation, service credits and exit provisions, working with Legal. 
• Apply third-party risk management, outsourcing and regulatory requirements as they apply to HR, Recruitment and Contingent, and identify regulatory risk such as material outsourcing. 
• Apply procurement standards and governance proportionately, and record activity in the system of record and eSourcing tooling.

Data, Digital and AI
• Use spend data, Power BI dashboards and AI tools to analyse trends and anomalies, identify future sourcing opportunities and present a clear commercial account of what the management information shows. 
• Question data rather than accept it at face value, and work with India colleagues to keep category data accurate.

People and Capability
• Coach and develop Category Specialists and India colleagues working in the category, reviewing their work and building category capability across the UK and India. 
• Plan how onshore and offshore capacity is used across the category, so that effort is directed at the highest value work. 
• Share category intelligence across the Procurement team and support cross-category opportunities.

Person Specification
Essential
• Substantial category management or strategic sourcing experience, with a track record of delivering measurable savings in a complex organisation. 
• Category knowledge and experience as set out in the Category Knowledge Requirements above. 
• Demonstrable experience of planning and leading negotiations on high-value contracts with major vendors, including setting negotiation strategy and BATNA. 
• Credibility with senior stakeholders, evidence of influencing business decisions without formal authority, and experience of presenting commercial recommendations to senior governance forums. 
• Strong commercial and financial judgement, including total cost of ownership and should-cost analysis, and the ability to explain budget and P&L impact to stakeholders. 
• Confident using spend data and management information to identify trends, anomalies and sourcing opportunities. 
• Able to work from the London or Kildean (Stirling) office for the majority of the working week.

Desirable 
• Experience in a regulated environment such as financial services or insurance. 
• Experience with eSourcing platforms such as Market Dojo, and with Power BI or similar analytical tools. 
• Experience directing offshore or nearshore teams as an extension of the UK operation. 
• CIPS or an equivalent professional qualification.

Working Pattern 
This role is based in London or Kildean (Stirling). The postholder is expected to work from their base office for the majority of the working week. Regular, in person contact with senior stakeholders is central to the role, because building trust and influencing business decisions depend on it.

## Job description

Made Tech helps UK government and public sector organisations build better digital services - and security is central to that mission. As a Lead Security Engineer in our Cyber practice, you'll be the most senior security engineering voice on client engagements, setting technical direction for how organisations design, build, and defend secure systems. You'll work across complex government programmes where the stakes are real: services that affect citizens, systems that hold sensitive data, and teams that need to move quickly without cutting corners.

This isn't a role where you sit at the edge of delivery reviewing outputs. You'll be embedded in multidisciplinary teams, shaping how security is engineered into everyday work - from threat modelling and architecture at design time to hardened, monitored systems in production. You'll build trusted relationships with client engineering leads, platform teams, and senior stakeholders, translating between deep technical decisions and the trade-offs senior leaders need to understand. You'll bring the judgement to know when a heavyweight security architecture is warranted and when a lighter-weight, faster-moving approach serves the engagement better. 

At Lead level, your impact extends beyond the immediate team. You'll establish security engineering standards and reference architectures across engagements, grow the technical capability of the people around you — colleagues and client engineers alike — and contribute to how Made Tech's Cyber practice develops as a community. If you'd rather build the paved road than police the off-road, who treat security as an engineering discipline rather than a compliance exercise, and who cares about leaving client teams genuinely stronger than you found them, this role is for you. 

## Key responsibilities

- **Own end-to-end technical security architecture across engagements.** Design secure-by-default reference architectures, set patterns for identity, network, and data protection, and maintain living technical standards — feeding directly into how teams build, not just how they're audited.
- **Lead vulnerability remediation as an engineering programme.** Define the prioritisation framework — drawing on EPSS, KEV, CVSS, and asset criticality — set remediation SLAs, own the risk-acceptance register, and drive fixes directly into delivery backlogs alongside product teams. Report programme KPIs (MTTR by severity, backlog age, coverage, recurrence rate) to senior stakeholders.
- **Drive security into the team's normal engineering rhythm.** Embed threat modelling, secure code review, SAST, SCA, dependency policy, and container scanning into design and delivery cycles — building the tooling and automation that make this the default, not a specialist handover at the end of a sprint.
- **Navigate UK government security standards with confidence — as an engineer, not a paperwork exercise.** Design systems and controls that satisfy the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework, GovAssure, Cyber Essentials, and HMG Security Policy Framework, applying them proportionately across engagements as guardrails that enable safe delivery, not barriers to it. Engage with government security communities and coordinate with departmental technical teams.
- **Communicate security risk in terms that drive engineering decisions.** Report system posture, remediation programme performance, and architectural risk to senior client stakeholders — tailoring the frame for the audience and structuring reports around the decisions the reader needs to make, not just the findings.
- **Set the standard for incident response and detection engineering.** Build and drive adoption of detection, alerting, and IR tooling across engagements, own the IR-to-vulnerability-management feedback loop, and coordinate cross-team exercises including known-exploited-vulnerability scramble drills.
- **Grow the people around you.** Mentor colleagues across the practice and at client organisations, pair on complex or unfamiliar engineering problems, and create structured development opportunities — including for client engineers who may not yet have strong security habits. 

- **Contribute to Made Tech's Cyber practice beyond delivery.** Shape practice standards, contribute to hiring and technical calibration, build and share expertise externally, and help grow a security engineering community that raises capability across the organisation.

## Skills, knowledge and expertise

**Essential**

- Deep hands-on experience designing and building secure cloud architectures (AWS, Azure, or GCP) at scale, including IAM, network segmentation, and data protection patterns.
- Proven track record embedding security tooling and automation into CI/CD pipelines and engineering workflows across multiple teams.
- Strong proficiency in at least one programming/scripting language, used to build production-grade security tooling (not just scripts).

**Desirable**

The following would strengthen your application. We don't expect every candidate to bring all of these.

**Certifications**

- OSCP, OSWE, or equivalent offensive security credential
- AWS/Azure/GCP security specialty certification
- CKS (Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist)

**Capabilities and experience**

- Experience establishing and operating vulnerability remediation programmes at organisational scale — including risk-based prioritisation using EPSS, KEV, and asset criticality, and driving fixes across multiple delivery teams.
- Evidence of designing systems that satisfy UK government security frameworks — GovAssure, CAF, Cyber Essentials, HMG Security Policy Framework — in a complex multi-supplier or multi-team environment, as an architect rather than an assessor.
- Experience conducting or coordinating technical security reviews and penetration testing in UK public sector contexts, including remediating findings and briefing senior technical stakeholders.
- Working knowledge of exposure management beyond CVE-only approaches — incorporating misconfiguration, identity exposure, and attack-path analysis using cloud-native tooling (AWS Inspector, GuardDuty, Security Hub, or equivalents).
- Experience securing software supply chains — SBOM generation, dependency provenance, artifact signing — and integrating this into build pipelines rather than a standalone assurance process.
- Experience building or shaping security engineering capability within a consultancy, programme delivery, or multi-client environment — including growing technical skills in colleagues and client teams.
- Evidence of acting as a trusted technical adviser to senior client stakeholders — anchoring recommendations on engineering outcomes, challenging briefs constructively, and making security value visible through what gets shipped.
- Experience setting team ways of working in iterative delivery environments — establishing retrospective cadences, collaborative problem-solving norms, and pairing practices that spread security knowledge across the team.

**Tooling and practice familiarity**

- Deep familiarity with structured threat modelling approaches — STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, attack trees — and experience embedding these into agile delivery ceremonies.
- Experience integrating SAST, SCA, dependency scanning, and container security tooling into CI/CD pipelines as part of a shift-left security approach, including building custom tooling where off-the-shelf doesn't fit.

**About the role**

You will play a critical role in designing, implementing, and maintaining our clients’ cloud infrastructure, ensuring it is secure, scalable, and highly available. You will provide dedicated cloud and infrastructure expertise within your team and advise on best practice.

We expect our cloud engineers to have a background in and thorough understanding of software engineering. You will keep abreast of emerging technologies and be able to work collaboratively in a multi-disciplinary software delivery environment.

You will be expected to maintain a broad technical knowledge across all major cloud platforms and build credibility by pursuing relevant certifications.

## Key responsibilities

Delivery of high quality cloud-based technical solutions for our clients:

- Collaborate within cross-functional teams to design cloud architectures that meet the client’s requirements around scalability, performance, and security
- Deploy and manage cloud resources, containers, and related services using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform or CloudFormation
- Configure and maintain networking, security, and access control in the cloud environment
- Implement and maintain robust security practices to protect data and resources in the cloud environment
- Develop and maintain automated processes for provisioning, monitoring, and scaling cloud resources, including the use of CI/CD pipelines to streamline application deployments
- Monitor cloud infrastructure for performance bottlenecks and proactively optimise resource usage
- Implement load balancing, caching, and content delivery solutions to ensure high availability and performance
- Design and maintain backup and disaster recovery solutions to ensure business continuity in the event of system failures or data loss
