Senior Service Designers at Made Tech are expert practitioners who specialise in understanding, designing, and improving end-to-end public services. We are looking for an expert who can operate strategically and tactically across the full-service lifecycle, from initial policy intent to digital delivery and organisational change. Success in this role means using a systemic, Service Design approach to deliver positive, measurable outcomes for citizens and the public sector. 

Made Tech wants to positively impact the country's future by using technology to improve society. We believe a Service Design-led approach is crucial for creating positive outcomes in the public sector, ensuring critical service - enabled by technology - are cohesive, accessible, and efficient across all channels. You will be instrumental in maturing our community of designers and researchers to meet the growing demand for systemic, service-led delivery. 

### **About the role:**

- Senior Service Designers are expert Service Practitioners able to develop new and novel, service-centred approaches to highly complex challenges, based on fundamental design and public service principles.
- We expect the role holder to be a strategic thinker able to facilitate conversations with senior stakeholders to build understanding and alignment and help deliver intended outcomes and impact.
- Take the initiative and be fully responsible for defining the Service Design approach from first principles, proposing alternative ways to deliver complex service improvements.
- Define what ‘good’ end-to-end service design looks like on an engagement, enabling and holding cross-functional teams to account for producing high-quality service maps, blueprints, and deliverables, measuring the impact of your designs.
- Comfortable with owning a problem and committed to seeing the service improvement through to resolution. Actively look to deliver a positive service outcome,using data and research insights to influence wider organisational or policy change. 

### **Collaborative and Communicative**

- Growth Mindset: Always willing to learn and develop, bringing new approaches and thinking into our Service Design community.

## Key responsibilities

**Scope**

- Assure the successful design and delivery of public services by applying a holistic Service Design lens across technology, policy, process, and organisation.
- Build service design maturity, facilitating the design process, communicating complex service decisions to teams, and setting strategic expectations with senior stakeholders.
- Design, prototype and test seamless (online and offline) services, ensuring all organisational, service, and user outcomes are aligned.
- Championing the practice across Made Tech through CoP participation, development and delivery of training/briefings, providing coaching and mentoring support, etc
- Build trust with clients by demonstrating the value of a Service Design approach and understanding their strategic needs for service improvement.
- Support the commercial team to win new work by contributing strategic Service Design thinking and reviewing bids related to service transformation and user-centred design (UCD).
- Represent and advocate for user-centred Service Design publicly and internally through talks, blogs, and case studies, contributing to the definition of Made Tech's Service Design principles.
- Take an active role in the Service Design community, leading on developing and sharing good practice, and actively supporting the hiring and retention of expert Service Designers.

- An expert in using core Service Design tools, including but not limited to Service Blueprints, Ecosystem Maps, and Stakeholder Maps, as well as prototyping tools like Figma and the GOV.UK prototyping kit.
- Experience of championing the value and practice of Service Design internally and externally, influencing clients, partners, and peers on its contribution.
- Able to coach and mentor other designers, defining and setting the Service Design standards which others will apply across our engagements.
- Lead activities to map the existing service landscape, identify user and business needs, and create a shared, cross-organisational understanding of the problems to solve.

The role
The UK Media Ops team is being built at a critical point of transformation. The business needs clearer media operating standards, stronger operational discipline, better adoption of common processes and a practical way of turning governance into improved delivery across agencies and client teams.
Reporting to the Head of Operational Excellence, the Director of Media Excellence will lead the day-to-day media excellence agenda across UK Media Operations. The role is accountable for making best practice practical: translating operating standards into clear workflows, playbooks, training, adoption tracking and governance outputs that teams can use.
This role will manage the Operational Excellence Manager and provide leadership across process excellence, documentation, training, operational issue management, stakeholder engagement and continuous improvement. It will also work closely with Finance, Commercial, Activation, Analytics, agency operations and client teams to improve financial hygiene and reduce avoidable billing, debt and Mediaocean balance risks.
Key collaborators
• Head of Operational Excellence
• UK Head of Media Operations
• Media Operational Excellence Manager
• Business Operations Lead
• Central OM Operations Team
• Agency COOs, agency operations leads and client teams
• Discipline operational leads and discipline teams
• Finance, Commercial, Billing and Credit Control teams
• Activation, Investment, Analytics, Data and Technology teams
• EMEA Operations teams
• Omni, Mediaocean and other platform owners
• OGS/GCC and offshore/nearshore delivery teams
Vision
To build one joined-up discipline that works smarter, moves faster and delivers consistently high standards, giving teams and clients a better experience and the business a stronger platform for growth through automation, AI, data, operational discipline and clear governance.
Media Operations should be the operating backbone of the business: clearer standards, smarter workflows, stronger governance and better use of Omni, automation and AI to improve delivery at scale and remove friction across all agencies and disciplines.
Summary of the role
• Lead the Media Excellence agenda across UK Media Operations, ensuring standards, playbooks, training and governance are clearly defined, maintained and adopted.
• Manage the Media Operational Excellence Manager, setting priorities, expectations and development focus.
• Translate Media Operating Standards into practical ways of working across planning, activation, analytics, finance and delivery workflows.
• Own the structured approach to documentation, adoption, feedback, issue tracking and continuous improvement across priority media operations processes.
• Work with Finance, Commercial, Billing and agency/client teams to improve financial hygiene, reduce billing and debt queries, and keep Mediaocean balances at minimal risk to the business.
• Investigate recurring financial and billing issues, identify root causes and work with the right teams to prevent repeat problems.
• Support the Head of Operational Excellence in embedding UK governance, compliance, CLM/Operational Foundations, Omni-related process controls and agency adoption.
• Be the ultimate SME for financial systems, data and processes within Media Operations, setting strategic direction, owning complex diagnosis of root causes and working with stakeholders.
Responsibilities:
Media excellence, process and best practice
• Lead the creation, maintenance and continuous improvement of practical Media Operating Standards across priority workflows.
• Translate complex processes into clear playbooks, handoff guidance, process maps, decision frameworks and training materials.
• Ensure process guidance is simple enough to use, strong enough to manage risk and aligned to the wider UK Media Ops governance model.
• Review legacy and agency-specific ways of working to identify duplication, friction, gaps, rework and inconsistent delivery.
• Work with agency and discipline leads to test standards and playbooks before wider rollout, making sure they work in practice.
Documentation, knowledge management and adoption
• Own the single source of truth for media excellence documentation, playbooks, guidelines and training materials through the agreed repository.
• Govern version control, publication standards and review cycles so teams can trust that materials are current and accurate.
• Remove outdated, duplicated or conflicting guidance and ensure updates are communicated clearly to relevant teams.
• Track adoption of new and existing standards, capturing agency feedback and turning it into improvement actions rather than simply reporting non-compliance.
• Build a practical rhythm for launch communications, refreshers, process reminders and targeted support for teams with low adherence.
Training, capability and community
• Design and oversee structured onboarding, refresher and targeted training programmes that improve adoption and confidence across agencies and disciplines.
• Build role-specific training journeys for priority workflows, making sure training reflects current process documentation and agreed standards.
• Partner with agency operations leads and discipline leads to embed process adherence through capability, not enforcement alone.
• Track training effectiveness through adoption, feedback, process adherence and operational performance indicators.
• Support the development of a media operations community that shares best practice, surfaces issues early and builds stronger operational discipline across agencies.
Financial hygiene, billing and Mediaocean risk control
• Work closely with Finance, Commercial, Billing, Credit Control, Activation and agency/client teams to ensure financial hygiene is understood, followed and visible.
• Help ensure agencies and client teams are adhering to agreed processes for booking accuracy, reconciliation, billing readiness, query resolution and debt prevention.
• Investigate and diagnosing complex financial and billing issues, either owning the exercises or through the managed teams. Example issues will include recurring billing queries, debt blockers, aged items, missing or late bookings, not-vouched costs and unreconciled media balances.
• Work with relevant teams to understand the root cause of financial hygiene issues, identify whether the problem is process, ownership, data quality, training or system behaviour, and agree actions to stop repeats.
• Maintain visibility of Mediaocean balances and related risk areas, ensuring aged or unexplained balances are escalated early and do not build into material commercial exposure.
• Partner with relevant Mediaocean workstream owners to move Mediaocean improvement activity forward where it supports feature enablement, cleaner process control or reduced balance risk, with minor setup or feature-enablement work routed to the right platform specialists, including Harvey where appropriate.
• Support regular reviews with Finance and agency teams to keep billing and debt queries to a minimum and make sure issues have clear owners, actions and resolution dates.
• Provide clear reporting to the Head of Operational Excellence on financial hygiene themes, risk exposure, recurring issues and improvements needed across agencies and client teams.
Governance, risk and issue management
• Support the UK Media Ops governance model by surfacing issues, identifying patterns and turning risks into clear actions.
• Maintain structured visibility of process feedback, risks, adoption gaps and operational issues across agencies and disciplines.
• Contribute to governance forums with insight, trends, recommendations and clear status updates.
• Identify recurring issues and systemic failures, not just individual problems, and work with senior stakeholders to resolve root causes.
• Support the Head of Operational Excellence with decision logs, risk/dependency tracking, escalation routes and follow-up discipline.
Omni, CLM / Operational Foundations and platform alignment
• Support the embedding of CLM, Operational Foundations and Omni-enabled workflows from a media excellence and process adoption perspective.
• Work with relevant system and platform owners, including Omni, Mediaocean and other operational tools, to ensure process guidance, training, controls and reporting are joined up.
• Ensure Omni-supported and non-Omni workflows are documented, owned and governed, so teams have a clear model regardless of platform maturity.
• Identify where existing agency processes need to be simplified, codified or cleaned up before they can be supported effectively through platforms or automation.
• Feed recurring process and data quality issues into the automation and business information agenda where technology can remove friction or reduce risk.
Team leadership and stakeholder management
• Line manage the Media Operational Excellence Manager, setting clear objectives, priorities, delivery expectations and development plans.
• Coach and support the manager to deliver high-quality documentation, training, issue tracking, adoption reporting and governance support.
• Upskill team to ensure they become SMEs in the discipline overtime and own issue diagnosis, data analysis, best practice standards and documentation.
• Build trusted relationships with agency COOs, agency operations leads, Finance, Commercial, Activation, Analytics, EMEA Ops, platform owners and offshore/nearshore teams.
• Lead through influence across teams where there is no direct reporting line, using clarity, credibility and practical problem-solving to move work forward.
• Support the Head of Operational Excellence by driving delivery, preparing clear updates, escalating blockers and helping maintain momentum across the process and governance agenda.
What you will bring
• Strong media operations, process excellence, governance or business operations experience, ideally within a complex agency or media environment.
• Proven ability to turn complex operational processes into clear, usable standards, playbooks, training and management information.
• Strong understanding of financial hygiene in a media environment, including booking, billing, reconciliation, debt queries, Mediaocean balances and commercial risk management.
• Ideally has experience in either biddable channels or planning, with a practical understanding of finance hygiene best practice gained through hands-on media delivery.
• Comfortable working in fast-paced environments and able to handle rapid organisational change, ambiguity and shifting priorities without losing delivery discipline.
• Strong data analysis skills, with the ability to interrogate issues, spot patterns, validate assumptions and turn operational data into clear recommendations.
• Experience reducing day-to-day repetitive work and making teams more effective through automation, better tooling or practical use of basic AI.
• Confidence working with Finance, Commercial, agency leadership, Activation, Analytics, Data, Technology and platform teams.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence teams and drive progress without relying on hierarchy.
• Pragmatic, detail-oriented and commercially aware, with a focus on adoption and impact rather than process for process sake.
• A strong manager who can set direction, coach others and raise the quality of team outputs.
Success measures
• Media Operating Standards: priority workflows documented, current, accessible and actively used by agencies and disciplines.
• Process adoption: measurable improvement in adherence, consistency and execution quality across priority workflows.
• Training effectiveness: onboarding, refresher and targeted training delivered, with evidence of improved confidence and reduced repeat issues.
• Financial hygiene: reduced billing queries, debt blockers, late bookings, not-vouched items, unresolved Mediaocean balances and aged commercial risk areas over time.
• Mediaocean workstream support: relevant Mediaocean risks, feature-enablement needs and balance-control issues are tracked with platform/workstream owners, with clear actions and fewer unresolved blockers.
• Issue investigation: financial, billing and process issues are investigated properly, root causes are identified and actions are tracked through to closure.
• Governance effectiveness: risks, dependencies, actions and escalations are visible, with fewer unresolved blockers and clearer ownership.
• Documentation quality: the agreed repository is accurate, current and trusted, with no material gaps, duplication or outdated guidance.
• Stakeholder confidence: Finance, agency operations, discipline leads and leadership see Media Excellence as practical, responsive and useful.
• Team delivery: the Media Operational Excellence Manager has clear priorities, visible progress, strong outputs and meaningful development support.

Job summary:
Working within the Engagement Strategy team, the Senior Engagement Strategist is responsible for leading the development of integrated, omnichannel engagement strategies and customer experiences for our clients’ brands.

At its core, the role is about understanding audiences, their behaviours and needs, and the environments in which they engage with healthcare brands. The Senior Engagement Strategist brings together audience insight, customer experience, channel strategy, content, data, technology and measurement to create clear, actionable engagement strategies that deliver against client and brand objectives.

The Senior Engagement Strategist will lead engagement strategy projects and pitches from brief interpretation through to strategic development and client-ready recommendations, working with oversight from senior leadership where appropriate. They will collaborate closely with media, data and analytics, creative, technology and account teams to turn strategic thinking into practical, integrated campaign plans.

About you:
You’re a strategic thinker who understands how people engage with healthcare brands and can turn complex information into clear, actionable recommendations. You’re confident working across the full omnichannel ecosystem and understand how audience needs, content, channels, data, technology and measurement connect to create effective customer experiences.

You’re comfortable taking ownership of a project from brief through to recommendation, while bringing the right people together to strengthen the thinking. You can confidently engage clients, lead workshops and present your point of view, and you know how to balance strategic ambition with practical delivery.

You’re curious about people, behaviours, technology and the changing healthcare landscape. You’re collaborative by nature, able to work effectively across disciplines, and are ready to provide guidance and support to more junior members of the team.

Essential Functions:
Engagement Strategy
• Lead engagement strategy projects and pitches end-to-end, turning complex or unclear briefs into a clear strategic approach and activation-ready, client-ready recommendations, with little senior oversight.
• Develop integrated omnichannel engagement strategies and customer experiences across HCP, patient and wider healthcare audiences.
• Apply audience segmentation, persona development and behavioural/customer insight to inform engagement strategy, synthesising qualitative, quantitative, attitudinal, behavioural and performance evidence alongside relevant data, research and market inputs.
• Develop engagement frameworks across the customer journey or adoption ladder, identifying key moments, barriers, triggers, content needs and engagement opportunities, and translating these into clear strategic priorities and actions.
• Develop channel strategies across markets and specialties, defining the role of paid, earned, shared and owned touchpoints and translating channel analysis and audience behaviours into actionable omnichannel plans.
• Define how engagement should be sequenced and orchestrated across moments, including messages, content needs, behavioural triggers, channel roles and next-best actions.
• Develop joined-up omnichannel ecosystems that define how content, channel roles, data flows and technology work together across those moments, including how CRM, tracking, personalisation, behavioural triggers, next-best actions and audience-specific content delivery can tailor engagement across channels.
• Develop both global and local customer engagement strategies, including launch planning and optimisation of established brands.

Client Leadership & Workshops
• Build strong and trusted relationships with clients, acting as a strategic engagement partner and confidently articulating the agency's point of view.
• Design and facilitate client workshops that move strategic thinking forward, including audience development and prioritisation, journey mapping, channel planning, tactical ideation and engagement ecosystems.
• Present complex thinking clearly and persuasively, challenging assumptions where appropriate and turning strategic recommendations into a clear course of action.
• Identify engagement opportunities within existing and prospective client business and help shape the strategic response, contributing to organic growth and new business.

Cross-functional Activation
• Work closely with media, data and analytics, creative, and account teams to turn engagement strategy into practical, integrated campaign plans.
• Bring together, brief and challenge specialist inputs across media, data, technology and other disciplines, ensuring they contribute to a coherent, customer-centric engagement strategy and activation-ready plan.
• Inspire and empower creative teams by providing a clear strategic foundation for ideas that can work effectively across channels.
• Develop relationships with relevant external partners, platforms and technology providers where appropriate.

Measurement & Optimisation
• Define KPIs, learning agendas, optimisation frameworks and reporting requirements in partnership with data and analytics teams as part of the engagement strategy.
• Use performance data and learning to identify opportunities to optimise customer experiences, channel activity and engagement plans.
• Build learning and optimisation loops that help teams refine the experience and improve future activation based on performance.
• Stay abreast of developments in data, technology, platforms and healthcare engagement to identify opportunities for innovation and effectiveness.

Team Contribution
• Support the development of engagement strategy capabilities across the wider team through knowledge sharing and by providing guidance and constructive support to more junior team members within project work.
• Share relevant learning and developments in omnichannel engagement, customer experience, data and innovation across the agency.
• Model high standards of collaboration, responsibility, accountability and inclusive working.

What you'll bring:
• Strong relevant experience in digital and omnichannel engagement strategy, with healthcare or pharmaceutical experience and a strong understanding of HCP, patient and wider healthcare audiences.
• A proven ability to independently own complex engagement strategy work from an ambiguous brief through to a high-quality, actionable client deliverable, while working with little senior oversight.
• Strong strategic storytelling and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex information simple and create clear, compelling, decision-ready recommendations.
• Confidence engaging senior clients, facilitating decisions and bringing together multidisciplinary teams without relying on formal authority.
• Strong analytical and organisational skills, with curiosity, rigour and sound judgement in interpreting audience, behavioural, market and performance evidence.

You’ll lead our Advanced Analytics product area, including MAPs, our strategic customer intelligence capability, while developing our Data Product team and helping shape how we use data, analytics and AI across the Group.

If you’re excited by turning complex data opportunities into products that create genuine customer and commercial value, we’d love to hear from you.

About the Role

As our Data Product Lead, you’ll sit at the intersection of Data, Product and the wider business, identifying where data and advanced analytics can have the greatest impact and turning those opportunities into clear, scalable products.

You’ll own the vision and roadmap for Advanced Analytics and MAPs, our account-level customer intelligence capability bringing together Main Account Facts, Activities and Predictions. Working across Data Science, Data Engineering, CRM, Finance and other teams, you’ll balance competing priorities and focus investment on the opportunities that can create the greatest value.

This is a leadership role as much as a product role. You’ll lead and develop three Data Product team members, establishing strong product practices, clear accountability and a culture of continuous learning.

You’ll also help us explore what’s next. As AI and advanced analytics continue to evolve, you’ll bring new thinking into the team, helping us identify where emerging capabilities can solve real problems and create practical value for our customers and business.

• Purpose with scale - The data products you shape will help us make better decisions and create better experiences for millions of customers across some of the UK’s most trusted consumer brands.

• Collaboration by design - You’ll work across Data Science, Data Engineering, Product, CRM, Finance and Commercial teams to turn complex opportunities into scalable products.
• Responsible innovation - We’re exploring the opportunities created by AI and advanced analytics while keeping data quality, privacy, explainability and responsible use at the heart of what we do.
• A culture built on Accountability, Simplicity, Inclusion and Innovation - We take ownership, value diverse perspectives, challenge ourselves to improve and focus on making the complex simple.

• Own the vision, objectives and roadmap for Advanced Analytics and MAPs, our strategic customer intelligence capability.
• Turn complex business challenges into clear Data Product opportunities, defining objectives, outcomes, KPIs and measures of success.
• Balance priorities across CRM, Finance, Data and other teams, focusing investment and capacity on the highest-value opportunities.
• Work closely with Data Science and Data Engineering teams to take products from discovery and proof of concept through to production, adoption, monitoring and iteration.
• Ensure analytical and predictive products are solving clearly defined business problems and their impact can be measured.
• Lead, coach and develop three Data Product team members, setting clear objectives and helping them grow their product skills and careers.
• Communicate priorities, progress, value, dependencies and trade-offs clearly to senior and executive stakeholders.
• Ensure appropriate standards around data governance, privacy, security, model evaluation, explainability and responsible AI.
• Stay close to emerging Data Product, advanced analytics and AI trends, identifying where new approaches could create practical value for MONY Group and our customers.

Above all, we’re looking for someone who:
• Thinks about outcomes and value, not just outputs.
• Can turn complex data and analytical opportunities into clear, understandable product strategies.
• Is comfortable navigating ambiguity and making evidence-based decisions.
• Builds strong relationships across technical and non-technical teams.
• Can challenge constructively, balance competing priorities and create alignment.
• Enjoys developing others and building strong product capability within a team.
• Stays curious about how data, analytics and AI can be used to solve meaningful customer and business problems.

Position Overview
We are seeking a talented and intellectually curious Quantitative Analyst to join our central Quantitative Research & Analytics team. The team partners with fundamental investment teams to enhance investment research and decision-making through quantitative analysis, data science, and innovative technology.
The successful candidate will work alongside investment professionals to develop analytical frameworks, investigate investment questions, and build tools that generate differentiated insights and improve research efficiency.
This role offers a unique opportunity to apply quantitative and computational techniques to real-world investment problems, combining rigorous analytical work with exposure to fundamental equity investing, portfolio analytics, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence.

Quantitative Investment Research
Support the development and application of quantitative frameworks that enhance fundamental investment research and decision-making.
Analyze company fundamentals, financial statements, market data, and other datasets to investigate investment hypotheses and identify meaningful patterns.
Conduct statistical analyses, empirical research, and backtesting to evaluate investment signals, relationships, and analytical methodologies.
Collaborate with senior quantitative researchers to develop approaches for assessing business quality, valuation, earnings dynamics, and other investment characteristics.
Translate analytical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights for investment professionals.
Data Science & Advanced Analytics
Apply statistical methods, machine learning, and data science techniques to investment research problems.
Work with large, complex datasets, including financial, economic, and alternative data.
Develop and maintain robust data pipelines, analytical workflows, and reusable research code.

Support the development of scalable analytical capabilities that can be leveraged across multiple investment teams.

Assist in developing analytical tools and visualizations that help investment teams understand portfolio positioning and sources of risk.
Collaboration & Analytical Delivery
Partner with colleagues across the central quantitative team and fundamental investment teams to understand research requirements and deliver analytical solutions.
Present findings clearly, explaining methodologies, assumptions, limitations, and implications.
Document research processes, analytical methodologies, and code to support reproducibility and knowledge sharing.
Contribute to a collaborative, intellectually rigorous, and innovative research environment.

Professional experience in quantitative research, data science, financial analytics, or a related analytical role.
Strong programming proficiency in Python, including experience with data manipulation, statistical analysis, and analytical libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and scikit-learn.
Solid foundation in statistics, probability, regression analysis, and empirical research methods.
Experience working with large datasets, including data cleaning, transformation, and exploratory analysis.
Familiarity with SQL and modern data analysis workflows.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and methodological rigor.
Ability to communicate technical findings effectively to both quantitative and non-quantitative audiences.
Intellectual curiosity, a collaborative mindset, and a strong interest in financial markets and investing.
Preferred
Experience in asset management, investment research, financial services, or a related industry.
Familiarity with equity fundamentals, financial statements, valuation concepts, and investment research processes.
Experience with financial market datasets and platforms such as Bloomberg, FactSet, or Capital IQ.
Exposure to machine learning, natural language processing, large language models, or generative AI applications.
Familiarity with Git, cloud computing platforms, and software development best practices.

job_title: 2027 UK Degree Apprenticeship Programme: Rail Systems Engineering
job_description:
Before making an application, please browse all apprenticeship opportunities available as we will only accept one application per candidate.  Once you have made an application you will not be able to make changes to your selection or make a new application.  The exception is if we open new vacancies in Spring 2027.  
 
These opportunities are for those who have A-levels or equivalent and looking to undertake a degree apprenticeship (level 6).  We will close for applications on 15th January 2027.
 
Application process
 

Application form
Online strengths-based assessment

 
CVs and cover letters are not required as part of the application process. Candidates will be assessed through a single-stage strengths-based interview.
 
Eligibility
 
If you are successful and are offered an apprenticeship with us, you will enrol onto the Rail Systems Engineering BEng at London South Bank University, or Sheffield Hallam University, the courses will be delivered as block release.
 
For more information including their grade requirements, please visit:
 
Rail and rail systems senior engineer | Sheffield Hallam University
 Rail and Rail Systems Engineering Apprenticeship BEng (Hons) | London South Bank University
 
Are you ready to start your career journey with purpose, passion, and possibility? Our apprenticeships offer more than just a job - they’re an opportunity to shape your future.
 
As a paid degree apprentice, you’ll gain hands-on experience working on real projects while studying towards your degree. You’ll develop your technical and professional skills alongside experienced engineers, applying what you learn through your studies directly in the workplace.
Help shape the future of rail
 
Imagine beginning your engineering career by helping create safer, more reliable and more sustainable transport connections for the communities that depend on them.
 
As a Railway Engineering Degree Apprentice within our Track team, you’ll have the opportunity to do exactly that. From day one, you’ll be part of a collaborative team, contributing to real rail projects while learning from experienced engineers and developing towards your BEng (Honours) Railway Engineering degree.
 
You’ll combine academic study with practical experience, giving you the opportunity to apply what you learn and see the impact of engineering decisions in the real world.
 
Most importantly, you won’t be expected to know everything when you join us. This is an apprenticeship designed to help you build your knowledge, confidence and experience over time, with support from the people around you.
 
Our Transport team
 
We help conceive, develop and deliver transport solutions for cities, regions and infrastructure owners and operators around the world.
 
Our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle, from developing business cases and advising on areas such as procurement, revenue and environmental legislation through to engineering design, infrastructure delivery and ongoing asset management.
 
Our planning, engineering, environmental and management specialists work together to solve complex challenges responsibly, creating solutions that connect people and places while delivering lasting benefits for society.
 
Beyond transport, our teams also contribute to complex multidisciplinary civil engineering projects, including water and power tunnels, as well as providing specialist advisory services in areas such as technology and socio-economics.
 
Our Transport unit consists of four divisions:
 

Aviation, Maritime and Offshore
Heavy Civil Infrastructure
Rail
Transport and Mobility Solutions

 
You'll be joining an environment where collaboration across teams, disciplines and locations helps us share knowledge, challenge ideas and achieve better outcomes together.
 
Your apprenticeship
 
An apprenticeship allows you to earn while you learn, combining a paid role and valuable workplace experience with structured academic study.
 
Meet your team
 
You'll join our Rail division's Track team, working alongside people with a wide variety of skills and experiences, including civil and mechanical engineers, engineering managers, project managers and technical specialists.
 
Different perspectives make our teams stronger. You'll have opportunities to learn from colleagues with different professional backgrounds, share your own ideas and work together to solve complex engineering problems.
 
Our portfolio is varied and includes both UK and international work, with projects for clients including Network Rail, East West Rail, the Department for Transport, Northern Powerhouse Rail and London Underground.
 
From concept and feasibility through to detailed design, you'll see how different disciplines come together to turn ideas into infrastructure that people can rely on.
 
What you could be doing
 
You’ll be part of the team from day one, supporting our engineers while gradually developing the technical knowledge and practical skills you need for a successful career in railway engineering.
 
Your experience could include:
 

Track alignment design, helping identify suitable routes for new railways and modifications to existing rail infrastructure.
Infrastructure inspections and analysis, using desktop studies and site surveys to understand the condition and requirements of existing assets.
Gauging assessments, helping ensure appropriate clearances are provided for trains, structures, platforms and passengers.
Journey time evaluations, helping teams understand how different designs could influence railway performance.
Track-Ex and rail wear modelling, developing your understanding of how railway operation affects track infrastructure.
Buffer stop risk assessments, contributing to the safe and responsible design and operation of the railway.
Track design and specification, helping develop infrastructure solutions that optimise performance, reliability and resilience.
Preparing engineering reports, calculations and specifications.
Developing your digital engineering capabilities through BIM models and CAD drawings.
Supporting site-based activities and learning how designs translate from drawings and models into real infrastructure.

 
The work you undertake will develop as your knowledge and confidence grow. You'll be supported to ask questions, learn from others and understand not only how engineering decisions are made, but why they matter.
 
Learn, contribute and grow
 
Your apprenticeship is the beginning of your professional journey.
 
Alongside developing your technical knowledge, you'll have opportunities to strengthen skills such as teamwork, communication, problem solving, collaboration and responsible decision-making.
 
Working alongside experienced colleagues means you'll be able to learn from different perspectives while starting to identify the areas of railway engineering that interest you most. As you progress, you'll have opportunities to take on greater responsibility and celebrate each milestone towards becoming an engineering professional.
We want you to feel comfortable asking questions and sharing ideas. Trust and integrity are fundamental to good engineering, so you'll be encouraged to speak up, consider different perspectives and contribute thoughtfully to the decisions our teams make.
 
Candidate Specification
 
As well as the eligibility criteria detailed, above, we are looking for future apprentices with the following strengths: 
 

Proactively takes initiative to complete tasks efficiently and independently.
Communicates effectively and clearly with clients and colleagues.
Delivers high quality written work with strong attention to detail and clarity.
Demonstrates a structured and analytical approach to problem solving.

 UK Immigration

Mott MacDonald Ltd. are not currently offering sponsorship to candidates under the Skilled Worker visa route in the UK. This decision is as a consequence of the changes made to the Skilled Worker route by the UK Government in April 2024.

Technical strategy. Help define the multi-year technical direction for the platform, tie it to business outcomes, and turn it into a roadmap the team can execute against. We have strong engineers working on this, and you’re expected to join and push together.

Operated at Staff level or above. You’ve been formally recognised at Staff, Principal, or equivalent, or you’ve been the senior technical lead at a startup with clearly equivalent scope. Your impact reached across multiple teams or the whole engineering organisation.

Enterprise B2B SaaS at scale: multi-tenancy, SSO, data isolation, and compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR).
Event-driven and streaming architectures (e.g. Kafka) in production.
Took a platform and engineering team through a rapid growth phase at a startup.
Public technical work, such as talks, writing, or meaningful open-source contributions.

You’re a strong Senior engineer looking for your first Staff role. We’d love to hear from you for other openings, but not this one.
You haven’t written production code regularly in the last two years.
You need a detailed spec, a stable roadmap, or a large supporting team to be effective.
Your experience is mainly in a narrow specialism, and you haven’t owned broad technical direction.

Frontend: React
Data: Postgres, DynamoDB, Kafka

We care about fundamentals over specific languages, but you’ll be expected to become credible across this stack quickly.

Direct influence on the technical direction of the company, working alongside the CEO and leadership team
Remote-first working, with a private office in Temple/Strand, London for collaboration and team lunches

Deep dive (1.5 hours): a deep-dive walkthrough of a system you led. Expect us to probe every decision, failure mode, and trade-off or an open-ended design problem.

We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

We're on a mission to reinvent how our clients work

Most companies are bolting AI onto old processes and hoping for the best. We think that's the wrong way round.

Nearform is on an exciting journey with AI, and we're building a new team to lead it. The team brings together two worlds that rarely meet: the business thinking of a strategy firm and the engineering depth of a company that builds and ships real products. That puts us in a small group of firms that can do both. We work out what should change and we build it.

The Role

Our clients don't all start in the same place. Some know something has to change but have no idea where to start. Others have a clear picture of the future and are ready to build. Most are somewhere in between.

Your job is to work out where each client really is and shape the right solution for them. That could mean helping a leadership team choose which process to tackle first. It could also mean turning a rough idea into something our engineers can build.

This isn't a traditional management consulting role

You won't be writing a strategy deck that sits on a shelf. This is  hands-on work, close to the technology, and focused on results you can see.

Primary Responsibilities:

•  Get on the ground. Sit with the teams doing the work, whether they're checking customers against sanctions lists or pulling together month-end reports. Learn how it really happens, including the workarounds, the judgement calls and the steps nobody wrote down.

• Spot the opportunity. Find where AI and automation can change the game, and where a person still needs to make the call.

• Design what comes next. Work side by side with a forward deployed engineer to shape a better way of working, testing ideas against what can actually be built.

• Prove the value. Own the business case for each process you redesign. Work out where the value is, put numbers on it, and set up how it will be measured, so that after go-live you can show the client what changed.

• Make it real. Turn your design into a plan clear enough for our engineering teams to build, then see it go live.

• Bring people with you. Run workshops, win over frontline staff and make the case to senior leaders.

Between clients, you'll help build what comes next:

• Help win new work. Join early conversations with prospective clients and help shape proposals that show what's possible.

• Shape our offer. Turn what you learn on projects into the methods, tools and stories that make the next engagement faster and sharper.

• Make the team stronger. Share what works, test new ideas and help define how this team operates as it grows.

Experience:

•  At least 10 years in consulting, business analysis, operations improvement or a similar role.

• A track record of mapping a business process and redesigning it with real stakeholders.

• Confidence in front of clients, whether you're running a workshop, interviewing frontline staff or presenting to a broad group of client stakeholders, including the C-suite.

• Outcomes thinking. You start with the result the client needs, such as faster turnaround, lower cost or fewer errors, and work backwards from there. You judge success by what changes for the business, not by what gets delivered.

• Commercial sharpness. You've built business cases before and can turn operational improvements into numbers a CFO will believe.

• Storytelling. You can pull together a clear, compelling storyline for presentations, quarterly business reviews and leadership updates, the kind that gets decisions made.

• Builder's mindset. You work in short cycles and test ideas quickly. You'll spin up a proof of concept with tools like Claude Cowork, Lovable or Replit to show a client what's possible, rather than waiting for a perfect plan.

• A solid grasp of what AI and automation can and can't do. You don't need to code, but you'll hold your own with engineers.

• Sharp writing: you turn messy conversations into a clear document others can act on.

• Able to spend time on client sites.

The Role:

We're looking for a software engineer to join the Neo4j Sharding Engineering team. We own Infinigraph and Composite, and we make them work as managed offerings on Aura, Neo4j’s cloud platform.

Aura is Neo4j’s fully managed graph database as a service. Customers create, scale, and use Neo4j databases in the cloud without installing, clustering, or operating the database themselves. Aura runs on Kubernetes across Google Cloud, AWS, and Azure, and handles provisioning, networking, security, upgrades, and day-to-day operations for those databases.

Composite is the technology behind distributed query execution in Neo4j: one query can span multiple databases. Infinigraph is our database sharding offering for large data volumes, built on a distributed database architecture. Distributed query execution is a complex and interesting topic covering query language design, performant networking, and concurrency. Those capabilities still have to run as a cloud product, and that's where a large part of this role sits: building the Go services and Kubernetes machinery that provision, scale, and operate sharded and composite clusters on Aura, reliably, at the data volumes our customers keep growing into.

As part of an energetic and fun team of engineers, you'll work at the frontier of designing and implementing new capabilities for Neo4j on Aura.

The Role:

The Kernel team builds the storage engine and transaction machinery inside Neo4j. If you join us, you will not be building web APIs or shuffling data between services. Instead, you will be working directly on the database engine itself.

Our day-to-day is low-level systems engineering. We write and maintain custom storage engines, the page cache, transaction handling (WAL, ACID guarantees), indexing, and memory management. The code we write determines how fast queries run across billions of nodes and relationships, and how safely data is written when a machine crashes.

We are a pragmatic, engineering-led group split between Malmö and London. We read and discuss database papers (VLDB, SIGMOD, and others) to see what ideas are worth pulling into the product. We also run regular “Do What You Want” weeks so everyone has dedicated time to experiment with their own prototypes or tooling improvements.

What you will actually be doing:

• Designing, profiling, and implementing core database features, including storage formats, index structures, and recovery paths.

• Diagnosing tricky concurrency bugs, race conditions, and lock contention.

• Performance engineering: profiling CPU, memory allocation, off-heap memory, and disk I/O to improve latency.

• Reviewing designs and PRs with a heavy focus on correctness, data integrity, and long-term maintainability.

• Helping decide technical direction and architectural trade-offs as our engine evolves.

What we are looking for:

• Systems programming experience: You are comfortable working close to the hardware. Most of our codebase is Java, but if your background is in C++, Rust, or Go and you understand memory layouts and concurrency, that translates well.

• Concurrency and data structures: You have a clear understanding of threads, locks, atomic operations, cache locality, and algorithmic complexity.

• Pragmatic engineering: You write thorough tests because edge cases in database kernels are painful to debug in production.

• Collaborative attitude: You are comfortable having your technical choices questioned, you back up decisions with data or benchmarks, and you treat code review as a two-way discussion rather than a hurdle.

It is a bonus if you have:

• Prior experience with database internals, storage engines, or file systems.

• Deep knowledge of JVM internals, such as GC behavior, JIT compilation, and off-heap memory.

• Hands-on experience with profiling tools like async-profiler, JFR, or perf.

• Experience navigating and evolving large, mature codebases.

At Neo4j, we have always strived to help the world make sense of data. 

As business, society and knowledge become increasingly connected, our technology promotes innovation by helping organizations to find and understand data relationships. The Team:

Neo4j's managed cloud offering, Aura, brings the power of graph databases to the cloud. We're forming a new Product Analytics Platform team.

As Neo4j Aura’s platform and product surface area have grown, so has the need for a consistent, purpose-built way to capture what's happening across them. Today, each product tracks its own data, but retrieving it can be difficult.

This team will own the Analytics API and infrastructure that collects raw product analytics events from across Neo4j's products so every team integrates with one contract instead of inventing their own.

The Role:

In this role you’ll be one of the founding members of the Product Analytics Platform team. You’ll help define the technical foundations for how product analytics data is captured across Aura, building the Analytics API and underlying infrastructure that provides a consistent integration point for engineering teams across Neo4j.

You’ll have significant ownership over the design of the API, balancing the needs of multiple product teams with the long-term maintainability of the platform. You’ll work closely with Product Management and other engineering teams to shape the solution, drive adoption, and evolve it as the platform grows.

Primary responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate the Analytics API and the underlying infrastructure, defining the schema and integration contract used by teams across Aura.

• Make pragmatic architectural decisions around event ingestion, data contracts, reliability, and scalability as the platform grows.

• Build a simple, well-defined integration layer that makes it easy for product teams to send analytics events without coupling them to the underlying data infrastructure.

• Drive adoption across the Engineering organisation, working with teams to integrate with the API and providing the guidance and documentation they need.

• Keep product analytics and billing concerns cleanly separated, even where the underlying data flows or infrastructure may be similar.

• Evaluate build vs. buy across the existing analytics and data stack, including tools such as Segment and BigQuery, keeping the API focused on collection rather than reimplementing downstream capabilities.

• Partner closely with the team building the downstream data pipeline to ensure raw events are reliable, well-structured, and usable for analytics.

• Define and evolve the platform through RFCs, technical documentation, and close collaboration with Product Management and other engineering teams.

What you'll need

• Strong backend software engineering experience, with Go as your primary language, building and operating APIs, services, or ingestion systems that other teams depend on.

• Experience designing well-defined APIs and integration contracts, including thinking about schemas, backwards compatibility, validation, and how other engineering teams will consume them.

• Experience building production services in Go, from smaller utilities and scripts through to larger, long-running services or microservices.

• Some experience with TypeScript or JavaScript and an ability to work comfortably in a codebase that spans backend and frontend technologies. This is primarily a backend role — you won't be responsible for UI development.

• Familiarity with event-driven systems, data ingestion, or data pipeline tooling such as Segment, BigQuery, or similar.

• Ability to work independently in a new area, make pragmatic technical decisions, and drive work forward with limited direction.

• Comfortable writing RFCs and technical documentation, and working across teams to establish and drive adoption of a new integration point.

• Clear, concise communication — a lot of this role involves defining contracts, documenting decisions, and helping other engineers integrate with what you build.

What's nice to have

• Experience with observability, including tracing, logging, and metrics.

• Experience integrating with GCP, AWS, or Azure.

• Experience working with product analytics, event tracking, or telemetry systems.

About the Team

The Guardian team builds practical safety and oversight systems for increasingly capable AI agents. Our goal is to make it possible for agents to take on longer-running, higher-autonomy work while preserving meaningful safeguards, respecting user intent, and intervening when actions could cause serious or difficult-to-reverse harm.

Auto-review is an early example of this work. When an agent reaches a permission boundary, a separate model evaluates the proposed action in context and determines whether it should proceed. The team is now extending this foundation into more capable oversight systems that account for richer user context, support a broader range of agent experiences, and integrate across OpenAI products.

Guardian sits at the intersection of engineering, alignment research, product, infrastructure, and security. The team already has a strong engineering foundation in London and will continue to grow there as a concentrated, highly collaborative group.

The role

You will own the product capability that lets PhysicsX and its customers improve LLMs for their specific work.

You will be a hands-on product ML engineer embedded deeply with our Research group and accountable for turning post-training methods into something customers can use. The first goal is to make open models perform strongly on the evals and benchmarks that matter to us. The longer-term goal is a repeatable platform capability through which customers can train models on their own workflows keeping their data, learned behaviour and intellectual property under their control.

The remit is broader than supervised fine-tuning. You will choose and apply the right post-training methods, including preference optimisation, reinforcement learning, distillation, synthetic data and verifier-based approaches. You will own the capability roadmap and production outcome; Research will be a close partner in developing methods, and platform product teams will be partners in integrating the experience.

What you will do

• Own the path from a base model and customer workflow to a measured, deployable model improvement.

• Build reliable post-training harnesses covering data preparation, training, evaluation, model artifacts and hand-off to serving.

• Improve open models against PhysicsX's agent and engineering benchmarks, using evidence to decide whether training is better than changes to prompts, tools or the agent design.

• Develop and operate methods spanning SFT, preference optimisation, RLHF/RLAIF, RL with verifiable rewards, distillation, rejection sampling and related techniques.

• Build reproducible synthetic-data and expert-data pipelines, including quality filtering, provenance, licensing and contamination controls.

• Design reward signals, verifiers and rollout workflows while detecting reward hacking, benchmark overfitting, model collapse and unintended regressions.

• Make post-training available through a mix of managed workflows and expert-facing interfaces.

• Ensure customer data and resulting model artifacts can remain within the customer's platform environment across SaaS, VPC and air-gapped deployments.

• Help determine how this capability should grow and, over time, shape the team around it.

What you bring

Where you need to be strongest

• You have measurably improved model behaviour through post-training and turned that work into a capability used in production.

• You are deeply hands-on across data, training, evaluation and debugging; you can take an experiment from hypothesis to deployed artifact.

• You understand modern post-training methods well enough to choose among them based on the task and evidence rather than fashion.

• You have built high-quality training datasets from expert, behavioural or synthetic sources and understand that data design is part of model design.

• You can diagnose training and behavioural failures, including instability, drift, reward exploitation, leakage and overfitting to evals.

• You are product-minded: you start from a user workflow, define success, make trade-offs and build an experience others can operate.

• You can work as the accountable product owner of a technical capability while collaborating closely with research scientists, platform engineers and product teams.

• Distributed training, accelerator utilisation, checkpointing, recovery, experiment tracking and reproducibility.

• Model packaging and the operational path from training to evaluation and production serving.

• Experience building managed and expert-facing model customisation products.

Position Summary 

The Customer Support Specialist - LC (Liquid Chromatography) Software plays a critical role in enabling Thermo Fisher Scientific chromatography systems to operate seamlessly on the Empower™ Chromatography Data System (CDS) through Seamless Instrument Integration (SII). This role serves as the technical and functional bridge between Thermo Fisher Scientific and Empower, ensuring reliable, compliant, and scalable integration of Thermo instrumentation within customer Empower environments.

Operating within the HPCS Business Unit of the CMD Division, the SII Empower Expert supports both Analytical Development (AD) and Quality Control (QC) customers who standardize on Empower as their CDS. The role works collaboratively with internal stakeholders—including Commercial, Technical Sales Support (TSS), IES/Service, COE, and Software teams—as well as external partners and customers, to support pre-sale positioning, post-sale execution, and long-term customer success.

The Customer Support Specialist - LC Software operates in a hybrid environment, balancing home office and customer-facing activities, and requires strong technical expertise, cross-functional influence, and the ability to manage complex integrations across matrixed organizations.

Key Objectives
Act as the primary subject-matter expert for SII integration between Thermo Fisher chromatography systems and Empower CDS. 

• Support customers in successfully running Thermo instrumentation on Empower, ensuring performance, reliability, and compliance in regulated environments. 

• Serve as the technical interface between Thermo Fisher and Waters for SII-related topics, including compatibility, issue resolution, and lifecycle changes. 

• Assist sales colleagues in pre-sales engagements to set clear expectations and address customer concerns related to Empower compatibility and SII capabilities. 

• Partner with TSS, IES, COE, and Software teams to support pre-sale positioning and post-sale execution. 

• Participate proactively in escalations related to SII/Empower integrations to accelerate resolution and protect customer confidence. 

• Provide guidance on data integrity, validation, and compliance considerations (e.g., 21 CFR Part 11) for Thermo instruments controlled via Empower. 

• Capture and share lessons learned, recurring issues, and best practices to improve SII reliability and customer experience. 

• Support standardization of workflows, documentation, and troubleshooting approaches aligned with Thermo Fisher’s PPI Business System. 

• Deliver targeted internal and customer-facing training related to SII-Empower operation and best practices.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Engineering, Informatics, or a related scientific or technical discipline, or equivalent experience. 

• 7+ years of experience supporting chromatography systems and/or CDS integrations, with strong expertise in Empower. 

• Demonstrated experience enabling third-party CDS control of analytical instrumentation. 

• Experience working directly with customers in regulated Pharma/BioPharma environments (AD and/or QC). 

• Ability to collaborate effectively across internal functions and external partners in a matrixed organization. 

• Ability to travel to customer locations up to 60% including overnight & international travel 

Desirable Personality Traits & Skills

• Recognized technical expert with the ability to build credibility and trust with customers and internal stakeholders. 

• Strong problem-solving skills with a structured, systems-level approach. 

• Clear and confident communicator, able to translate complex technical topics into practical guidance. 

• Proactive, self-directed, and comfortable operating independently with minimal supervision. 

• Strong sense of ownership and accountability for customer outcomes. 

• Ability to mentor peers and contribute to team capability building.

job_description:
Location: UK or Europe (Netherlands, France, Belgium, Switzerland)
Status: Full-Time, on going
Starting Salary: UK £60,030; NL and other EU countries €70,920, commensurate with professional experience and internal equity
Closing Date: Submit application by November 10
Risk Level: Level 1 - Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data
About Prosper Global
Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Prosper Global to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.
The Program / Department / Team (Program / Department Summary)
The Technical Support, Evidence, and Program Quality (TEQ) unit sits within Programs. TEQ supports program impact though direct program support, program systems and tools, and influence. Our team, in collaboration with our regional and program counterparts, provides technical leadership for all four Prosper Global impact priorities and the sectors they encompass. We bolster program quality by leading the development of guidance and tools that shape how we implement programs and how we assess program effectiveness. 
In 2022, Prosper Global piloted a mechanism to measure our progress towards our strategic intent and are now scaling and regularizing associated processes. Our strategy measurement mechanism includes two important components: 1) measuring the alignment and the progress of our programs towards participant-facing strategic goals and outcomes (“Organizational Outcome Measurement”, or OOM); and 2) tracking internally facing indicators of operational health (“Organization Performance Indicators,” or OPIs).
The Position 
The position is focused on OPIs, OOM and MEL program support and is part of the MEL team. They will work under the supervision of the Director of Measurement, Strategy and Program Performance, and, in collaboration with various departments, will develop systems and structures to periodically collect, report, and track our OPIs, as well as curate programmatic data. The Senior Advisor will promote appropriate integration of OPIs in country and regional strategic workplans. Additionally, the position will support OOM by analyzing and summarizing programmatic data in each of Prosper Global’s impact priorities, conducting deep dives to identify areas where operational and programmatic progress may be co-dependent, and developing OOM dashboards. In addition to working closely with TEQ and MEL, the position will also work closely with the office of the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Operations Management, Financial Planning & Analysis, and People Team. The position is expected to promote the MEL Tech suite and support teams to integrate their data for use and decision making. Finally, the role will provide training and capacity building support to program teams in the areas of data management, visualization and VfM, and promote the overall efforts around data standardization and data use in countries and programs.
The MEL position is a critical role that requires the incumbent to master organizational performance metrics, data collection, analysis, and reporting, as well as demonstrate exception skill with visualization platforms. 
Essential Responsibilities 
Coordinate and support the alignment of OPIs across various units and departments, regions and country offices. (20%) 
Oversee and lead the OPI working group in refining OPIs, determining data collection cycles, aligning data protocols, developing clear standard operating procedures, promoting integration across technology platforms, and continuously improving these processes. The working group and community of practice will consist of team members from each department contributing OPI data. 
Act as a key organizational authority on OPIs, providing strategic guidance and serving as the primary representative for engaging with senior agency stakeholders. Lead efforts to disaggregate, refine, and adapt OPIs to maintain their accuracy, relevance, and alignment with organizational decision-making and strategic priorities.
Work closely with the SRU to integrate the selected OPIs in country and regional strategies, by conducting webinars, and leading key communication events as needed. 
Act as technical advisor to Country and Regional teams as necessary, ensuring appropriate integration of OPIs in their strategic workplans. Oversee standardization of measurement units, alignment of reporting schedules, and synchronization of data sources with global reporting mechanisms to ensure consistency and accountability.
Produce ad-hoc reports for senior leaders, including the Board of Directors, the Executive Leadership Team and Leadership Team, showcasing OPIs and related metrics to gauge organizational health. 
Strengthen data literacy within the organization on appropriate use of OPIs at various levels.
Collect, analyze and report progress against Organizational Performance Indicators (20%)
Lead OPI reporting cycles and set expectations for delivery of new functionalities.
Actively seek and encourage feedback from stakeholders to inform the prioritization of new product features and enhancements for development.
Design, implement, and oversee the strategic scaling of a comprehensive framework for the systematic collection, analysis, and reporting of OPIs, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and scalability across all operational levels. 
Oversee the collection of OPIs from various units, ensure data quality and consistency over time and identify areas for improvement. Lead efforts to identify and address systemic gaps, driving continuous improvement and alignment with organizational standards and goals.
Work with data-contributing teams to refine their data collection and management processes as needed for individual OPIs.
With the support of IT and the Data Strategy Working Group, lead the development of a data infrastructure to automate data ingestion into Fabric and visualization in PowerBI. Streamline existing organizational reporting and data collection efforts to reflect OPI reporting and facilitate data transfer.
Analyze OPI data on a regular basis or on demand by various units, producing brief reports as requested. Conduct, facilitate and co-facilitate sensemaking sessions, to contextualize, localize and ground truth the observations and analysis generated from the findings.
Work closely with the other Strategy Measurement team members to identify areas where OPI progress analysis can be integrated in the overall Strategy Results Measurement and progress tracking, identifying interdependencies between OPIs and program results. 
Organizational Outcome Measurement and Mapping Our Reach (30%)
Analyze programmatic quantitative data reported through TolaData and supplementary sources.
Create data analysis products/results that are clear, easy to understand, and relevant, including dashboards for country and regional users.
Support OOM report writing, including providing clear interpretations of data analysis
Liaise with the MEL automation team to coordinate data gathering, cleaning, and analysis efforts.
Support the analysis efforts of the annual Mapping Our Reach participant count, including development of dashboards for tracking, quality assurance and final reporting.
Program and HQ data integration support (30%)
Support the HQ MEL Tech team in the rollout of the MEL Tech suite with programs.
Work with IT, MEL and T4D towards data integration to promote data use and learning.
Provide technical assistance in areas that use blend of datasets and methods, including value for money (VfM) and internal performance reviews.
Support the organizational efforts in generating cost-efficiency analysis by conducting VfM analysis based on donor requests and programmatic needs.
Co-lead the workstream on Generative AI and data integration across MEL, Finance, People Team, among others.
Ensure data integration across departments and automate data ingestion in OPI dashboard, OOM products and program delivery outputs.
Provide training and capacity building support to teams in the areas of data management, visualization and VfM.
Supervisory Responsibility
None.
Accountability 
Report directly to: Director of Measurement
Works directly with: TEQ, Finance, Pople Team, Ethics and Compliance, Fundraising team and other OPI leads focal points, in addition to MEL members at HQ and countries/regions.
Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders
Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.
Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills
- Education: BA/MA in international development, social science , MEL, data analysis, or related sector (or equivalent hands-on experience) and relevant certifications preferred.
- Experience: at least 7 years of experience in aggregating and reporting data across various programs, or for agency-level indicator measurement, including environmental, social and governance (ESG) measurement. In some agencies they are known as internal progress indicators, KPIs, and others. Experience with similar agency reporting mechanisms, such as Balance ScoreCards, and ESG reporting highly preferred. 
- Expertise and Knowledge: Deep knowledge of data management is required, including standardization of data variables, data cleaning, data analysis and reporting. Expertise in producing interactive data visualizations, communicating data findings, ground truthing and producing reports on data findings that is understandable and accessible to a wider audience is going to be a core part of the job and skills and knowledge in this area are mandatory. Therefore, the candidate will be required to demonstrate previous success in other employment opportunities.
- Technology and Data Literacy: Knowledge of how to produce and communicate accessible interactive dashboards, help interpret and communicate findings are mandatory for this role. Candidates with prior experience of supporting or leading development of databases, and with a strong understanding of data engineering, data structures, and building data models will be preferred for this role. Familiarity with mobile data collection platforms , Advanced experience with Power BI, including DAX and M languages is required. Familiarity with data automation, Microsoft Azure and SQL is an added advantage. 
- Knowledge of English is required and knowledge of French, Arabic or Spanish is preferred.
Success Factors
- Strategic critical and evaluative thinking skills: 
Demonstrated abilities and track record in strategic systems and holistic thinking, managing resistance to change and understanding of organizational culture and behavior, learning and change management.
Strong organizational and process management capabilities. Ability to effectively set priorities and handle competing time and resource demands for self and others. Comfortable working independently and with limited oversight in a fast-paced environment across diverse teams.

What makes this role different
From product to platform. Altium 365 is opening up to customers, partners, developers and AI agents. The Altium Developer Center is the focal point: one place to find our APIs, SDKs, MCP servers and developer tools.
A real solution built on it. Renesas 365 is the first vertical solution built on Altium 365, and you'll shape the architecture for the ones that follow.
A domain worth modelling. Electronics design data links requirements, components, schematics, layouts, supply chain and manufacturing. Model-first, domain-driven design is at the core of this role.
One platform, many environments. Four commercial regions, GovCloud, China and on-prem, all served by the same platform.
AI agents on engineering data. You'll shape how agents work with design data through MCP, with the security and access control that enterprise customers need.
Influence, hands on. You'll shape the platform's direction and how architecture decisions are made, and still prototype and work in the code.

As Senior Staff Architect for Altium 365, you'll own the big picture of how the platform is structured and how it evolves. You'll drive a model-first, domain-driven approach to design, so teams agree on the domain before the implementation.
You will:
Lead domain-driven design: facilitate domain modelling, define bounded contexts and maintain shared domain models.
Define the target architecture for Altium 365 and keep it consistent across every deployment.
Guide the platform's openness: API strategy, integrations, the Developer Center, and the architecture that lets partners build vertical solutions on top.
Shape how AI agents work with Altium data: MCP, authentication, scopes and security.
Advise teams through the architecture advice process, and own cross-cutting decisions and their ADRs.
Build prototypes and proofs of concept to test ideas before teams commit to them.
Review designs and mentor engineers.
This is a hands-on role: expect deep dives into a large codebase and complex production environments.

10+ years in software development, with substantial experience as an architect of a large cloud platform.
Practical experience with domain-driven design and model-first approaches, including introducing them to other teams.
Strong C#/.NET, or another modern language and willingness to work in C#, and the ability to prototype quickly.
Experience building multi-tenant, multi-region SaaS products.

• Coordinate specialized enablement sessions focused on the nuances of the PE investment lifecycle, financial modeling, and executive engagement strategies.

• Solid track record of recruiting, developing, and retaining a high performing enterprise sales organization
• Experience selling HCM software and or related products preferred.
• Able to accurately forecast team performance on a monthly and quarterly time frame.
• Proven ability to manage teams focused on both direct revenue generation as well as influence and indirect revenue generation (rather than purely transactional sales).
• Deep understanding of the financial and operational drivers within Private Equity portfolio companies.
• Motivated with a desire to learn and have a strong work ethic

Location: London / Coventry Store Support Centre & Home – colleagues go into the office 1-2 days per week on average.

About the team
The Customs team helps the Group manage its customs obligations and keep imports and exports compliant, efficient and supported by accurate evidence. Working within Finance, the team partners with Supply Chain, Procurement, external customs agents and other business areas to identify risk, resolve issues and improve customs data and controls. This role offers broad exposure to the movement of goods and the opportunity to make a practical difference to compliance, cost and operational decision-making.
More about the role
As Customs Analyst, you will support the Customs Manager with the preparation, validation and monitoring of customs declarations and duty. You will maintain records for tariff classification, customs valuation and country of origin decisions, complete reconciliations across customs systems, broker data, deferment accounts and Finance records, and investigate exceptions or data-quality issues.
Your day-to-day work will include responding to customs queries, supporting registrations, guarantees and authorisations, and helping monitor compliance with agreed procedures and controls. You will provide analysis for duty optimisation, customs reliefs and preferential origin under applicable free trade agreements. You will also gather evidence for audits and authority enquiries, track actions through to completion and contribute to improvements in customs reporting, controls, data and automation.
More about you
You will bring practical knowledge of UK customs requirements, including tariff classification, valuation and origin, together with experience of customs declarations, import data, brokers, duty and import VAT records.
