Behind every Argos order is a network of cutting edge logistics automation. As our FM and Depot Automation Manager, you'll own it from the day a new site is mobilised through to steady state operation, refurbishment and eventual replacement.

You'll be the single point of accountability for how our automated assets are handed over, stabilised and performed once live. You'll make sure new technology launches safely and runs reliably. You'll also manage suppliers, protect service performance and make sure our automation investment keeps paying back.

This is a high impact role for someone who loves the pace of a 24/7 operation and wants to shape how automation is run across multiple sites. You'll report to the Head of Facilities Management, Operations and Systems and work closely with senior stakeholders across the business.

What you'll be doing day to day
• Leading the mobilisation and early life stabilisation of new automated logistics assets, taking them safely from project delivery into business as usual.
• Providing operational oversight across multiple automated sites, setting consistent standards, deployment strategies and recovery approaches.
• Acting as the primary link with automation suppliers, holding them to account on KPIs, SLAs, milestones, commissioning, testing and operational readiness.
• Leading automation contract renewals and supplier governance with Procurement, challenging performance and commercial proposals to make sure contracts deliver value and resilience.
• Owning automation budgeting, forecasting and financial management, and prioritising annual and multi year capital and operating investment against risk, asset condition and business need.
• Building and maintaining a rolling five year asset lifecycle and refurbishment plan, spotting obsolescence, reliability and capacity risks early.
• Identifying, prioritising and governing improvements across mechanical, electrical, controls and software systems to boost safety, reliability, performance and cost effectiveness.
• Providing out of hours leadership for major incidents. You'll coordinate site teams, suppliers and senior stakeholders for rapid recovery, and use asset, incident and supplier data to drive better decisions.

What experience you'll bring (essential skills)
• A strong Facilities Management and/or automation background, with experience in a 24/7 logistics or industrial automation environment.
• Demonstrable experience of site set up and mobilisation, including defining and running performance frameworks, reporting and governance.
• Experience managing multiple service providers, and handling incidents, escalations and supplier performance at pace.
• Commercial awareness, including a solid understanding of service contracts, service level agreements and cost drivers.
• A methodical, analytical approach to decision making under pressure, with clear ownership during mobilisation, stabilisation and incidents.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including confidence updating senior leaders during live incidents.
• The ability to challenge suppliers constructively and drive corrective action.

The Fraud Investigation Manager protects Argos and its customers by leading the day-to-day investigation of suspected and confirmed fraud. Lead complex end-to-end investigations into suspected internal and external fraud, ensuring evidence is gathered, assessed, recorded, retained and shared objectively, confidentially and lawfully.
Analyse ecommerce transactions, customer accounts, payment activity, device and channel behaviour, promotions, refunds, fulfilment journeys and linked intelligence to identify patterns, connected cases and emerging fraud methods.
Coordinate investigations that cross Argos Digital, Stores, Contact Centres, Logistics, Payments, Finance, Technology, People, Legal, Loss Prevention and Nectar, establishing clear ownership and timely actions.
Produce clear investigation strategies, evidence packs, case reports and risk summaries for the Fraud Risk Manager and relevant decision-makers, setting out findings, impact, root causes, control gaps and recommended action.
Support appropriate criminal, civil, disciplinary and asset-recovery outcomes by providing well-evidenced recommendations and working with law enforcement, payment providers, external agencies and specialist partners where required.
Use investigation findings and trend analysis to recommend improvements to ecommerce controls, fraud-detection rules, screening activity, customer journeys and operational processes, balancing fraud prevention with customer experience.
Maintain effective case governance, record keeping and reporting, ensuring investigation activity is timely, proportionate, auditable and compliant with relevant law, data protection and information-sharing requirements.
Share learning from cases and emerging online fraud trends, providing practical guidance that helps Argos and Nectar teams recognise risk, escalate concerns and prevent further loss.

Strong analytical capability, with the ability to interpret transaction, account, payment, device, fulfilment and behavioural data and connect information across systems and customer journeys.
Good working knowledge of relevant criminal and civil law, rules of evidence, data protection and lawful information-sharing in a commercial environment.
People-management skills, with the ability to organise case workloads, set standards, give constructive feedback and develop Investigation Specialists.
Experience of producing clear investigation plans, evidence packs, case reports and recommendations for operational, specialist and senior stakeholders.
Sound judgement and integrity, with the ability to manage sensitive information, assess competing risks, make balanced recommendations and escalate material concerns appropriately.
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to work across Digital, Technology, Payments, Retail, Logistics, People, Legal and external agencies.
Understanding of fraud-detection tools, screening rules or data-led investigative methods, with the ability to recommend practical control improvements.
Strong planning and organisational skills, with the resilience and flexibility to manage complex cases, changing priorities and travel to Argos locations when required.

At Sainsbury's, we're passionate about understanding our customers and using that understanding to create better experiences, make better decisions and deliver better outcomes. As Martech Manager - Data, Intelligence & Optimisation, you'll play a key role in helping us do exactly that.

Working across Marketing, Loyalty, Product, Engineering, Retail Media, Analytics and Data teams, you'll help unlock the value of our customer data and turn insight into action. You'll lead the evolution of our customer intelligence capabilities, helping colleagues better understand customer behaviour, improve marketing effectiveness and identify new opportunities to create value for both customers and the business.
This role isn't about owning data platforms or reporting dashboards. It's about helping the organisation make smarter decisions, fostering a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement, and ensuring we get the maximum value from the data, technology and capabilities available to us.
You'll be at your best in this role if you're curious, customer-focused and enjoy bringing together people, insight and technology to solve complex challenges.

What I need to do

Customer Data & Audience Strategy
• Help shape and evolve our customer data and audience capabilities to support business objectives and customer needs.
• Work with teams across Marketing, Loyalty, Retail Media, Product and Technology to improve how customer data is understood, governed and activated.
• Support the ongoing development of our Customer Data Platform (CDP) and audience management capabilities.

Customer Identity
• Help create a more connected understanding of our customers across channels and touchpoints.
• Work with Data, Product and Technology teams to ensure customer information is trustworthy, accessible and usable.

Data Enrichment & Customer Understanding
• Identify opportunities to improve customer understanding through internal and external data sources.
• Help teams develop richer audience insights and stronger segmentation approaches.

Measurement & Performance Insight
• Work with stakeholders to establish clear measurement frameworks and success metrics across Martech initiatives.
• Support consistent performance reporting and insight generation across the organisation.

Attribution & Marketing Effectiveness
• Improve our ability to understand how marketing activity contributes to customer and business outcomes.
• Work closely with Analytics, Media, Retail Media and Marketing teams to improve decision making and investment effectiveness.

Experimentation & Optimisation
• Champion a culture of testing, learning and continuous improvement.
• Help teams design and measure experiments that improve customer experiences and business performance.

AI Enablement & Innovation
• Identify opportunities to leverage AI and emerging technologies across customer intelligence, audience management, optimisation and decision making.

Customer Intelligence
• Ensure data and insight are accessible, understandable and actionable.
• Improve the organisation's ability to understand customer behaviour, performance drivers and future opportunities.

Team Leadership
• Lead and develop a high-performing team of Martech specialists.
• Create an environment where people can learn, grow and do their best work.

Success measures
Success in this role will be reflected through:
• Improved customer data quality and trust.
• Increased audience scalability and utilisation.
• Greater adoption of customer intelligence capabilities.
• Improved measurement consistency and maturity.
• Stronger marketing effectiveness and optimisation outcomes.
• Increased experimentation and learning across teams.
• Practical adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.
• Clear business value generated through data and insight.
• Strong stakeholder confidence in decision making.
• Improved understanding of customer behaviour and performance drivers.

What I need to show
• A genuine curiosity about customers and what drives their behaviour.
• The ability to balance analytical thinking with commercial understanding.
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
• Confidence translating complex information into clear and actionable insight.
• A passion for continuous improvement and learning.
• The ability to bring people together around data, evidence and opportunity.
• Strategic thinking combined with a pragmatic approach to delivery.
• Comfort working through ambiguity and bringing clarity to complex challenges.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to tell compelling stories through data and insight.

What I need to know
• Customer Data Platforms and audience management approaches.
• Customer identity and data governance principles.
• Analytics, measurement and performance frameworks.
• Attribution and marketing effectiveness methodologies.
• Experimentation and optimisation techniques.
• AI and emerging customer intelligence capabilities.
• Data-driven decision making in complex organisations.
• Product, engineering and agile delivery environments.

Essential Criteria

• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
• Experience of data-driven decision making in complex organisations.
• Experience of customer data platforms and audience management approaches.
• Knowledge of analytics, measurement and performance frameworks.
• Team management and leadership experience

Merchandiser - Seasonal - Fixed Term
We’re recruiting for a fixed term, 6 month contract within Seasonal and have an exciting Merchandiser opportunity within the Lesiure team. In this role, you’ll be right at the centre of how we plan, build and deliver ranges that truly connect with our customers. You’ll shape decisions, improve stock flow and influence the commercial direction of your category, working closely with buyers, suppliers and cross‑functional partners to drive performance. If you bring a merchandising background and want to play a key role in how our ranges come to life across all channels, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a team that values product, pace and customer insight. We are open to a secondment.

What You’ll Do
In this role, you’ll take ownership of delivering a customer‑led merchandising strategy for your category, ensuring we build balanced and commercial ranges. You’ll use data, trends and customer insight to inform decisions, manage budgets and understand what truly drives performance. You’ll work closely with Buying, Supply Chain, Retail and suppliers to keep stock flowing, optimise availability, and deliver to key milestones in the critical path. You’ll review performance regularly, identifying risks and opportunities that help shape trade conversations, planning cycles and future ranges. From forecasting and trading to supporting great product decisions, you’ll be at the heart of bringing standout ranges to our customers.
Who You Are
You’re someone with a passion for product and a natural curiosity about what makes customers buy. You bring experience in merchandising, ideally within general merchandise and you’re confident working with data to guide your thinking. You enjoy collaborating with buyers, suppliers and wider teams, using your communication skills to bring clarity and drive aligned decisions. You’re organised, proactive and thrive in a fast‑moving retail environment where you can influence results and see your work come to life in‑store. Above all, you care about delivering great customer experiences and want to develop your career in a team that values creativity, pace and teamwork.
Essential Criteria
• Previous merchandising experience
• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with data
• Experience delivering results to target as an individual and as part of a team
• Comfortable working under pressure in a fast‑moving retail environment
• Ability to influence and build strong relationships with key stakeholders
• Highly organised with strong planning and problem‑solving capabilities
• Customer‑focused with a positive, collaborative approach
• Strong Excel skills

You’ll split your time between home and Coventry, coming into the office when it matters most for collaboration and business needs.

Why this role matters

The People Partner will ensure the successful delivery of our people plans, this includes people development interventions, change / transformation projects and cyclical people activity. 

Putting our colleagues first, the role holder will work with the Senior People Partners to help design, implement and embed a wide variety of people change initiatives and cyclical activity (such as talent reviews, bonus and pay review, peak recruitment), creating a great colleague & line manager experience.   

Hybrid: London SSC and Home.

What I am accountable for

• Work with relevant stakeholders and People Centres of Expertise to design, implement and help embed the cyclical activity within the people plan, creating a great colleague & line manager experience. 

• Consulting and communicating with a variety of stakeholders to gain insight and buy in into cyclical processes. 

• Working with your peer group to maximise the effectiveness and efficiency of the wider team in delivery of people plans.  

• Owning and effectively planning cyclical talent and reward activity. 

• Successful delivery of people plan activity within agreed timescales 

• Working closely with the Senior People Partner to support the delivery of the wider People Plan and business transformation projects as required. 

• Help to manage risks and overcome issues that prevent the project/s or work from being successful 

• Analyse data to support development of the people plan / track and monitor progress 

• Provide support as required to organisational effectiveness and design project delivery 

• Build effective relationships with business stakeholders, peer group and CoE’s, to enable delivery of divisional and functional people plans. 

• Works effectively with others to drive efficiencies or economy of scales within our model – “Country before club” mentality, minimising cottage industries and driving consistency across division. 

What I Need to Know
• Relevant combination of people partner knowledge skills and experience or CIPD Level 5 - essential 
• Take full accountability for issues through to resolution - essential 
• Ability to identify opportunities to make the way we work simpler or looks for ways of improving service in the team. Encourages others to deliver results by making decisions and trying new approaches. - essential 
• Strong team working and collaboration skills, working with others to solve business problems, and finding the most effective and efficient ways of delivering – essential 
• Proven track record of delivery in equivalent roles within a fast-paced, complex, commercial organisations – essential 
• Experience of collaboratively delivering people plans - essential 
• Experience tracking and monitoring project, programme or initiative progress, and flagging when things are behind schedule - preferable 
• Experience with project management methodology / governance / working in an agile environment. - preferable 
• Ability to consume and analyse data – essential 
• Learning agility - essential

job_title: People Services and Right to Work Manager
job_description:
Why this role matters
You’ll be responsible for the effective delivery of Argos People Services operations, ensuring colleagues and leaders receive accurate, timely and consistent support across core people processes. Alongside this broader service focus, you’ll lead Argos compliance with Right to Work legislation, ensuring processes are completed accurately and on time. You will lead a team to manage operational services and complex cases, guide colleagues on the execution of our procedures, and drive continuous improvement across both in-house and BPO (Business process outsourcer) -delivered services. As the subject matter expert for People Services and RTW, you’ll be the primary contact point with the Home Office, keeping up to date with legislative changes and translating them into clear, effective Argos and BPO processes. 
You’ll oversee service performance, customer experience, assurance and audit activity across the BPO and in-house People Services teams, using insight and service measures to identify risks, resolve recurring issues and improve colleague outcomes. You’ll develop and monitor control frameworks, supported by the People Admin, and work closely with the Head of People Transformation & People Services on service governance, operational priorities and the responsible use of colleague data. You’ll attend Data Clinic and advocate good practice in the use and protection of colleague data.
Location: London or Coventry (Hybrid) 

What I am accountable for 
• Lead, manage, motivate and develop the People Services and RTW team 
• Lead the effective end-to-end delivery of People Services operations, ensuring services are accessible, responsive, accurate and consistent for colleagues and leaders 
• Own service performance across in-house and BPO delivery, setting clear standards and using service measures, colleague feedback and operational insight to improve outcomes 
• Partner with People teams, leaders, Technology and service providers to simplify processes, resolve recurring service issues and deliver continuous improvement across the colleague lifecycle 
• Ensure operational priorities, service risks, demand and capacity are understood and managed through effective governance, escalation and planning 
• Attend periodic colleague data clinic, providing guidance and advice as the SME as well as completing relevant actions and follow up 
• Work closely with the Privacy team to support the investigation of colleague data breaches 
• Review and approve colleague data transfer requests 
• Monitor the use and governance of colleague data 
• Prepare colleague data governance reports for DGC 
• Ensure the business are aware of how to use colleague data, linking in with Privacy team 
• Support with educating People team colleagues and the broader business in the importance of good data governance and protection processes 
• Oversight of audit activities, aligning with Head of People Transformation & People Services for review and sign off 
• Act as audit liaison for all fieldwork activities, supported by the HR Assurance Lead and HR Assurance Administrator. 
• Monitor effectiveness of control frameworks, supported by HR Assurance Lead and HR Assurance Administrator 
• Oversight of all monitoring and evidencing of BPO activity 
• Oversight of user access reviews and approving new user access requests 
• Ensure that BPO RTW processes are aligned to current RTW legislation 
• Engage with Tech to develop and manage solutions that support RTW processes 
• Work closely with Ops Admin for review and final sign-off on: 
• Case management of errors and potential fraudulent documents 
• Skilled worker visa applications and reporting 

What I need to know 
• Strong knowledge of People Services operating models and end-to-end colleague lifecycle processes, with experience of leading high-quality operational service delivery 
• Experience of managing service performance, customer experience and continuous improvement using operational data, service measures and feedback 
• Knowledge of Right to Work legislation, and its application in a large organisation 
• Strong understanding of data protection legislation relating to colleague data, in an operational environment 
• Experience of building and monitoring control frameworks and supporting audit activities 
• Good knowledge of HR operational processes and HR systems and the risk profile associated with those activities 
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate complexity simply across a range of stakeholders 
• Good planning skills, with an up to 12-month outlook 
• Analytical problem solving, able to use data to identify issues and find solutions 
• Strong relationship management skills with the ability to influence at senior manager level 
• Desirable experience of working with a BPO or similar outsourced provider in delivering service

Why this role matters
The Policy Manager leads people policy across the business, ensuring legal compliance and alignment with our business and people strategy. You will manage day-to-day policy activity and develop policy and broader reward strategy with the Head of Reward, Policy and Performance. You will ensure policies are clearly communicated, effectively implemented and inclusive, accessible and aligned with our valued behaviours.
Hybrid between any Argos Support Office and Home.

What I am accountable for 
• Develop future-fit, legally compliant people policies that reflect our business direction and values, ensuring consistency across Argos while accommodating population differences where appropriate. 
• Partner with subject matter experts, including Reward, Retail Operations/Labour, Safety, Government Relations and Asia People teams, to develop and maintain an organisation-wide policy strategy, measuring its effectiveness against business objectives. 
• Identify, assess and track policy risks and issues, judging business impacts, recommending pragmatic solutions and supporting resolution or escalation. 
• Provide ER and policy expertise, working with Union Relationship teams to resolve complex policy-related ER issues and Trade Union queries. 
• Identify and embed simpler people policies and procedures. Work with subject matter experts to keep policies, procedures and processes coherent and seamless. 
• Review and update policies and guidance, creating documentation where needed to support our People and business strategy, Valued Behaviours and Argos Performance Expectations. 
• Own and maintain the policy framework and internal governance, ensuring consistent development, approval, application and communication across Argos, with timely, controlled updates, including legislative changes. 
• Produce reports and Board papers on internal and external policy developments, sharing insights and recommendations with stakeholders up to Board Director level. 
• Build strong relationships with People Partners, the wider People team and business stakeholders, involving them in scoping new policies and updates. 
• Monitor external policy trends, best practice, employment law and economic factors to anticipate business impacts and recommend responses. 
• Partner with Performance and Development teams to align manager and colleague tools and learning with people policies, build manager advocacy, and deliver workshops and training on HR policies and best practice. 
• Work with Ask HR, People Operations, ER, Payroll and Sainsbury’s Tech to identify third-party and internal system impacts of policy changes and develop solutions. 

What I need to know 
• Strong knowledge and experience of people policies and HR, particularly ER, IR, Diversity, Equity & Inclusion and employment law. 
• Excellent written and verbal communication, making complex topics clear to all audiences. 
• Sound judgement and problem-solving, balancing operational, commercial and colleague needs, including where no policy or precedent exists. 
• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, identifying opportunities and translating strategy into action. 
• Strong personal impact, resilience and ability to influence diverse stakeholders up to Director level.
• Experience managing multiple policies, people topics and projects across different populations in a fast-changing environment. 
• Trade Union experience is advantageous. 
• Emotional intelligence and strong interpersonal skills, building effective relationships across divisions and with external partners.
• Ability to work under pressure and adapt to challenges, prioritising changing deadlines and requirements with confidence, drive and enthusiasm.

Why join us

Joining Sainsbury's as the Post Production Manager for Argos offers a unique opportunity to lead the development of a new post-production arm dedicated to transforming high-quality content for diverse channels such as E-commerce, Marcom, PR, and Social. Collaborating closely with in-house studios and creative teams, you will play a pivotal role in enhancing and delivering assets. With a focus on automation, AI, CGI integration, and operational excellence, this role provides a platform to drive innovation, mentor teams, and shape the future of post-production workflows in a dynamic and inclusive environment.

What you'll do

As the Post Production Manager at Argos, you will lead the new post-production arm to edit and transform high-quality content for E-commerce, Marcom, PR, and Social channels, in collaboration with in-house Studios, production, and creative teams. Your role entails ensuring content, retouching, and edit guidelines align with brand objectives, meeting KPIs, SLAs, and operational targets. With a keen eye for detail and expertise in creative retouching and edit techniques, you will drive automation initiatives, onboard new AI and CGI suppliers, lead post-production strategy, mentor team members, develop business cases for new partnerships, and implement workflows leveraging AI and CGI technologies. Your success will be measured by successful supplier integration, team adoption, metrics tracking, early wins delivery, and streamlined post-production workflows, making a significant impact on content creation and delivery processes.

Who you are

As a Post Production Manager at Argos, you are a dynamic and strategic leader with a strong background in post-production operations and asset management workflows. Your experience in creative agency or in-house studio environments, coupled with your proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, enables you to drive the implementation of new CGI and AI partnerships, streamline post-production workflows, and lead cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality content for E-commerce, Marcom, PR, and Social channels. Your ability to innovate, communicate effectively, and foster collaboration across technical and creative teams positions you to drive impactful change, optimise operational processes, and ensure the successful integration of new technologies to enhance Argos's brand objectives and meet operational targets.

Essential criteria

Experience in post‑production operations and asset management workflows – you’ll be the go‑to expert across retouching, editing, CGI and delivery.

Demonstrable project management skills, including planning, reporting and coordinating teams to deliver at pace.

Previous experience in a creative agency or in‑house studio environment with experience of how content flows end to end.

Working knowledge of Adobe Workfront and Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems.

Experience onboarding and managing large suppliers, ideally across AI, CGI, retouching or editing.

Hands‑on experience using or implementing automated production tools or systems.

Leadership and mentoring experience, supporting Editors, Retouchers and Post‑Producers.

Why join us?
Sustainability is a big part of how we’re shaping the future of Argos, and this is an opportunity to be right at the heart of it.
As our Sustainability Lead, you’ll be our carbon specialist, leading our carbon programme and helping turn our environmental ambitions into meaningful action. What you’ll do
You’ll lead our carbon reduction programme across Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, translating our commitments into clear plans, targets and practical actions that can make a real difference.
A big part of your role will be bringing together carbon, operational, supplier and product data to understand our emissions profile, where our biggest opportunities are and where we need to focus next. You’ll monitor and drive progress towards our net zero ambitions, supporting carbon reporting, climate disclosures and wider sustainability requirements.
Collaboration will be key. You’ll partner with teams across Argos to identify and deliver opportunities to reduce emissions and embed decarbonisation into the way we work and make decisions. You’ll also work with suppliers and external partners to help address emissions across our wider value chain, particularly Scope 3.
You’ll help shape the policies, standards and guidance that underpin our approach to carbon, keeping an eye on emerging climate and carbon requirements and making sure risks and opportunities are understood and acted on.

We’re looking for someone who combines strong carbon expertise with the confidence to bring people with them. You’ll be comfortable working with emissions data and technical detail, but equally able to step back, tell the story behind the numbers and influence stakeholders across a complex organisation.
Essential criteria:
• A professional qualification or equivalent experience in Sustainability, Environmental Management, Geography, Environmental Science, Carbon Management or a related discipline.
• Experience delivering carbon reduction, carbon accounting or decarbonisation programmes within a complex organisation, supply chain or product-led business.
• Strong knowledge of carbon accounting principles, including Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, climate disclosure requirements, science-based targets and supplier emissions data.
• Strong project and programme management skills, with experience coordinating multiple priorities, workstreams and stakeholders.
• The ability to analyse, interpret and communicate carbon and emissions data, including operational, product and supplier data, to identify emissions hotspots, risks, reduction opportunities and track performance.
• Experience developing or supporting carbon or climate-related policies, standards, guidance or business processes.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence teams, suppliers and external partners.
• Experience identifying and managing carbon, climate or decarbonisation risks and opportunities using sound judgement and established governance processes.

Experience working with suppliers, industry groups or external organisations on Scope 3 emissions, supplier decarbonisation or product carbon would be a real advantage. Exposure to carbon or sustainability training and engagement, budget management or business case development would also be useful, as would membership of, or an interest in, a relevant professional body such as ISEP.

Hello. We’re Severn Trent and we think water is wonderful. And we’re pretty keen on people too.
 
 
24 hours a day, 365 days a year we serve 4.8 million households and business across the heart of the UK. Each cuppa drank, each toilet flushed is only possible because of the brilliant team members working across our patch.
 
 
We welcome people from all walks of life and celebrate individuality. We know diverse minds, experiences and backgrounds help us to learn and better serve our customers and the communities where they live.
 
 
If you want to do more because you care, we’d love to talk to you. There really is something for everyone here.
 
 
Here at Severn Trent, we take pride in knowing we come to work each day and help make a difference to our customers, working together with our colleagues to solve problems as soon as we can. Our Customer Advisor role sits at the heart of this value with the opportunity to really make a difference to our customers. 
 
 
 
EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW  
 
 
We’re looking for part-time Customer Advisors to work within our Operations Team in Coventry.
 
 
Central to this is being there for our customers when they need us the most, 365 days a year. Whether they are without water or find they have wastewater where they don’t want it, we need our Customer Service Specialists to listen, support and guide our customers through their questions from simple queries to complex complaints. Every conversation is different.
 
 
Supporting customers who might be anxious or annoyed is never easy, but it does feel good to help reassure people, diffuse problems, and explain clearly what we’re going to do to help.
 
 
Our water is vital to our customers, so we need to be around when they need us. 
 
This role is perfect for anyone looking for greater flexibility whilst still being part of something meaningful. Working Monday to Friday, 16:15 to 19:15, you'll enjoy a schedule that can fit around family life, caring responsibilities, studies or other commitments, whilst still giving you the opportunity to make a real difference for our customers every single day.
 
We are currently recruiting for you to start with us on Monday 18th January, where you will then go through a 5 week training programme (Monday to Friday, 16:15 to 19:15). This training will give you all the tools, knowledge and confidence you need to thrive in your new role. 
 
Please note, there is free onsite parking for this shift pattern. 
 
Your key accountabilities in helping us will be, talking to customers over the phone, helping us resolve queries quickly, first time. Being a first-class communicator with the skills to build a rapport with customers, as well as our internal and external departments. 
 
 
 
WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE ROLE 
 
 
Customer service or contact centre experience would be ideal, but If you have a natural flair for communicating, can empathise with customers and see how their problem could be affecting their homes, their health or their loved-ones, you’ll love this role.
 
 
We also have a comprehensive training programme that you’ll go through when you start, which will help develop your problem-solving skills and give you the full knowledge you’ll need of Severn Trent so you can support our customers.
 
 
The right skills and experience are important. But if you have the right character, positivity and a caring attitude we want to talk to you, too.
 
 
We welcome people from all walks of life and celebrate individuality as we know diverse minds, experiences and backgrounds help us to learn and better serve our communities. We want people who show up and get involve. Those who are ready to be part of something bigger and who want to make a difference because they care.
 
 
 
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU  
 
 
Working here isn’t just a job. You can build a career at Severn Trent. We’ll reward you for it, too. We have a range of benefits that recognise great work, and award-winning training to help you reach your potential. And we’ll also help you play your part in looking after the environment and the communities where we live.
 
 
With that in mind, here are just some of our favourite's perks that you’ll get being part of the Seven Trent family:
 

A salary of £11,146.90 (pro rata) with a company pay increase each year
25 days holiday + bank holidays (pro rata) and the ability to buy/sell up to 5 days per year
Annual bonus scheme (of up to £1,500, subject to eligibility and pro rata where applicable)
Family-friendly policies (including a year off fully paid maternity and adoption leave)Leading pension scheme, we'll double your contribution (up to 15% when you contribute 7.5%)
Sharesave, the chance to buy Severn Trent plc shares at a discounted rate
Dedicated training and development with our Academy
Two paid volunteering days per year
Free onsite parking for this shift pattern

 
 
 
 
WHAT’S NEXT 
 
 
We can’t wait to hear from you. 
 
Before you apply, you’ll need an updated copy of your CV and about five minutes to spare.
 
And if your curiosity has peaked and you're wanting to find out even more, search #LifeAtSevernTrent on social media.
 
Ps. we’ll always let you know the outcome of your application after the closing date - so keep an eye on your phone and emails!

**This Opportunity** 

Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work. AI-native transformation is the operating priority for the business, and the Applied AI team owns it: the platform every team's AI work runs on, the pattern for how a function's critical workflows move onto agents, and the measurement of whether it worked. Individual AI adoption is already high across the company. The next stage is redesigning functions so that agents run the recurring work and people set the goals and judge the output. 

You are the first Forward Deployed Engineer on the team, reporting to the Senior Director of Applied AI. The team is also hiring a principal engineer to own the platform and an Applied AI engineer to embed with our Growth team. The Senior Director you report to still ships code. You are the one who moves between functions. You embed with one function at a time alongside its leader and the people who do the work by hand today, map how the work actually runs, build the agentic workflow that takes it on, tune it with the experts until they trust it, and hand it back to the function to own. Then you move to the next one. 

You sit with our major business functions, one at a time. The Senior Director of Applied AI and the function's leader choose each engagement, and your workflow maps are the evidence they choose from. Priorities will shift as the transformation moves, and the role is designed for that. 

This is the forward deployed model applied inside our own company. You write the code, and you also do the discovery a consultant would. The function's leader owns the decision to change how their team works. You own the engineering and the pattern. You'll spend as much time listening to someone walk through a task they do by hand every week as you will writing the agents that run it, and the deliverable is a function that works differently, understands why, and can run what you built. 

**What you will own** 

- The workflow map. You sit with the people who do the work and leave with how it actually runs today: where work enters, what moves between steps, who says yes, and what "good" means. It is the first thing you do in every engagement.
- The case for whether to build. Before anything gets built, you bring the evidence from the map and make the case for whether the workflow is worth moving onto agents, including when the answer is that it does not need AI. The decision sits with the function's leader and the Senior Director; the evidence is yours.
- The build. You design and build agentic workflows on Snowplow's shared factory framework, which Applied AI runs: declared queues and gates, focused agents, and a central ledger that records every agent run. Every factory you build is compatible with every other one, in any function.
- Approval gates. You decide where the agent acts on its own, where it proposes and a person approves, and what gets recorded so anyone can see what the agent did and why. The people in the function keep the judgment. The agents take the rest.
- Agent readiness. You make the function's knowledge, systems of record, and quality bar explicit enough for agents to work from. Often this is the real work, and the agents are the easy part.
- The last twenty percent. Most of the work comes after the prototype: reliability, edge cases, evaluation, and a team choosing it over the way they worked before. You tune the output alongside the domain experts and encode their judgment into checks that hold after they step back.
- The handoff. You train the function to run and evolve what you built, then leave. Where an Applied AI engineer is embedded in the function, you hand it to them. Success is a workflow still running months after you have moved on, owned by people who are not you. After the handoff you stay available: when the function sees a problem or a way to improve the workflow, you coordinate it with the embedded and platform engineers rather than taking it back, and you help build the platform those workflows run on.
- The pattern itself. You own how a workflow moves from map to agents to handoff, written down so the next engagement starts from it. What you build also goes back into the shared framework as reference implementations. The second factory in any function should be cheaper than the first.

- Built with LLMs in production. You have designed agents or agentic workflows that run real work, with prompts, tools, evaluation, and the failure modes that come with them. You know the difference between a demo and something a team relies on every day, and you have done the unglamorous work of closing that gap.
- An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation, or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.

This Opportunity

Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work, and the Applied AI team owns Firn, the single data and AI platform the whole company runs on. Firn already gives people and agents the same governed tools over our Snowflake warehouse through an MCP gateway, routes every model call through one LLM gateway with tracing, runs agentic workflows on a factory framework with a ledger that records every run, and holds the skills catalog the company draws on. Most of the company uses it every day. The platform is at its beginning, and the next stage is to expand it until it holds the company's commercial intelligence and lets agents act on it safely.

You are the principal engineer who leads that expansion. The first engagement is Go-to-Market, full time for about six months. Our buyers research with AI agents now, and reaching them means using our own data and AI to decide which accounts and people to engage, with what, and learning from every experiment. The GTM teams have built a lot: daily account and engagement scoring, signal feeds from Apollo, Vector and reo.dev, an always-on outbound engine, a paid-media loop, a curated GTM knowledge base, and the integrations between them. Much of it was built by operational teams to get results fast, and it did. You design how those services come onto Firn, unify and modernize them, build the agents and tools and learning loops on top, and make the whole thing production grade.

This is a principal role. You report to the Senior Director of Applied AI, who still ships code, and work as a peer. Marketing, Sales, Account Management and Partnerships are the platform's customers and set their own priorities. You decide how it gets built and whether it is sound. Once the GTM services run without you, they stay yours as their owner and most of your time goes to what Snowplow needs next.

What you will own

- The GTM intelligence engine on Firn. The data and AI that decide who we engage and with what, and that learn from the outcome of every action. You design it with our data engineers as a set of platform services with several internal customers, and you bring the GTM services that exist today onto the same foundation.
- Agents and tools. The agents that run GTM work and the tools people and other agents call, built on the factory framework with review steps and evaluations as the standard shape, so every agent on the platform can be trusted and inspected the same way.
- Platform architecture. The MCP gateway, LLM gateway, tracing, factory framework and ledger, and how they grow to hold more of the company's work. You decide what is built, what is bought, and what is retired.
- Production grade. Version control, CI, alerting and recovery, cost visibility, documentation, and handover for every service on the platform, including the ones that arrive from operational teams. You set the bar and you make it visible to the teams that depend on it.
- Logic as code. Rules that today live inside individual tools move into versioned code on the platform, where agents can read them and engineers can test them, and the tools become endpoints the platform drives.
- Learning loops. Every action the platform takes is recorded and tied to its outcome, so people and agents can see what worked and the next action is better. Metric definitions sit with our data engineers; the instrumentation that applies them is yours.
- Eval and tracing infrastructure. The harness the embedded and forward deployed engineers use to prove their agents work. You own the tooling; they own the checks.
- The technical bar and the roadmap. You set the engineering bar for the Applied AI team and own the platform roadmap, and you keep the long view of the platform at all times.

We would love to hear from you if you have

- Years of production software behind you. You have designed, shipped and run systems other teams depend on, in Python or TypeScript, with SQL, CI/CD and cloud infrastructure as everyday tools. This is a principal role and the bar is set there.
- Built LLM systems that real work runs on. Agents with tools, MCP servers, gateways, tracing and evaluation, and the failure modes that come with them. You can say what broke in production and what you changed.
- Platform instincts. You have built systems other people depend on, whether internal teams or customers, through interfaces you designed, and you know the difference between a platform and a pile of integrations.
- Data platform fluency. Snowflake or an equivalent warehouse, dbt, data contracts, and the pipelines that move warehouse data into SaaS tools and back.
- Operational discipline. Alerting, recovery, runbooks and cost tracking are things you add before anyone asks, and you have run systems where that discipline mattered.
- Judgment about where an agent belongs. You can tell which decisions should be deterministic code, which an agent can make, and which should stay with a person, and you can explain the reasoning to a non-engineer.
- An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, agent or tool you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
- Comfort with internal customers who are not engineers. You can sit with a growth director, a seller or a marketer, take a requirement, and hold the line on how it gets built. No sales or marketing background is needed.
- Technical direction without a title. You have set direction for a platform that other engineers followed because the design was right, not because they reported to you.

How we hire for this role

The interview process includes a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup, and a design conversation on a system we run today. We work this way ourselves, and you are welcome to use AI when applying.

- Discovery that finds the real problem. You ask the questions that uncover what a prospect is trying to achieve, then connect it to what Snowplow does.

- Competitive situations. You position Snowplow honestly against the alternatives a prospect is weighing up, including building it themselves.
- The voice of the field. You bring what you hear from prospects back to Product, Marketing and the wider team so we keep getting sharper.

- Experience selling into retail, media, iGaming or financial services

Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.

We think AI is what makes the problem solvable; better software alone wasn't enough. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here https://www.sona.ai/careers.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Sona's Customer Success function is being built from the ground up. $Millions of ARR is moving from Implementation to Customer Success, we're heading into our first year of renewals at scale, and there's meaningful seat expansion across the base. We need CSMs who can shape what good looks like, not operate inside a playbook someone else wrote.

You'll own a book of around 20-25 enterprise accounts across social care, hospitality and retail, partnering with Support, Product and Sales to own the post-live customer experience end to end. Some of the accounts you'll inherit are in difficult places, so you'll be rebuilding trust, holding rooms independently and driving outcomes in ambiguity.

We're a high-performance team. Everyone holds an important seat and is expected to perform at an elite level. We have each other's backs, we assume good intent, and we have zero space for internal politics. If that's your default, you'll thrive here.

This is an on-site role. Four days a week you'll be in our London office or out with customers, with one day working from home. Regular travel to customers across the UK is part of the job.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own senior customer relationships at Director level and above (Operations, Finance, HR), in person as well as over video, and act as the escalation point for your accounts

 - Run the QBR cadence and own renewals end to end, so the value case is made long before the renewal conversation

 - Drive proactive value work: account audits, surfacing unused functionality, and translating product usage into business outcomes

 - Progress seat upsells as customers grow, and flag wider expansion opportunities to AEs

 - Hold difficult conversations with diplomacy, including product feedback that isn't on the roadmap

 - Manage customer-side projects such as integrations and configuration changes, keeping status visible so customers always know where they stand

 - Help shape how Customer Success works at Sona, from health scoring to escalation




REQUIREMENTS

 - You've owned a book of enterprise SaaS accounts, whether as a CSM, Solutions Architect, Pre-Sales, Implementation Consultant or PM

 - You've held Director-level customer relationships independently and been accountable for the customer health that drives renewal

 - You're commercially fluent around NRR and value realisation, and treat accounts as long-term assets

 - You're confident in complex SaaS products: you can demo, discuss configuration trade-offs and translate capability into business value

 - You've worked in a scaleup where process was still being built

 - You use AI tools daily in your CS work and can point to specific workflows

 - You can disagree with a senior customer and keep the relationship intact

It’d be a bonus if you could bring

 - Hands-on experience with Planhat, Salesforce, or similar CS platforms

 - Track record of identifying and converting commercial expansion opportunities (seat upsells, module flags)




BENEFITS

 - Salary: £55,000 - £75,000

 - On-site working: 4 days a week in the London office or with customers, 1 day from home

 - Share options

 - 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

 - Extra day of leave for every year of service

 - Pension contributions matched up to 5%

 - Comprehensive health insurance

 - Enhanced parental leave & pay

 - Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

 - Annual team off-sites and quarterly socials

 - The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

 - Professional development budget

 - Unlimited free books

Note: this represents a typical benefits package for a UK-based, full-time employee. Exact details may vary based on location and employment type but we try to be as fair as possible to all of our team members. Please ask your contact in the Talent team to clarify the available benefits for you.

Summary:

Are you a data whiz who loves solving real-world problems? Do you want to play a critical role in tackling one of the biggest challenges in the water industry?

We are looking for a Leakage Data Analyst to join our Leakage Data Team in Snodland. The candidate will also be expected to spend 1-2 days a week in the Kent regional office near Detling.

This is an opportunity to apply your analytical expertise to complex and meaningful work. Leakage reduction is a fundamental part of South East Water’s overall strategy, and this role is integral to providing the analytical information that drives our strategic goals.

This role would work closely with the Kent regional leakage operations team to help target leakage using all available data. Alongside targeting of leakage, the successful candidate would be expected to perform area specific deep dives and investigations to help improve our overall understanding of the network to ensure more efficient identification of leakage. There will also be an element of regulatory reporting making this a great opportunity to begin a career in the water industry.

The Leakage Data team is expanding, meaning you’ll work with a wide range of data on exciting projects, including innovative techniques like satellite surveys, drone surveys, and dark fibre. We are dedicated to continuous improvement of our processes to ensure all components of the water balance are as accurate as possible.

You will need to be proficiency in the use of data manipulation tools. A bonus would be understanding of water networks but this can be learnt within the role. If you are driven by challenging projects and providing high-quality, granular insight, you will find this role both rewarding and crucial to ensuring we remain compliant and meet our team objectives.

Main responsibilities:

• Lead the regulatory reporting of leakage and the water balance, ensuring timely and accurate completion.
• Work within the Leakage Data Team as we develop a new system and methodology for leakage management and reporting.
• Provide analysis of Zonal and DMA nightline data to explain movements and trend analysis.
• Identify errors, trends, and unusual activity through data analysis.
• Receive, interpret, input, and update technical information to ensure the integrity of recorded information and record databases.
• Continuously improve processes and data to ensure all components of the water balance are as accurate as possible and readily available for timely reporting.
• Evaluate and analyse operational information and understand data integrity difficulties to resolve basic problems.
• Support the development of new systems and insight into leakage operations to enable field teams to work as efficiently as possible.
• Other duties may include: Supporting the roll-out of Smart Water Networks and interpreting the resulting data and alarms to reduce leakage and the impact of supply interruptions.

What you’ll need
Skills / Qualifications / Experience:

• Educated to a degree level, including some level of statistical analysis experience (e.g., an undergraduate module in statistics).
• A strong understanding of statistical analytics.
• Proficiency in data manipulation tools.
• An understanding of the component parts of regulatory reported leakage.
• The ability to find ways of solving or pre-empting problems
• A basic level of Structured Query Language (SQL) to efficiently retrieve, manipulate and clean large datasets from operational databases (e.g., asset management systems, SCADA systems).

Summary:

We are seeking an experienced and visionary Leakage Strategy Manager to lead the transformation, scaling, and delivery of advanced smart network solutions across our regional water infrastructure. In this pivotal leadership role, you will be responsible for defining and executing comprehensive leakage reduction and pressure management strategies that directly align with rigorous Ofwat performance commitments and long-term regulatory frameworks. Driving operational resilience and sustainable water balance, you will champion the integration of cutting-edge acoustic sensors, telemetry, and predictive data analytics to proactively detect, locate, and mitigate network losses. Working in close collaboration with capital delivery, field operations, and data science teams, you will establish a culture of continuous improvement, ensuring all leakage management activities are delivered safely, efficiently, and with minimal environmental impact.

To succeed in this role, you will bring an exceptional blend of technical water network expertise, robust commercial acumen, and proven strategic capability. You will manage substantial operational and capital budgets, driving commercial value and contractor performance while optimising end-to-end network efficiency. A confident communicator and influencer, you will engage across senior stakeholders, industry regulators, and technical specialists to communicate risk, report on statutory performance commitments, and justify future infrastructure investments. Main responsibilities:

• Strategy & Innovation: Leading the development and implementation of comprehensive leakage optimisation strategies and smart network technologies across the supply network. 
• Regulatory & Target Alignment: Aligning leakage operational plans with Ofwat regulatory performance commitments (AMP targets) to ensure compliance and avoid financial penalties. 
• Smart Infrastructure Deployment: Driving the integration of smart network technologies, acoustic logging, and pressure control into existing infrastructure to accelerate leak detection and response. 
• Performance & KPI Management: Managing leakage key performance indicators (KPIs) ensuring localised and region-wide reduction targets are consistently met. 
• Data Stewardship & Analytics: Overseeing network data governance, optimising flow/pressure data feeds, and leveraging predictive analytics to drive proactive maintenance and investment decisions. 
• Project & Scheme Governance: Developing, budgeting, and managing project plans for smart network installations, DMA maintenance, and targeted leakage schemes within defined financial guidelines. 
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborating with internal operational teams, asset management, and external service delivery contractors to ensure smooth implementation and operational alignment. 
• Health, Safety & Operational Risk: Embedding high Health & Safety standards across all strategy implementations and anticipating network risks to support operational contingency planning. 
• Business Transformation: Driving business-wide transformation through data-driven insights, emerging technology trials, and smart system innovations. 
• Evaluation & Reporting: Monitoring, evaluating and reporting performance outcomes to executive leadership, board committees and regulatory bodies as required.

You'll need:
Skills / Qualifications / Experience

• Degree or equivalent professional qualification/in-work training in engineering, water management, hydraulics or a related technical discipline. 
• Relevant professional accreditation (e.g., CEng, CIWEM) or safety management certifications (IOSH/NEBOSH) preferred.
Strategic thinking and leadership in implementing large-scale network optimisation and leakage reduction programmes. 
• In-depth understanding of water balance methodology, DMA (District Metered Area) design and network hydraulics (pressure management and flow analysis). 
• Advanced data analysis skills, with the ability to manage and interpret complex network data to guide regulatory reporting and operational decisions. 
• Commercial and financial acumen, with experience managing operational/capital budgets and monitoring contractor performance against KPIs. 
• Excellent communication, leadership and stakeholder management skills, with proven experience collaborating across operational, asset management and regulatory teams. 
• Strong technical acumen in leakage detection, smart metering, logging technologies and continuous network monitoring systems. 
• Proactive, safety-first and results-driven approach to project delivery and continuous operational improvement.
• Proven experience in smart networks, hydraulic management and/or leakage optimisation within the UK water industry. 
• Strong practical knowledge of Ofwat regulatory frameworks, AMP performance commitments, and regulatory data governance standards. 
• Significant experience as a strategic thinker implementing large-scale network optimisation and water efficiency schemes. 
• Extensive experience in managing and analysing complex data sets to guide strategic investment and daily operational performance. 
• Demonstrable experience in promoting Health & Safety management procedures and managing operational risk within field environments. 
• Proven track record of leading, influencing and communicating effectively across multidisciplinary teams and external delivery partners.

job_description:
We are seeking a business-minded, forward-looking HR leader to join our global Human Resources team as Head of EMEA HR and Strategic HR Business Partner. If you want to learn and shine at a company committed to you, then ISS STOXX might be the best move you’ll ever make.

As the Head of EMEA HR and Strategic HR Business Partner, you will lead our people agenda across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) and act as a thought partner to a member of our Executive Leadership Team (ELT). You will help that organisation become more effective, enabling faster delivery for our clients and supporting business growth. This part of the role is less about running HR processes and more about helping the business win through its people: how the organisation is designed, how it changes, how its leaders lead, and how its culture drives performance.

At the same time, you will modernise how HR is delivered in the region. As a key client of our global HR Shared Services, you will own the successful move of transactional and operational work out of the region and keep finding more that can move. You will also champion an AI-enabled way of working, so our team spends its time where it adds the most value: talent, leadership, organisational effectiveness and change.

As a member of the HR Leadership Team, you will help shape global HR strategy, not just execute it regionally. You will represent a key area of transformation for the company and are expected to be a significant contributor and team player.

Responsibilities

Regional leadership, employee relations and compliance
• Act as the senior point of escalation for HR in the region, with high-risk matters escalating to the CHRO, ensuring practices comply with local employment law and global policies.
• Lead, develop and inspire the EMEA HR team (approximately 15 people), and partner with regional specialists such as Talent Acquisition, building a business-focused team with strong succession.
• Manage day-to-day relationships with Works Councils, unions and employee representative bodies, and run consultation processes, with CHRO and Legal oversight on significant changes.
• Manage complex employee relations matters, balancing risk, fairness and business needs, working with Legal and external counsel as appropriate.
• Deliver annual performance, promotion and compensation cycles effectively in the region, in partnership with global Centres of Expertise and Shared Services.
• Design and lead change management for restructuring and integration, making sure change is well planned, well communicated and lands appropriately with employees.
• Help leaders build a high-performing, accountable culture aligned with our values, using engagement and culture insights to drive targeted action.
• Lead the people elements of mergers and acquisitions (M&A) across the region, including due diligence and post-deal integration.

Strategic business partnership
• Serve as the senior HR thought partner to an ELT member, bringing an independent, constructive point of view on people, organisation and culture.
• Help the client organisation operate more effectively and at greater pace, strengthening how it works with commercial and client-facing teams so solutions reach clients faster.
• Understand how the business makes money, its value streams, clients and priorities, and translate these into a clear people plan that the business owns.
• Coach and counsel senior leaders on leadership effectiveness, team dynamics, difficult decisions and how they shape our culture.
• Use people data (engagement, attrition, capability, productivity, cost) to diagnose issues early and recommend practical, evidence-based solutions.

HR operating model transformation: Shared Services and AI
• Own the success of the EMEA transition to global HR Shared Services: partner with the Shared Services leader on scope, sequencing, service levels and knowledge transfer, and hold the service to a high standard.
• Continually identify further activities that can move to Shared Services or be simplified, automated or removed; track and report the capacity released and how it is reinvested.
• Coach and lead the EMEA HR team through the shift from regional execution to the right mix of regional operations and business partnering.

Champion AI-enabled HR: identify high-value use cases, drive adoption across the team, and redesign processes rather than automate old ones.
• Act as a steward of the responsible use of AI in HR, in line with EU data protection and AI regulation and our governance framework.

HR Leadership Team
• Contribute to global HR strategy, policy and priorities, and take enterprise-wide ownership of selected initiatives.
• Partner closely with HR colleagues in the Americas and Asia-Pacific, and with Talent and Learning, Compensation, HR Systems and Analytics, Benefits, Talent Acquisition and Shared Services.

Qualifications

Education
• Degree in Human Resources, Business, Economics, Law or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Experience
• 15+ years of progressive HR experience, including significant senior experience partnering directly with executive-level leaders on strategy, organisation design and change in a complex, international, matrixed organisation.
• Proven record of moving an HR team from operational delivery to strategic business partnering, including moving work to Shared Services or a global capability centre, simplifying processes and adopting HR technology and AI.
• Experience leading restructuring, M&A integration and large-scale change across several European countries, including Works Council consultation.

Knowledge, skills and abilities
• Thorough working knowledge of employment law and practice across key EMEA markets.
• Business and financial acumen: reads a profit and loss statement, understands value streams and cost drivers, and makes people decisions that improve outcomes.
• Thought partnership and influence: confident, credible and willing to challenge senior leaders constructively.
• Organisation design and change leadership: structured, practical and focused on making the organisation simpler and more effective.
• Data and AI fluency: uses people analytics and AI tools to generate insight and productivity and leads others to do the same.
• Coaching: helps leaders grow their own effectiveness and lead their teams through change.
• Enterprise mindset: puts what is right for the whole company ahead of regional or functional interests.
• Fluent English required.

Nice to have
• Experience in financial services, financial data or technology.
• Organisation design, change or coaching accreditation.
• Experience with Workday and/or SAP SuccessFactors.

ISS-Corporate (ICS) is seeking an experienced Sustainability Product Manager to lead the development and evolution of our Sustainability Reporting and Carbon Accounting solutions. This role will be responsible for developing and executing the product strategy and roadmap for scalable SaaS solutions that enable corporations to measure, manage, and disclose sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions data. 
The Sustainability Product Manager will lead product planning and execution across both solutions, from strategy and market analysis through requirements, delivery, launch, and continuous improvement. The role will work closely with Development, Client Advisory, Sales, and Marketing to ensure that the solutions address customer needs, support regulatory requirements, and contribute to revenue and customer satisfaction goals.

The ideal candidate combines strong product management and leadership experience with an understanding of sustainability, enterprise SaaS, data-driven products, and the application of AI capabilities within software solutions.

Product Strategy and Leadership 
• Own the product strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle for the Sustainability Reporting and Carbon Accounting solutions. 
• Lead, support, and develop the Product Owner responsible for Carbon Accounting, ensuring clear objectives, accountability, and effective execution. 
• Establish priorities across both solutions based on customer needs, regulatory developments, commercial opportunities, and technical dependencies. 

Product Development & Delivery 
• Drive product development across Engineering, Data, Research, UX, Client Advisory, Sales, and Marketing. 
• Translate complex sustainability methodologies and customer needs into clear product requirements and priorities. 
• Guide the development of core capabilities across sustainability reporting, carbon accounting, data management, analytics, and auditability. 

Customers, Market & Regulation 
• Gather and prioritize customer and market requirements through research, client consultations, and user groups. 
• Monitor regulatory, technology, market, and competitive developments and translate relevant changes into product priorities. 
• Communicate product vision, roadmap, priorities, and progress clearly to internal and external stakeholders. 

Integration & Innovation 
• Drive the integration of Sustainability Reporting and Carbon Accounting with each other and with the broader ISS-Corporate platform. 
• Identify and prioritize opportunities to use AI and automation to improve data collection, processing, analytics, quality control, and user experience.

• Experience managing, coaching, or providing functional leadership to product professionals. 
• 4+ years of progressive experience in a corporate environment.

• Experience in sustainability reporting, carbon accounting, ESG, or regulated enterprise software is preferred. 
• Familiarity with AI/ML concepts and their application in enterprise software is desirable. 

Skills and Personal Attributes 

• Strong leadership skills and the ability to establish direction, priorities, and accountability. 
• Ability to translate complex methodologies and business needs into clear software requirements. 
• Excellent oral and written communication skills and the ability to build effective relationships. 
• Strong product management, market research, trend analysis, technical writing, and presentation skills.

• Ability to work effectively across global, diverse, and cross-functional teams.

job_description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The UK Financial Services sales team works with some of the largest and most important financial institutions in the UK. We help our users modernise their infrastructure, create better digital experiences for their customers, launch new products, and develop new sources of revenue.

As the banking expert within the UK Financial Services team, you will target net new enterprise business from a named account list comprising some of the UK’s largest Tier 1 banks. You will bring deep knowledge of the banking sector, help shape Stripe’s approach to the market, and navigate complex, highly regulated organisations to build relationships with senior stakeholders across business, technology, operations, risk, compliance, procurement, and finance.

If you’re motivated, smart, persistent, and a great teammate, we want to hear from you!

What you’ll do

The UK Financial Services sales team works across the financial services sector, helping leading institutions modernise legacy infrastructure, improve customer experiences, expand their digital capabilities, and identify new opportunities for growth.

As the banking expert within the team, you will develop new relationships within a named list of Tier 1 UK banks. You will identify high value use cases for Stripe, build compelling transformation and commercial cases, and lead complex opportunities from initial engagement through negotiation and close. You will also help strengthen our understanding of the banking market and shape how Stripe positions its products and capabilities with major banks.

If you’re motivated, smart, persistent, and a great teammate, we want to hear from you!

Responsibilities

• Own a named account list of Tier 1 UK banks and develop detailed account plans for winning and expanding business across complex organisations

• Act as the banking expert within the UK Financial Services team, sharing market insight and helping colleagues navigate the sector

• Own the full sales cycle, from initial outbound engagement and use case discovery through business case development, deal structuring, negotiation, and close

• Design and execute sales strategies suited to the extended decision making, budgeting, procurement, risk, and regulatory processes of large financial institutions
