The Story Engineers design and deliver live experiences that move people.

We work across museums, brand spaces, entertainment venues, and major events. The work varies – permanent installations, touring exhibitions, premium activations, placemaking – but the challenge is constant: a story that needs to be told in a space that has to perform.

We call this Story Engineering. It’s what closes the gap between what a creative team imagines and what an audience actually experiences. The brief defines our scope. The experience defines our responsibility.

Enabling Big Ideas.

## ROLE

Commercial Management at The Story Engineers is how big ideas stay commercially sound. The Commercial Manager brings the discipline of a quantity surveyor to a business that designs, engineers and installs experience technology, and applies it to the questions every project asks: what will this cost, what are we owed, and what is the best deal we can honestly strike with the people we buy from.

While the Project Manager has ultimate responsibility for project profitability, the Commercial Manager sits alongside them, providing well considered commercial advice, negotiating supply chain agreements, validating payment applications, identifying potential claims and compiling documentation to  justify them.

The role suits someone who wants to apply real commercial acumen to a creative production environment, applying innovative commercial skills to help projects reach their potential, whilst always ensuring The Story Engineers are  protected.  It is a new role, its core is clear, and its edges, including how far it reaches into such diverse topics as overseas supply chains  and subcontractor agreements, are shaped by the person who takes it on.

Within the first six to twelve months success will look like payment applications the Project Managers trust, claims and variations spotted early and argued well, supplier terms negotiated rather than accepted, and an estimating tool in use on live work, with the Commercial Manager setting what it needs to do and how the business uses it. Alongside all this sits a clear, agreed way of working between the Commercial Manager and the Project Managers across the commercial aspects of our projects.

## RESPONSIBILITIES

#### **Projects and Clients**

- **Payment applications.** Owns the payment application process across all projects, working with Project Managers and others to agree what to apply for and when.
- **Claims and variations.** Evaluates claim opportunities with Project Managers, structures the case and negotiates with the end client, working closely with the Project Manager.
- **Client-side counterpart.** Acts as the counterpart to the client’s quantity surveyor on placemaking and construction-led contracts, with the commercial fluency to hold the conversation as an equal.
- **Commercial forecasts.** Owns the claim positions and commercial forecasts, working alongside Finance.

#### ** 
Suppliers and Subcontractors**

- **Supplier negotiation.** Owns pricing, terms and retrospective discounts with suppliers, using competition where it serves the project and weighing price against reliability and availability because a project that doesn’t complete on time is not an option and a saving that fails on site is not a saving.
- **Procurement approach.** Builds and maintains how The Story Engineers buys and how supplier performance is judged. Works alongside Business Support on day-to-day ordering.
- **Overseas supply chains.** Develops relationships with local suppliers in the territories where The Story Engineers works, and the processes that keep those supply chains commercially sound.
- **Subcontract agreements.** Authorises subcontract agreements, making sure every appointment of a subcontractor or bespoke solutions provider carries an appropriate scope, programme and contract.

#### ** 
Estimating and Bids**

- **Estimating.** Leads the estimating capability: what The Story Engineers needs from it and how the business uses it, bringing industry best practice and working with colleagues across the business. The capability draws on historic project pricing, project data and current supplier pricing, so that cost certainty grows as a design and a sale develop. Produces and justifies allowances where engineering detail is necessarily limited.
- **Value engineering.** Drives value engineering jointly with engineering, finding savings that protect quality and reliability, including product substitution drawn from supplier deals.
- **Bids.** Owns the commercial content of bid pricing and tender returns, working alongside Business Development.

#### ** 
WHAT YOU’LL BRING**

- **Commercial judgement.** You read a variation, a supplier quote or an estimate and see what is really at stake in it. You decide what is worth pursuing, say why, and care about how the business makes its money, not only how it measures it.
- **Conviction in the room.** You form a view and argue it with Project Managers, engineers, suppliers and the client’s quantity surveyor alike, always for the sake of the outcome and never for sport, and you change your mind when someone shows you a better answer.
- **Standards that serve the work.** Your numbers are right, your records are complete, and you say plainly when something isn’t good enough yet. You hold the standard because a wrong figure costs a project, not because the standard exists.
- **Hands-on commercial craft.** You have compiled valuations and payment applications yourself and handled variations and claims on projects where the numbers had real consequences. You work independently, know what good looks like, and are ready to widen your remit into estimating, suppliers and value engineering.
- You have typically gained three to six years experience in quantity surveying or commercial management in a project environment.
- **Negotiation with judgement.** You negotiate price and terms well. You know when giving a little margin buys a stronger relationship, and when to hold the line.
- **Estimating practice.** You have worked with estimating and cost-planning models and know what makes one useful: what it should do, what data feeds it, and how people will really use it. You lead that conversation with colleagues, and you stay with it until it is in use.
- **Commercial points, made simple.** You think about what the engineer, creative producer or Project Manager across the table needs to hear, plan the difficult commercial conversation before you have it, and make the numbers usable by people who don’t think in them. You give the honest answer even when it isn’t the one they hoped for.
- **Generosity with what you know.** You pass on commercial know-how so Project Managers and engineers get sharper at it, and you make sure the team gets the credit for a recovered claim or a saving.
- **Tools and technology.** You are digitally fluent, quick to pick up new platforms, and curious about how emerging technology, including AI, can improve the way you work.
- **Welcome, but not required.** A degree in quantity surveying, commercial management or a related subject. Experience in live events, museums or exhibitions. The sector is quick to learn; the commercial judgement is what we hire for.

We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.
The Role
We're looking for a highly technical Product Manager to own how developers discover, build on and grow with Telnyx.
Telnyx operates a global infrastructure platform spanning communications, AI inference, GPUs, edge compute, databases and real-time applications. We've invested heavily in building the underlying infrastructure. Now we want to make it dramatically easier for developers to understand what's possible, build useful applications and get into production.
This is a hands-on product role leading a small team of six engineers across Developer Relations and Product-Led Growth. We aren't looking for a traditional DevRel leader or someone whose primary skill is managing people. We want a strong engineer with excellent product judgment who understands developer experience, builds things personally and knows how to turn developer adoption into revenue. 
The Team
You'll lead a team of six: three DevRel engineers (sample apps, open source, technical content and demos) and three PLG engineers (activation, AI agents and automation, self-service conversion and expansion). You'll report to the Chief Operating Officer. 
What you'll own
Build applications developers actually want to use — Lead the DevRel team in building production-quality sample applications, integrations, templates and reference implementations on Telnyx. Publish them on GitHub, maintain them and make them easy for developers to deploy and extend. Turn those applications into compelling technical content, live demos and developer distribution.
Drive product-led growth — Own the PLG operation responsible for moving developers from signup to meaningful usage and revenue. Use product telemetry, behavioral signals, AI agents and human intervention to identify friction, accelerate onboarding, improve conversion and expand self-service usage.
Make the developer experience better — Get hands-on with our APIs, SDKs, documentation and infrastructure. Work directly with product engineering to identify and resolve the issues that make products difficult to use. Our reference applications should continuously test whether our products are genuinely ready for developers.
Build AI-native growth systems — Work with Growth Engineering and RevOps to develop automated workflows for developer acquisition, onboarding, account intelligence, technical assistance and expansion. We believe small teams of excellent technical people supervising powerful automation can outperform much larger traditional GTM organizations.
Connect the entire developer journey — Applications attract developers. Developers experiment with the platform. PLG helps them succeed. Production usage generates revenue. The feedback from that process improves our products and informs what we build next. You'll be accountable for making that system work. .
What we're looking for
A strong software engineering background. You should be comfortable building and debugging real applications, working with APIs, reading code and understanding complex infrastructure.
Experience as a Technical Product Manager, founding engineer, technical founder or similar role with substantial personal responsibility for shipping software.
Exceptional product judgment, particularly around developer tools, APIs, documentation, onboarding and usability.
Familiarity with AI infrastructure, LLMs, inference, cloud platforms, real-time systems or developer infrastructure.
Understanding of product-led growth, including developer acquisition, activation, conversion, retention and monetization.
Ability to work with AI coding agents, automation frameworks, product analytics and modern developer tooling.
Strong technical communication skills. You can explain complicated technologies clearly and recognize what makes a useful demonstration or reference application.
Comfortable leading a small technical team while remaining deeply involved in the actual work.

Job Description Summary: 

We are seeking an accomplished leader to serve as Senior Director, Global Logistics Network Optimization & Digitization within Global Logistics Services and Global Procurement. This role leads enterprise capabilities that improve how logistics networks are designed, sourced, optimized, digitized, and governed across a complex global supply chain.

The Senior Director will lead a high-performing team responsible for network optimization, transportation sourcing digitization, data and analytics strategy, market intelligence, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate combines strategic vision, quantitative problem-solving, technology fluency, stakeholder influence, and people leadership to deliver measurable business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Strategy and Leadership
• Define and execute the strategic roadmap for logistics optimization, digitization, analytics, and capability development across global and regional stakeholders.
• Translate business objectives into scalable transformation initiatives, governance models, investment priorities, and measurable value-delivery plans.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to procurement, supply chain, logistics, technology, and business leaders on network, sourcing, and digital capability decisions.

Network Optimization
• Lead transportation and logistics network modeling to improve flows, facility footprints, service models, inventory positioning, modal strategies, and network design.
• Evaluate tradeoffs among cost, service, capacity, resilience, sustainability, and operational feasibility to shape practical recommendations.
• Develop business cases, implementation roadmaps, and repeatable methodologies that convert analytical insights into measurable results.

Digitization and Technology
• Define and advance the digitization strategy for transportation sourcing, rate management, scenario analysis, supplier assessment, reporting, and workflow processes.
• Identify opportunities to streamline manual activities through technology, automation, artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and process redesign.
• Champion adoption of scalable, user-centered tools through effective stakeholder engagement, governance, change management, and alignment with enterprise technology standards.

Data, Analytics, and Market Intelligence
• Develop logistics data, analytics, and market intelligence capabilities that improve visibility, data quality, sourcing strategy, supplier insights, and business decision-making.
• Build dashboards, executive reporting, analytical products, and decision-support tools that translate complex data into clear business recommendations.

Sourcing Capability and Value Delivery

• Apply network, supplier, market, demand, and cost intelligence to improve sourcing decisions while respecting category ownership and decision rights.
• Build and maintain a pipeline of optimization, sourcing, digitization, productivity, risk mitigation, and value-realization opportunities.

Stakeholder and Change Leadership
• Partner effectively with procurement, supply chain, transportation, finance, technology, data, suppliers, and operating unit leaders in a global matrixed environment.
• Define project scope, governance, decision frameworks, deliverables, and stakeholder expectations while navigating ambiguity and evolving business needs.
• Communicate complex analytical findings in concise, executive-ready language and build alignment through credibility, collaboration, and practical problem-solving.

People Leadership
• Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of logistics, optimization, sourcing, analytics, and digitization professionals.
• Establish clear priorities, accountability, development plans, succession readiness, and a culture of curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning.
• Manage relationships with external consultants, technology providers, analytics partners, and solution vendors as needed.

Success Measures
• Deliver measurable logistics value through optimization, sourcing, analytics, digitization, productivity, and risk-reduction initiatives.
• Improve logistics network performance while balancing cost, service, resilience, sustainability, and operational feasibility.
• Increase adoption and effectiveness of digital tools, analytical capabilities, decision-support solutions, and reusable enterprise frameworks.
• Strengthen data quality, market intelligence, sourcing effectiveness, stakeholder confidence, team capability, and succession readiness.

• Strong understanding of transportation networks, logistics operations, sourcing strategies, supply chain tradeoffs, and quantitative decision support.

job_description:
Project Director Time Out Market London
London
Reporting to the COO, Time Out Market
Fixed-Term Contract until mid-2028
Time Out Market London will be the global flagship for Time Out Market. This role is the central point of coordination for the project, bringing internal teams, consultants, contractors, the landlord and vendors together into one integrated plan.
The Project Director will be responsible for delivering the Time Out Market London project from start to finish, leading the project management and organisation of every phase: from brief and design, through planning, licensing, construction and fit-out, to opening and handover to the operating team.
The Project Director will report to the COO, Time Out Market, who holds overall accountability for the project, including budget. They will work alongside the TOM leadership team, the internal development team, the London General Manager, Time Out Media and the Finance and Legal teams.
The role also carries responsibility for keeping the Group CEO, the Markets Board and other key internal stakeholders engaged and informed throughout the project, so that decisions on design, space utilisation, business modelling, curation and pre-opening plans are taken with the right people, at the right time and with the right information.
The role is London-based and will require regular time on site.
Key Responsibilities
End-to-End Project Delivery
Lead the delivery of Time Out Market London from initial brief and design through to planning, licensing, construction, fit-out, opening and handover.
Develop and manage the integrated project plan, overseeing milestones, critical paths, dependencies and deadlines to ensure delivery on time and to the agreed quality standards.
Design & Build Coordination
Coordinate the appointment and work of architects, designers, cost consultants and contractors in line with the project plan.
Oversee planning, building control and landlord consents, working closely with the internal Development team and external advisers to ensure design and construction remain on programme and meet Time Out brand standards.
Licensing & Consents
Own the licensing workstream, managing milestones, dependencies and documentation, and acting as the day-to-day point of contact for licensing lawyers, acoustic, security and other specialist consultants.
Coordinate internal teams and external advisers to ensure all drawings, operating plans, reports and supporting documentation are delivered on time, managing submissions and responses to representations while keeping the COO and Legal informed of progress, risks and potential impacts.
Budget & Cost Tracking
Monitor the capital budget, cost reporting and change control, identifying and escalating potential variances and risks to the COO.
Coordinate consultant and contractor tenders with internal and external stakeholders, preparing monthly reports on spend against budget and forecast costs to completion.
Operational Readiness
Lead the operational readiness programme until the London General Manager is appointed, then support them in delivering the pre-opening plan.
Coordinate vendor onboarding and fit-out, recruitment, training, equipment and furniture delivery, supplier contracts, systems and IT, trial trading and launch activities, ensuring the Market is ready to open.
Snagging & Handover
Coordinate commissioning, snagging and the formal handover of the completed project to the operating team.
Support the Market through its first months of trading, ensuring outstanding works and issues are resolved within agreed timescales.
Governance & Reporting
Lead weekly project meetings, maintain live risk, issue and decision logs, and coordinate health and safety and CDM compliance with the principal contractor and relevant advisers.
Provide clear progress reports and decision-ready updates to the COO, leadership team, Markets Board and Group leadership, capturing lessons learned to inform future Time Out Market developments.
Internal Stakeholder Engagement
Maintain regular engagement with the COO, Group CEO, Markets Board and key internal stakeholders, establishing clear updates, reviews and decision-making points throughout the project.
Ensure stakeholders are involved in key decisions covering design and brand standards, space utilisation, business modelling, vendor and bar curation, and pre-opening plans, ensuring decisions are recorded and reflected in the project programme, budget and design.
External Stakeholder Management
Act as the day-to-day point of contact for the landlord, contractors, consultants, licensing lawyers, acoustic and security advisers, local authorities and vendors throughout the project.
Work collaboratively with internal teams across Operations, Commercial, Design & Projects, Finance, Legal, Time Out Media and the London General Manager to ensure effective coordination and delivery.
Performance Measures
Project milestones delivered in line with the agreed programme.
Market opened on the agreed date.
Premises licence and all required consents secured on schedule.
Accurate cost reporting and delivery within the approved budget.
Key project decisions made at agreed stage gates, with appropriate senior stakeholder involvement.

Build the multi-agent systems that automate work banks currently do by hand. You'll own the orchestration, the auditability, and the evals that make our agents trustworthy.

## Welcome

Thanks for taking the time to consider Tuza.

When joining a company at the early stages of its growth story, there's often more than meets the eye. This is our opportunity to help you understand why your next role should be with us.

We're based in Shoreditch, spend three days a week in the office, and can sponsor visas for the right candidate.

Diversity is a priority for us. We build a better product when the people building it don't all think the same way.

If you're still unsure at the end, drop into our offices in Shoreditch and see it for yourself.

## What we do

We build AI agents for banks, taking on the manual work that stops them from growing.

Every business that comes to a bank for a financial product gets passed from team to team, sales to onboarding to activation, and so on. Right now, every one of those teams is only ever as fast as the number of people in it. Our agents do that work without the ceiling. To be trusted with it in a bank, they have to be accurate, quick, and accountable, with auditability, explainability and security built in rather than an afterthought. That's what makes banks the hardest place to attempt this, and the place where getting it right is worth the most.

## Where we're at

We've raised $7 million from Northzone, Connect Ventures and TriplePoint, and work with acquiring banks including Worldpay, Barclaycard and NatWest.

We're earlier than that list makes us sound. The problem is real, and banks are already paying us to solve it. We're still experimenting with the product that best surfaces our value, and that's a large part of this job, rather than something that will be handed to you finished.

Doing that work is a small but driven team of 12 based in our Shoreditch office who care about their work and its impact.

There's also something you might already know us for. We built the UK's first payments price comparison platform, helping small businesses compare providers. It still runs today on MoneySuperMarket, Uswitch and money.co.uk. You won't be working on it, but it's why we know this market so well.

## How we work

- Extreme ownership: you own the outcome of your work, not just the output. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom and the responsibility to fix it.
- Learning velocity: curious, adaptable, and quick to pick things up. Hard problems require grit, and we embrace them.
- Customer-centric: we spend a day a week inside our partner banks, watching problems happen before they're even reported. Product decisions get made in that room, not in a roadmap meeting.
- Open and direct: we communicate openly, directly, and with intent.

## What you'll do

- Develop and optimise AI agents for live banking workflows
- Design review gates, fail-safes, and fallback behaviour
- Build the observability and feedback loops behind agent performance
- Spend time with our partner banks in their offices, and turn what you see there into product changes

## What we look for

We're hiring mid- to senior-level individual contributors with at least 4 years' experience.

- Exceptional Python and experience orchestrating LLMs with tools like Temporal or LangChain
- AI automation shipped and running in production
- A record of making agents reliable and efficient
- Fluency with data pipelines and integrations

We're an early-stage and intentionally lean. That means:

- We judge impact by the outcome of work, not the output
- Priorities shift when we learn something new, and we try to communicate why, but it happens
- You'll be given a direction, and the plan is yours to work out

This suits people who are comfortable with ambiguity, ask early when context is missing, and would rather ship something good enough fast than perfect something late.

It's less suited for those who prefer clear hierarchies, detailed briefs, or predictable roadmaps. That's not a character flaw; we just don't offer that yet.

Probation is a mutual check-in. We give feedback as we go, and we expect the same in return. If the fit isn't there, we'd rather know at month two than month six.

## How you'll be assessed

Our aim is to get candidates through the whole process within two weeks of applying — quick enough to respect your time, thorough enough to keep our standards high.

Click Apply Now to email us your CV, LinkedIn or GitHub

02

20-minute intro call to talk through your background, what you're looking for, and how we work

03

40-minute technical interview digging into products you've built and the decisions behind them

04

3-hour technical assessment, ideally at our Shoreditch office but remote works too

05

30-minute conversation with our CEO, Ed, to close things out and answer anything still on your mind

## What's in it for you

- A competitive salary and generous equity
- Three days a week in our Shoreditch office, Tuesday to Thursday, and the rest wherever you work best
- 25 days holiday, with flexibility when you need it
- £350 a year towards taking a proper break
- £350 a year towards learning or a hobby
- Smart, kind colleagues who care about the work
- Soundbaths, terrarium making, saunas, cooked breakfasts, barbecues on the rooftop and the occasional Mario Kart tournament

Build category and supplier strategies that balance cost, quality, lead time and resilience across countries and programmes.
Establish the US supply chain: qualify suppliers, put sourcing and logistics arrangements in place, and build material plans aligned with programme and production milestones.

Connect demand, bills of materials, supplier lead times and production schedules through a practical sales and operations planning rhythm, supported by shared enterprise resource planning standards and reliable data.
Define the global team structure, hire and develop people, and establish clear responsibilities and ways of working with site supply-chain leads.
Use agreed baselines and targets to improve supplier delivery, material availability, lead times, inventory performance and landed cost.

WHY VALLORII EXISTS

Infrastructure is the backbone of societies, markets, and the energy transition.

Read more

How infrastructure is valued is central to its affordability and sustainability. Get the valuation wrong, and capital is misallocated, bills rise, and the energy transition stalls. Vallorii is fixing this from first principles.

Every energy, transport, and water system needs funding to continue operating and improve the services it provides. The right funding, from the right investors, at the right price generates fair returns to funders while keeping services affordable for the communities that depend on them. Without the right funding, capital misallocation has consequences that ripple for decades.

Legacy infrastructure valuation and regulation rely on fragile Excel spreadsheets, siloed data, and single-case sensitivities - an approach unfit for assets with >30-year lifespans and multi-billion-pound stakes. The models used by investors, regulators, and operators today are not fit for a world defined by energy transition, climate risk, and the need for unprecedented capital mobilisation.

Vallorii is fixing this. An Oxford-based venture applying advanced modelling, contemporary economic and financial theory, and AI to price the full spectrum of risks that drive infrastructure value - with full transparency, full traceability, and outputs ready for investment committees and regulatory filings.

The mission: create the global platform for infrastructure valuation and risk pricing, to channel global capital toward sustainable, inclusive infrastructure.

THE COMPANY

What Vallorii has built.

Read more

Vallorii's cloud platform connects live market, regulatory, and risk data with the latest econometric and AI modelling techniques. We build stochastic cash-flow models with clear, transparent pathways; simulate thousands of risk-weighted scenarios; and explain every output with full source lineage. No black box. No single-point estimates. Statistically sound downside and upside ranges, ready for the real world.

Research-led DNA. The team are infrastructure specialists combining an Oxford, Cambridge and LSE academic heritage with econometric arsenals including multi-factor asset-pricing and Bayesian filtering, leveraging modern AI tools.

Genuinely independent. No stake in assets. No advisory conflicts. Pure data-driven analytics. The kind of independence that gives investors, regulators, and operators a number they can trust.

One year in. Early deployments live. Growing client base. Clear thesis. Now scaling - and building the team to do it.

THE PLATFORM

Three products. One intergrated platform.

Read more

Within the Vallorii platform, three products provide a novel perspective on infrastructure accounting, cost of capital, and valuations. Each is modular, AI-enabled, and built for the rigour of investment committees, regulatory filings, and public market monitoring.

1 Asset Intelligence

Bottom-up accounting for physical assets - granular data, correct accounting value, asset health and social demand.

2 VAPRI

The Vallorii Price of Risk: risk-adjusted hurdle rates from asset risks → IRR uncertainty → cost of equity. True pricing of capital.

3 Cost of Capital Lab

Real-time analytics for public utility stocks, bonds and funds. The go-to platform for regulatory and market-based CoC.

Asset Intelligence estimates accounting values for infrastructure assets based on service quality, cost, and demand - using AI data collection, Bayesian inference, and stochastic forecasting. VAPRI translates asset risks through IRR uncertainty to portfolio-level cost of equity, delivering risk-adjusted hurdle rates that are comparable and auditable. Cost of Capital Lab provides real-time analytics on publicly traded utility stocks, bonds, and funds - the go-to source of truth for price control decisions and baseline cost of equity.

job_title: Senior Product Manager, AI Platform, vector8, London
job_description:
Our mission at vector8 is to elevate organizations by unlocking the true value of AI, getting the best from Human-Machine collaboration. We have a culture grounded in inclusivity, curiosity, ownership, and collaboration, where your ideas shape the future of AI consulting.

We believe that over the next decade, every business will become an AI business and that a new era of AI transformation will enable greater leaps than ever before. We see a world where the seamless integration of human expertise and advanced AI technologies sparks unparalleled growth, efficiency, and resilience across all sectors.

vector8 collaborates with ambitious enterprises to address these challenges by adopting a unique strategy that merges the strengths of a product vision and custom development expertise. We deliver tailor-made, fine-tuned optimized, and compliant AI solutions swiftly and affordably, leveraging AI Accelerators that tackle common industry problems and can be adapted and combined to build and deploy targeted use cases in production.

Alongside our consulting and delivery work, we are building our own AI Platform: an open-core platform that gives regulated enterprises one place to build, govern, evaluate, optimise and run their AI. It brings together a catalogue of reusable agents, workflows, tools and models; intelligent model routing that sends each request to the right model at the right cost; and a secure environment where teams build production apps on top of that catalogue. It is designed for environments where compliance and data sovereignty are not optional. 

As we take our AI Platform from early deployments to a product that enterprises buy, run and rely on, we are hiring our first dedicated Product Manager to join the AI Platform product and engineering team, where you will also act as its Product Owner.
 
You will help shape the product strategy and roadmap and, as Product Owner, own the backlog that turns them into clear, valuable increments that the engineering team can ship every sprint. Working side by side with the product lead, the engineering team and our client-facing consultants, you will be the voice of the user inside the team.
 
We are looking for someone who is equally comfortable in a discovery session with a Chief Risk Officer, a backlog refinement with engineers, and a demo to a client steering committee. A solid foundation of relevant experience matters, but beyond that baseline we value your judgement, curiosity and ownership more than years in the field.
 * At least 6 years in a Product Owner or Product Manager role on a B2B software product, ideally a technical or platform product (developer tools, data, cloud or AI platforms).
 * A track record of owning a backlog end to end and shipping, in short cycles, with a cross-functional engineering team.
 * Strong working knowledge of modern AI: LLMs, RAG, agents and agentic workflows, evaluation, and the cost and quality trade-offs between models. Hands-on coding is not required, but you can read an API spec, follow an architecture discussion and challenge an estimate.
 * Solid command of Agile practices (Scrum, Kanban) and tooling such as Jira and Confluence, with the judgement to adapt process to the team rather than the reverse.
 * Experience running user discovery and turning qualitative and quantitative insight into prioritised requirements.
 * Excellent written communication: your user stories, release notes and product documentation are clear enough that nobody needs to ask what you meant.
 * Confidence with senior business and technical stakeholders, and the ability to say no with good reasons.
 * Genuine empathy for customers and proven experience building trusted relationships with them: you understand their constraints and pressures, and they want you in the room when decisions are made.
 * Experience working in international, cross-cultural environments, with distributed teams and clients across   several countries, and the ability to adapt your communication style to each.
 * Experience with AI governance, model risk management or MLOps / LLMOps products (observability, evaluation, guardrails, model gateways or routers).
 * Exposure to banking, insurance or other regulated industries, and familiarity with the EU AI Act and GDPR.
 * Experience with an open-core or open-source product: community feedback loops, licensing boundaries, enterprise upsell.
 * Involvement in pricing and packaging decisions for a usage-based or tiered SaaS product.
 * A consulting, agency or systems integrator background, giving you empathy for how our delivery teams deploy the platform at clients.
 * A recognised Product Owner certification (e.g. CSPO, PSPO).
 * Fluency in English and ideally French.

 * Own and prioritise the AI Platform product backlog, keeping it ordered by value, risk and dependencies, and honest about what is and is not ready.
 * Contribute to the product vision and roadmap, and translate them into epics, user stories and acceptance      criteria that engineers can estimate and build without guesswork.
 * Run discovery with clients, prospects and internal consultants: interview users, map workflows, and turn real problems (governance, evaluation, cost control, app building) into product requirements.
 * As Product Owner, lead sprint ceremonies: refinement, planning, reviews and demos; accept or reject delivered work against clear definitions of done.
 * Make and explain trade-offs between new features, platform robustness, security and technical debt, together with the tech lead.
 * Define and track product metrics (adoption, active apps and agents, routing savings, time to first value) and use them, alongside qualitative feedback, to steer priorities.
 * Ensure compliance, security and auditability requirements for regulated clients (e.g. GDPR, EU AI Act) are built into the backlog, not bolted on.
 * Prepare releases with engineering, consulting and go-to-market colleagues: release notes, documentation, demos and enablement material.
 * Feed field insight into pricing, packaging and positioning work, including the open-core boundary between community and enterprise features.
 * Support pre-sales and client engagements with product demos, solution walkthroughs and feasibility input.

 * The chance to shape a product from its early stage: your decisions will define what the platform becomes and how enterprises use it.
 * Direct access to real users: our consultants put the platform in front of leading European companies.
 * Hands-on work with frontier AI technology (agents, model routing, evaluation, vibe coding for production) applied to real business problems.
 * A small, senior, entrepreneurial product team where ideas move fast and ownership is expected.
 * A collaborative culture built on our values: bold with change, excellent client focus, authentic always, collaborate to succeed, human first.

What is it all about?
The Director, Europe Sales Planning will lead the regional capability responsible for strengthening sales planning and commercial execution across all European Business Units and Clusters, as part of the Sales and Commercial Operations function in Europe. This is a senior, business-facing leadership role at the centre of Europe’s sales operating model. The Director will lead a team and work across Sales Performance Management and Business Intelligence (SPM/BI), Sales Process, Sales Enablement, Global Sales & Commercial Operations, Finance, Legal and regional business teams. The role will champion a data-first, AI-native sales mindset, using insight, technology and emerging AI capabilities to improve commercial decision-making and sales execution.

Europe is establishing a dedicated Sales Planning capability to bring greater consistency, commercial focus and execution discipline across its sales organisation. The successful candidate will help Sales Leaders understand whether the pipeline is sufficient to deliver targets, align the organisation around priority deals and interventions, and embed effective account-planning and coverage practices across the region.

What we expect of you, day by day:

Pipeline Management and Commercial Execution:
• Lead and embed a consistent pipeline-management discipline across Europe, working through existing Cluster and Business Unit pipeline calls and leadership forums.
• Assess whether the pipeline is sufficient to deliver agreed targets, considering its size, health, stage, maturity, conversion, timing and concentration.
• Challenge assumptions, identify material risks and opportunities, and work with Sales Leaders to agree the actions required to improve delivery.
• Align with Sales Leaders on the priority deals to sign and ensure Sales, Legal, Finance and other supporting teams are focused on the opportunities that matter most.
• Track agreed recovery and acceleration actions, maintaining focus and accountability through pipeline calls and Monthly Business Reviews.
• Identify recurring barriers to pipeline progression and collaborate with the relevant teams to resolve them and improve commercial execution.
• Provide pipeline context and commercial judgement to support forecasting, target delivery and senior leadership discussions.

Pipeline Insight and Commercial Decision Support:
• Partner with SPM/BI to shape the business questions, priorities and additional analysis required from pipeline reporting and insight.
• Use pipeline data and insight to focus leadership attention on the most important risks, opportunities, deals and interventions.
• Champion the effective use of data, automation and AI-enabled insight to improve pipeline visibility, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and enable faster, more informed commercial decisions.
• Bring field experience and Sales Leader feedback to recommend improvements to pipeline measures, thresholds and analytical approaches.
• Jointly develop clear commercial narratives, leadership commentary and recommended actions for Business Reviews and other senior forums.

Account Planning and Client Coverage:
• Lead the regional implementation of Global account-planning frameworks and establish a consistent cadence across Europe.
• Drive the quality and commercial value of account plans through clear expectations, targeted reviews and constructive challenge with Sales Leaders.
• Ensure account planning connects client priorities, stakeholder mapping, opportunity development and pipeline actions.
• Partner with Sales Enablement to ensure Account Executives have the training, tools and adoption support required to apply the framework effectively.
• Promote consistent client stakeholder mapping and stronger visibility of key client relationships and opportunities.

Segmentation, Coverage and Sales Operating Model:
• Partner with SPM/BI on segmentation, coverage and sales operating-model work, bringing commercial context to the analytical frameworks and modelling.
• Embed resulting recommendations across Clusters and Business Units, testing them against market realities and supporting effective implementation.
• Challenge the effectiveness and efficiency of account coverage, seller deployment and portfolio design to improve commercial focus and productivity.
• Gather feedback from the business and recommend refinements where evidence or implementation experience indicates the model should evolve.
• Support consistent use of sales taxonomy and planning standards in alignment with Global guidance.

Target Setting and Business Reviews:
• Support SPM/BI-led target-setting processes by providing pipeline, market and commercial context and helping Clusters and Business Units understand and apply the methodology.
• Recommend target adjustments or alternative allocations where credible pipeline and market evidence supports a different outcome.
• Provide commercial and pipeline input into Monthly Business Reviews and other performance forums, including risks, opportunities, priority deals and recommended actions.
• Ensure agreed actions are translated into clear ownership and followed through with the relevant Sales Leaders and supporting teams.

Leadership and Stakeholder Management:
• Lead, coach and develop the Europe Sales Planning team, setting clear priorities and creating a high-performing, collaborative culture.
• Act as a trusted commercial partner to Europe, Cluster and Business Unit Sales Leaders, combining constructive challenge with practical support.
• Build strong partnerships across SPM/BI, Sales Process, Sales Enablement, Global Sales & Commercial Operations, Finance, Legal and other relevant functions.
• Balance regional consistency with the differing commercial realities of Business Units, Clusters and markets.
• Represent the Europe Sales Planning perspective in relevant regional and global forums.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo's Procurement and Vendor Enablement Office (PVEO) is the engine behind our rapid scaling. We are a diverse, collaborative group with a mission to efficiently procure the critical infrastructure and technology required to scale the Waymo Driver. In this role, the IT Category Manager supports the business by leading strategic sourcing and category management for our Software (SaaS/On-Prem), End-User Hardware, and IT Professional Services. You will partner deeply with Waymo’s IT, Security, and Engineering teams to manage complex renewals, drive cost efficiency, and ensure our technology stack scales with our growth.

• Category Strategy: Develop and execute a comprehensive procurement strategy for Corporate IT, including SaaS, Hardware, and Telecom, balancing cost optimization with speed-to-market.

• Hardware & VAR Management: Optimization of Value-Added Reseller (VAR) relationships for end-user compute and peripherals, ensuring competitive pricing and seamless fulfillment logistics for a growing workforce.

• Stakeholder Partnership: Act as the trusted advisor to the CIO, IT Ops, and Security leadership; lead "make vs. buy" analyses and influence technical requirements to drive commercial value.

• 7+ years of strategic procurement experience, with at least 4+ years dedicated to IT, Software, or Technology sourcing.

• Deep expertise in SaaS licensing models (consumption-based, per-seat, enterprise agreements) and experience negotiating with Tier 1 software publishers.

• Proven ability to draft and negotiate complex commercial contracts, including MSAs, EULAs, DPAs, and Professional Services SOWs.

• Ability to operate in a high-velocity environment, managing multiple concurrent high-priority renewals and sourcing events.

The Business Analyst role focuses on analysing, redesigning, and enabling operational processes to support intelligent automation, AI-assisted workflows, and straight-through processing, while ensuring strong governance, risk control, and human accountability. The role uses generative AI to accelerate analysis and documentation, and builds wireframes and prototypes so stakeholders can test solutions before build begins. 
This is a hands-on analysis and change role operating at the intersection of Operations, Technology, and the AI Centre of Excellence (COE). The role supports the transition from manual, fragmented processes to scalable, standardised, automation-ready operating models. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
Utilise skills and experience in the areas of structured problem solving, business analysis, data analytics, design thinking, and lean process improvement to support performance excellence in the organisation. 
Elicit business requirements from stakeholders, based on project goals and objectives, supported by factual cost benefit analysis producing intelligent and strategic Business Cases for Executive level consideration. 
Collaborate inside project structures, as well as work independently, and engage directly with senior stakeholders to drive outcomes, including the facilitation of business interviews and workshops using proven techniques. 
Analyse and map end-to-end operational processes to identify automation and AI opportunities using structured prioritisation
criteria, and provide solution options and benefit analysis. 
Redesign processes to be automation-ready, clearly separating deterministic steps, AI-enabled interpretation, and human judgement points. 
Apply AI tools (e.g. M365 Copilot and generative AI assistants) to accelerate requirements capture, process analysis, documentation, test design and data analysis, validating outputs for accuracy, bias and confidentiality before use. 
Design and build wireframes, mock-ups and interactive prototypes (low to high fidelity) using tools such as Figma, Balsamiq or AI-assisted prototyping tools, to elicit, visualise and validate requirements with stakeholders and development teams before build. 
Identify, assess and document AI use cases, defining business requirements, data inputs, acceptance criteria, evaluation measures and human-in-the-loop controls, in partnership with the AI Centre of Excellence and in line with AI governance and risk standards. 
Ensure complete and holistic requirement coverage, creating detailed business, functional, non-functional and operating model requirements that are fit for purpose, and supporting the design, build, test and business readiness/training activities. 
Manage and coordinate multiple phases of one or more small-to-moderate projects, from business case to transition to BAU, tracking progress against schedule, managing stakeholder involvement, and proactively identifying and mitigating risks. 
Support Rapid Deployment Pods (RDPs) through discovery, rapid prototyping, testing, and implementation, iterating solutions quickly with stakeholder feedback. 
Act as a digital, data and AI change champion within Operations, promoting the responsible use of AI, building AI literacy and leading training, digital adoption and competency building across the practice. 

REQUIREMENTS 

Significant Business Analyst experience, ideally within the funds industry (preferred) or broader financial services industry, in highly regulated environments, with expertise in business analysis methodologies and emerging technologies. 
Proven track record in the delivery of digital, automation, or operational transformation initiatives. 
Excellent process mapping skills and worked on projects that have required process improvements, experienced in MS Visio. 
Working understanding of AI concepts and limitations (e.g. large language models, AI agents, hallucination risk), and of responsible AI, data privacy and governance expectations within regulated environments. 
Proven ability to create wireframes, mock-ups and clickable prototypes using tools such as Figma, Balsamiq, Miro, PowerPoint or AI-assisted prototyping tools, with a sound understanding of user-centred design and UX principles. 
Experience working with low-code / no-code automation and orchestration platforms (e.g. Power Automate, n8n). 
Proven ability to support quality assurance through test planning, creation and execution. 
Advanced data analytical skills and outstanding problem-solving capabilities, particularly with loosely defined structure and scope. 
Hands-on experience with M365 Copilot and generative AI tools, including effective prompt design, to support analysis, documentation and prototyping 
Deep knowledge of core business operations developed through executing projects in areas like strategy, operating model design, lean process improvement, and both waterfall and agile digital transformation and delivery. 
Demonstrable professional integrity, adherence to legal, regulatory and in-house policies, and dedication to the company’s high-quality standards and customer service focus. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate at both senior management and end user level. 
Education: 
Certified in Business Analysis, or equivalent 
Certified in Six Sigma , or equivalent

About Us

Craven Street Wealth is an award-winning Chartered financial planning and wealth management firm, helping individuals, families and businesses make confident financial decisions.

We combine expert advice with a personal approach, building long-term relationships that help our clients achieve their goals. With offices across London and the South of England, our teams work collaboratively to deliver outstanding service and tailored financial planning solutions.

As part of Quanta Group, we are backed by the strength of a wider financial services group that includes Wealthtime and Copia Capital. While each business operates independently, we share a commitment to delivering excellent client outcomes, supporting our people to grow and creating an environment where everyone can thrive.

We know that our success comes from our people. That is why we are committed to creating a supportive, collaborative culture where everyone can develop their skills, contribute ideas and build a rewarding career.

About the Role

To support the Group's inorganic growth strategy by identifying, assessing and progressing potential acquisition opportunities, with a particular focus on financial analysis, valuation modelling, transaction coordination and due diligence.

The individual will work closely with the Finance Director and senior leadership team to support acquisitions from initial screening through to completion and integration.

Key Responsibilities:

M&A Pipeline Management and Deal Sourcing

• Research and identify potential acquisition targets, primarily within the wealth management and financial advice sector.

• Maintain and manage the M&A pipeline, including tracking opportunities, deal stages and next steps.

• Liaise with brokers, intermediaries and potential acquisition targets.

• Undertake initial assessments of opportunities against agreed acquisition criteria.

Financial Analysis and Valuation

• Review financial information provided by potential acquisition targets.

• Analyse key metrics including AUA, revenue, recurring income, EBITDA, profitability, adviser productivity and client concentration.

• Prepare and maintain financial models, including valuations, adjusted EBITDA calculations and potential synergies.

• Assess different transaction structures, including upfront and deferred consideration.

• Identify key financial and commercial risks.

Transaction Execution and Due Diligence

• Coordinate the M&A process from initial screening through to completion.

• Prepare information requests and track outstanding information.

• Support financial, commercial, operational and regulatory due diligence.

• Liaise with internal teams and external advisers, including legal, tax and corporate finance.

• Maintain transaction trackers, action logs and deal timetables.

• Assist with the preparation and review of Heads of Terms and other transaction documentation.

Investment Papers and Management Reporting

• Prepare acquisition screening reports and investment scorecards.

• Draft investment papers and approval memorandums for senior management, the Board and shareholders.

• Prepare financial analysis and presentations to support investment decisions.

• Maintain accurate reporting on pipeline progress, potential valuations and expected completion dates.

 Post-Acquisition Integration Support

• Support the financial and operational integration of acquired businesses.

• Assist in tracking acquisition synergies, cost savings and financial performance against investment assumptions.

• Work with Finance and Operations to ensure appropriate handover following completion.

This isn't an exhaustive list and responsibilities may evolve over time to meet the needs of the business.

About You

Specialist Skills, Qualifications and Experience:

Essential:

• Approximately 3–5 years of experience in M&A, corporate finance, transaction services, investment banking or corporate development.

• Strong financial analysis and Excel modelling skills.

• Good understanding of financial statements, valuation methodologies and EBITDA adjustments.

• Experience reviewing financial information and preparing commercial analysis.

• Strong organisational and project management skills.

• Excellent written communication skills, including preparing management reports and presentations.

• Ability to manage multiple workstreams independently and work to tight deadlines.

• Strong attention to detail and a proactive, hands-on approach.

Desirable:

• Experience within wealth management, financial planning or the wider financial services sector.

• Understanding of IFA acquisition models, recurring revenue and AUA-based valuations.

• Experience supporting transactions through due diligence and completion.

• ACA, ACCA, CFA or equivalent qualification (qualified or part-qualified).

Skills and Knowledge:

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills.

• Good organisational and time-management skills.

• Ability to manage competing priorities effectively.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

• A proactive and solution-focused approach.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

• Comfortable using Microsoft Office and other relevant business systems.

We recognise that great candidates come from a variety of backgrounds and experiences. If you're excited by the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

Rewards & Benefits

At Craven Street Wealth, we believe in supporting our people both professionally and personally. In return for your contribution, you'll have access to a range of benefits including: 

• Competitive salary.

• Hybrid working, with time split between home and office.

• Discretionary annual bonus.

• 34 days holiday per calendar year, including bank holidays, with the option to purchase up to five additional days per year.

• Supported and encouraged professional development.

• Contributory pension scheme

• Medical cashback plan, helping cover the cost of everyday healthcare expenses such as dental treatment, eye care and physiotherapy.

• Occupational sick pay scheme.

• Group income protection scheme.

• Life assurance scheme

• Cycle to Work scheme.

• Up to 10 hours of volunteering leave each year.

• Opportunities for internal progression within Craven Street Wealth and across the wider Quanta Group.

• A collaborative and supportive culture where colleagues are encouraged to grow, contribute and succeed.

Craven Street Wealth is an equal opportunities employer and we're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and able to be themselves.

We recognise that people work in different ways and bring different experiences, perspectives and ideas. We believe these differences make us stronger and help us deliver better outcomes for our clients and colleagues.

We welcome applications from everyone, regardless of background, beliefs, culture, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability or long-term health condition.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know and we'll do our best to support you.

job_description:
About Wolt
At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.
We are looking for a Strategy & Operations Manager to join our EMEA Growth & Engagement team, which owns the growth and engagement of Wolt+ and Deliveroo Plus across 40+ markets in Europe and the Middle East and is working to build the best local commerce membership programs in the markets we operate in.
You will join our Engagement pod, which focuses on understanding what turns a subscriber into a healthy, engaged and long-term member. You will be responsible for i) identifying and prioritising the largest opportunities to improve our member experience and subscription health, ii) understanding how customer needs and behaviours evolve across different stages of the Plus lifecycle, and iii) driving the highest-priority opportunities from strategy through experimentation and execution to tangible business results.
To get the job done, you’ll work closely with our wider subscription team and cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, Data Science & Analytics, Marketing, Commercial and Finance, while taking full ownership of driving your initiatives to fruition and, most importantly, measurable results.
Our team is responsible for driving the growth and long-term health of our subscription programs. Your exact problem space may evolve as our priorities change, but in practice you will:

Build a clear view of the largest opportunities to improve member engagement and subscription health across EMEA. Use customer behaviour, market performance and economics to size opportunities and prioritise the areas most likely to materially move our business results.
Understand the member lifecycle end to end, identifying where customers struggle to onboard, build habit, discover value or remain engaged, and translate those insights into practical interventions that improve customer and business outcomes.
Own initiatives from initial problem definition through to execution and results, working closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science & Analytics, Marketing, Commercial and Finance.
Build and run an experimentation roadmap against the highest-priority opportunities. Translate business problems into clear hypotheses, design A/B tests or other appropriate experiments, analyse the results and make decisions on whether initiatives should be scaled, iterated or stopped.
Track and own the key performance indicators relevant to your problem space and, where necessary, drive corrective actions. This may mean pulling shorter-term lifecycle levers or shaping longer-term Product and Engineering solutions to address underlying drivers.
Collaborate closely with local and regional teams to ensure our strategies reflect customer needs and market context, and turn successful approaches into repeatable playbooks that can scale across Wolt+ and Deliveroo Plus.
Keep a close eye on our customer experience and identify opportunities to make Plus easier to understand, use and get value from throughout the membership lifecycle.
The Engagement pod works across a broad range of customer problems. Examples could include improving the first 30–60 days of membership, onboarding and early order progression, benefit discovery and adoption, lifecycle and CRM journeys, programs that drive incremental order frequency and activity, and initiatives that improve longer-term member engagement and retention.
Our humble expectations
5+ years of relevant experience, preferably in i) strategy & operations, consumer growth or engagement at a leading consumer technology / platform company, ii) subscriptions, loyalty or membership businesses, or iii) management consulting with subsequent operating experience.
Problem-solving and prioritisation skills: our team is in the business of solving hard problems and developing new solutions. There is rarely a ready-made playbook to follow, so you’ll need to be comfortable structuring ambiguous problems, getting into the details and identifying which opportunities are most likely to move the needle.
Analytical and experimentation skills: you’ll work with data every day and need to be comfortable identifying and sizing opportunities, designing and interpreting A/B tests and making decisions based on the results. Strong spreadsheet skills are a must-have and SQL experience is useful.
Customer and lifecycle judgement: you are able to understand how customer behaviour and needs evolve across the membership journey, identify the moments that matter most and translate those insights into practical ways to improve onboarding, engagement and retention.
Business ownership and independence: you have experience owning measurable business results and can demonstrate how you have taken a problem from initial analysis through to execution and impact. You’ll be given significant responsibility and freedom, so you need to be comfortable operating without a predefined roadmap.
People and project management skills: you’ll need to be able to inspire and persuade colleagues from a broad spectrum of backgrounds and seniority levels and get cross-functional teams working towards one goal in a coordinated and efficient way.
AI fluency: AI is increasingly part of how we work at Wolt day to day. You should already be comfortable using AI tools in your work, or be excited to quickly become so, and continuously look for ways to use them to work faster and solve problems better.
Business acumen and eye for superb user experience: you’ll need to be able to see the forest for the trees and have good intuition about what works best for customers while understanding the economics and trade-offs behind business decisions.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.
Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

Our first focus is to develop and scale technology that measures and mitigates methane emissions in the livestock industry. Today, 1.3 billion people rely on the industry for their livelihoods and food security. However, it is the single biggest human-driven source of methane emissions globally, emitting more than both the oil & gas industry and the coal industry.

The deployment of our technologies on a global scale has the potential to drive half the global methane reduction needed by 2030, and to transform the beef and dairy industries.

ZELP was an inaugural winner of the Terra Carta Design Lab, and has received funding and support from the European Commission, Innovate UK, The Global Methane Hub and the Gates Foundation.

Zenrows is the web data infrastructure for AI. Founded in 2021, we give developers, AI agents and businesses one reliable way to access, extract and structure data from any website, at any scale, however hard the site tries to block them.

 

Whether it’s an agent that needs fresh web context mid-task, an LLM application grounded in live data, or an enterprise pipeline pulling millions of pages a day, Zenrows handles the rendering, the anti-bot defences and the parsing behind a single API, 10B+ requests a month. Teams at more than 10,000 companies, including Microsoft, Amazon, Dell, IBM, Slack, eBay, EY, Nokia and Clay, rely on Zenrows to turn the web into a reliable source of data for their products, workflows and AI-driven applications, across e-commerce, finance, real estate and AI.

As we continue our expansion, we are now looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join us on a permanent basis and make an instant impact, working directly with the CEO and CTO. 

The Role

AI runs on web data, and more and more of the work that needs it is done by AI agents. Zenrows is how they get it. Fetch gets any page past the toughest anti-bot systems. Extract turns it into clean, structured data. Batch and Crawl do it across whole websites.

We’re also changing how software gets built. Our engineers already write 100% of their code with agents. We are moving more and more operational workflows from manual, to automated, to autonomous, trusting agents with real work in production. Very few teams are doing this for real. We are, and we want you to help lead it.

What You’ll Do

• You’ll own a customer-facing product end to end: what it does, how it runs, and the business number it moves. There are no product managers here. You talk to customers, decide what to build, build it with your agents, ship it, and own it.

• The problems are real. Our systems run on thousands of CPU cores, handle millions of requests a day, and stay ahead of anti-bot systems built by companies many times our size. You’ll design systems that hold up under that load. You’ll also build the tests, evals and guardrails that tell us when an agent’s work can be trusted.

At Zest Plan we’ve built a strong community of 40,000 customers over 20 years, and a database of former customers many times that size. 3 big priorities:
1. Direct marketing to existing and former customers: win back lapsed customers and grow renewals and upsell through targeted direct mail, email and lifecycle communications.
2. Insight and measurement: own customer segmentation, the test programme and our customer insights database, and supply the data, lists and learning behind our outbound sales campaigns.
3. Digital acquisition: own the plan and the targets for paid search and other online channels, delivered by our digital marketing specialist.
What you will own
· Direct marketing to former and existing customers including win-back + referral programmes and renewal campaigns

• Win-back: reactivation rate by recency band and cost per reactivated customer, measured against a control group.

• Digital acquisition: cost per acquisition and return on ad spend on paid search, against targets set by customer lifetime value.

• Proven experience in direct marketing to a customer database, ideally in service plan, subscription, insurance or other recurring-revenue consumer brands.

• Experience of supporting outbound telephone campaigns with data, lists and warm-up communications.

• Experience of managing retention, renewal or upsell programmes in consumer brands.
• Experience of setting targets for, and managing, digital marketing agencies, freelancers or specialists.
• Confident with data and analytics, and a clear understanding of UK GDPR and PECR as they apply to marketing, including email, SMS, phone and TPS rules.
• Good copywriting or copy-editing judgement.
• Experience of leading sales or service teams you don’t line-manage, through plans and evidence, and of managing external partners and specialists.

• Zest apparel drops
